details.body: MACADAMIZE: prastaraKaRqEH CAdayati (c. of Cad) or saMhanti (han, c. 2.).
MACARON: *cUrRanAlI, m. soup: cUrRanAlImiSraM yUzam.
MACAROON: *bAdAmapizwakaH.
MACAROON , s. bAdAmnirmmito mizwapizwakaviSezaH.
Macaw, s. vakratuMqaH, SukaH, kIraH.
MACAW: vakratuRqaH: v. Parrot.
MACAW , MACAO, s. SukaH, kIraH, vakracaYcuH m., vakratuRqaH.

Mace, s. jAtipatrI, jAti-tI f., jAti(tI)-koSaM, jAtiPalaM-koSaM. 2 gadA; daMqaH, yazwi m. f.; vetraM, laguqaH, musa(za)laH-laM, mudgaraH; ‘m(ace)-bearer’ daMqa-yazwi-DaraH, vetraDaraH, gadA-hastaH pARiH, yazwigrahaH, vetrapARiH, daMqaBft.
MACE: I A spice: jAti(tI)patrI, Bha. Powdered with m. cardamom, and cinnamon: trijAtakAva- cUrRitaH (tA, taM), D. vi.II A heavy staff: gadA, Mah.III In gen.: daRqaH: v. Staff.

MACE , s. (Club, ensign of authority) vetraM, gadA, yazwiH m. f., yazwikaH, daRqaH -RqaM, muzalaH, musalaH, laguqaH, laguraH, mudgaraH, vAtardDiH m. — (The spice) jAtIkoSaM, jAtikoSaM, jAtIkozaM, jAtikozaM, jAtiH -tI f., jAtiPalaM, jAtIPalaM, PalaM, jAtIpatrI, jAtipatraM, jAtipuzpaM, guqatvacaM, rAjaBogyaM.
MACE-BEARER: (1) daRqaDaraH;(2) yazwiDaraH: and sim. comp.s.

MACE-BEARER , s. vetraDaraH, vetraDArI m. (n), vetrI m. (n), vetrapARiH m. gadADaraH, gadI m. (n), gadApARiH m., gadAhastaH, daRqaDaraH, daRqI m. (n), daRqahastaH laguqahastaH, daRqaDArI m., daRqikaH, daRqaBft m., yazwigrahaH, yAzwIkaH.
Macerate, v. t. jalena Aplu c., ArdrIkf, 8 U, saM-DA 3 U. [Macerat]ion, s. saMDAnaM, pAcanaM, AdrIkaraRaM.
MACERATE: perh. drAvayati (c. of dru): v. To steep.

To MACERATE , v. a. (Make lean, waste) kraSa (nom. kraSayati -yituM), kfSIkf, parikfSIkf, kzi in caus. (kzapayati -yituM), kzIRaM -RAM -RaM kf, kzIRIkf, glE in caus. (glapayati -yituM), mAMsakzayaM kf. — (Steep) jala- sekena or jalaplAvanena komalIkf, cirakAlaM jalena samAplu (c. 10. -plAva- yati -yituM) or jalasamAplutaM -tAM kf or jalasiktaM -ktAM kf or ArdrIkf; ‘macerate indigo,’ nIlasanDAnaM kf, nIlapAcanaM kf.
MACERATED , p. p. (Made lean) kfSIkftaH -tA -taM, parikfSaH -SA -SaM, kzIRaH -RA -RaM. — (Steeped) jalasekena komalIkftaH -tA -taM or mfdUkftaH -tA -taM.
MACERATION: perh. drAvaRam, pAcanam (??).

MACERATION , s. (Making thin, mortification) kfSIkaraRaM, kzIRakaraRaM, karSanaM, kleSakaraRaM, kleSadAnaM, mAMsakzayaH, mAMsaSozaRaM, SarIrapAkaH, SarI- raSozaH, kAyakleSaH, kleSaH, kAyakfcCraM. — (Steeping) jalasekena koma- lIkaraRaM, ArdrIkaraRaM; ‘of indigo,’ nIlasanDAnaM, nIlapAcanaM.
MACHIHE-MAKER, MACHINIST: yantrakAraH.

Machinate, v. t. maMtr 10 A, (upAyaM) ciMt 10, saMpra-Df 10, parikxp c., yuj 10. 2 druh 4 P, kapawaprabaMDaM rac 10, gUQamaMtraRAM kf 8 U. [Machinat]ion, s. kukalpanA, kumaMtraRA, kUwaprabaMDaH, gUQaprayogaH, kapawaprabaMDaH, drohaciMtanaM, kalpanA, ciMtanaM, yojanA, viDAnaM. [Machinat]or, s. kumaMtraRA-kft m., kapawaprabaMDaracakaH.
MACHINATE: parikalpayati (klwap, c. 10.): v. To contrive.

To MACHINATE , v. a. parikxp (c. 10. -kalpayati -yituM), upAyaM kxp or Gaw (c. 1. Gawate -wituM) or viDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM) or anusanDA or saMviDA, mantr (c. 10. mantrayati -yituM), sampraDf (c. 10. -DArayati -yituM), kalpanAM kf, parikalpanAM kf, anusanDAnaM kf. — (Plot) druh (c. 4. druhyati, drogDuM), kapawaprabanDaM kf, kapawaprabanDena drohaM kf.
MACHINATION: (1) kumantraRA;(2) zaq yantram (?).

MACHINATION , s. kalpanA, parikalpanA -naM, kxptiH f., mantraRA, kukalpanA, kumantraRA, kuyuktiH f., kuprayuktiH f., kusfzwiH f., kusaNkalpaH, kapawaprayogaH, kapawaprabanDaH, GawanaM -nA, kuGawanA, viDAnaM, saMviDAnaM, anusanDAnaM, duzwakAryyasADanArTam upAyacintanaM, drohacintanaM; ‘against the king,’ rAjadrohaH, rAjaSarIrABidrohaH.
MACHINATOR , s. parikalpakaH, parikalpanAkft m., kumantraRAkft, kukalpa- nAkArI m. (n), GawakaH, upAyacintakaH, drohacintakaH.

Machine, s. yaMtraM, sADanaM, upakaraRaM. Machinery, s. yaMtrARi, yaMtrasAmagrI, yaMtra-samudAyaH. Machinist, s. yaMtrakAraH-vid, yaMtrakalAjYaH. Mechanic, s. Silpin m., SilpakAraH, karmakAraH, kAruH, SilpopajIvi-n m. [Mechanic]al, a. yaMtraM in comp., yaMtrasaMbaMDin, yaMtravizaya, yaMtra-Silpa-vidyAsaMbaMDin, yAMtrika (kA f.). 2 SilpavidyAkfta, yaMtraSAstrAnurUpa; ‘m(echanical) art’ SilpaM, kalA. 3 yaMtratulya, yaMtravat, apraboDayukta. 4 yaMtravidyA-SilpavidyA-nipuRa; SilpakArin. [Mechanic]ally, adv. yaMtra-vidyAnurUpaM, SilpaSAstrAnusAreRa. 2 yaMtravat, abudDipUrvaM, amati-apraboDa-pUrvaM. [Mechanic]ian, s. SilpaSAstrajYaH, yaMtravidyAkuSalaH. Mechanics, s. yaMtra-Silpa-vidyA-SAstraM, yaMtragatiSAstraM. Mechanism, s. yaMtraracanA, kalA, yukti f.; yaMtragati f., yaMtravyApAraH. Mechanist, s. yaMtrakAraH.
MACHINE: yantram: v. Also tool.
MACHINE , s. yantraM, upakaraRaM, vilAlaH, sADanaM, sADanayantraM.
MACHINERY: I Machines collectively: yantrARi (n. pl.).II Working parts of a machine: expr. by circumlo.: ‘m. of state’: rAjakAryavahAH (m. pl (?).
MACHINERY , (Collective mechanism) yantrasAhityaM, yantraSaktisAhityaM, yAntraM, yAntrikaM, yantratvaM. — (Machines in general) yantrasAmagryaM, yantrasamUhaH, yantrasamudAyaH, yAntraM, yantravidyA.
MACHINIST , s. yantrakAraH -rakaH, yantrakft m., yantranirmmARaSilpajYaH, yantravidyAnipuRaH, yantravid, kalAjYaH.
MACILENCY , s. kfSatA, kArSyaM, kfSANgatA, kzIRatA, kzAmatA, mAMsakzIRatA,
MACILENT , a. kfSaH -SA -SaM, kzIRaH -RA -RaM, kzIRamAMsaH -sA -saM.
MACKEREL: *makralaH, nIlabinduH, matsyaviSezaH.
Macrocosm, s. viSvaM, triBuvanaM, aKilaM ja-gat.
MACROCOSM: (1) viSvam;(2) viSvasaMsAraH and sim. comp.s.
MACROCOSM , s. jagatsarvvaM, jagatkftsnaM, viSvajagat n., viSvaM, triBuvanaM.
Macrology, s. ativistAraH, dIrGasUtratA.
MACROLOGY , s. dIrGasUtratA, ativistIrRavAkyaM, ativistaraH.
MACTATION , s. upahArArTaM GAtanaM or nihananaM or pramApaRaM, viSasanaM.
Macula, s. kalaMkaH, aMkaH, lAMCanaM, lakzman n. Maculate, v. t. kalaMkayati-malinayati (D.). [Maculat]ed, a. kalaMkita, kaluzita, lAMCita.
MACULA , s. kalaNkaH, lAYCanaM, cihnaM, vinduH m., kaluzaM, aNkaH.
To MACULATE , v. a. kalaNka (nom. kalaNkayati -yituM), malina (nom. malinayati -yituM), kaluza (nom. kaluzayati -yituM), cihna (nom. cihna- yati -yituM), lAYC (c. 1. lAYCati -YCituM).
MACULATE , MACULATED, a. kalaNkitaH -tA -taM, kalaNkI -NkinI -Nki (n), kaluzitaH -tA -taM, lAYCitaH -tA -taM, cihnitaH -tA -taM.

Mad, a. unmatta, vAtula, sonmAda, hata-nazwa-Brazwa-budDi, hatajYAna, BrAMta-vikzipta-citta; ‘make m(ad)’ unmAdaM nI 1 P, unmad c.; ‘to go m(ad)’ unmad 4 P. 2 (Of acts) bAliSa, unmAda-yukta, asamIkzyakfta, sAhasika (kI f.); ‘m(ad)-brain, -brained’ vikziptabudDi &c.; ‘m(ad)-cap’ sAhasikaH; ‘m(ad) with anger’ saMrabDa, kopAkula, madodagra; ‘m(ad)-house’ vAtulAlayaH; ‘a m(ad) dog’ alarkaH; ‘a m(ad) man’ vAtulaH, unmattaH. [Mad]den, v. t. unmad c., vAtulIkf 8 U, vyAmuh c., unmattIkf; ‘m(adden)ed with rage’ kroDAMDa; ‘m(adden)ed with liquor’ surApAnamatta [Madden]ing, a. unmAdaka, unmAdajanana (nI f.). [Mad]ly, adv. u-nmattavat, unmAdAta, sonmAdaM, vAtulavat, cittaviBrameRa, BrAMtacetasA. 2 sAhasikatayA. [Mad]ness, s. unmAdaH, unmattatA, vastulatA, mati-dudDi-BramaH, cittaviplavaH-vikzepaH, mati-budDi-BraMSaH. 2 (Fig.) vyAmohaH, mUQatA, sAhasaM.

MAD: I Of persons or mind:(1) unmattaH (ttA, ttaM) (best equiv (lit. and fig.) (we are) both m. about it: dvAvapyatronmattO,V ii.; o, m. woman: ayi, unmattike, K. ii.; to go or run m.; unmAdaM gacCati; to drive m.: unmattatAM nayati, K. ;(2) vAtulaH (lA, laM), vAyugrastaH (stA, staM), etc. (lit.) my son is m.: mama putro vAyugrastaH, D. ii.;(3) unmAdin (f. nI), N. xiii. 40.;(4) madodDataH (tA, taM) (fig.), Ki. xiv. 63.II Of acts, etc.(1) by comp.;(2) duzwaH (zwA, zwaM) (= vicious);(3) uddAmaH (mA, maM) (= unres- -trained).

MAD , a. unmattaH -ttA -ttaM, unmAdaH -dA -daM, unmAdavAn -vatI -vat (t), unmAdI -dinI -di (n), sonmAdaH -dA -daM, unmadaH -dA -daM, unmadizRuH -zRuH -zRu, mattaH -ttA -ttaM, vAtulaH -lA -laM, vAtUlaH -lA -laM, pramadaH -dA -daM, sUnmadaH -dA -daM, sUnmAdaH -dA -daM, hatabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, nazwabudDiH &c., vikziptabudDiH &c., BrazwabudDiH &c., budDiBrazwaH -zwA -zwaM, hatajYAnaH -nA -naM, viplutacittaH -ttA -ttaM, BrAntacittaH -ttA -ttaM, vikziptamatiH -tiH -ti, vikziptaH -ptA -ptaM, mUQacetAH -tAH -taH (s), nazwendriyaH -yA -yaM. — (Proceeding from madness) unmAdaprayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, unmAdasUcakaH -kA -kaM, budDi- BraMSamUcakaH -kA -kaM. — (Furious) madotkawaH -wA -waM, madodagraH -grA -graM, kopAkulaH -lA -laM, saMrabDaH -bDA -bDaM; ‘a mad dog,’ alarkaH, alakaH; ‘a mad fellow,’ pramadajanaH; ‘to go mad,’ unmad (c. 4. -mAdyati -madituM), unmattIBU; ‘drive mad,’ unmad (c. 10. -mAdayati -yituM).
MAD-BRAIN , MAD-BRAINED, a. vikziptabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, viplutabudDiH &c.
MAD-CAP , s. pramadajanaH, unmattajanaH, sAhasikaH, sAhasakarmmA m. (n).
Madam, s. AryA, BAvinI, kulajA; (in addressing) Arye, Bavati.
MADAM, -E: (1) devI: v. Lady;(2) AryA (by gentlemen).
MADAM , s. AryyA, AryyikA, AryyakA, BavatI, BAvinI. — (As a complimentary title) Aryye voc. c., Bavati voc. c.
MADCAP: pramattaH (ttA, ttaM): v. Rash, mad.
MADDEN (v. t.): (1) unmAdayati (c. of mad), m. ed by your form: tvadAkAronmAditaH (tA, taM), D. ;(2) unmattIkaroti.
MADDEN (v. i.): (1) unmAdyati (mad, c. 4.); (2) unmattIBavati. M. ed:(1) unmattaH (ttA, ttaM), m. ed with wine: madonmattaH;(2) anDaH (nDA, nDaM): v. Blind.
To MADDEN , v. a. unmad (c. 10. -mAdayati -yituM), mad, unmattIkf, mattIkf.
To MADDEN , v. n. unmad (c. 4. -mAdyati -madituM), unmattIBU, mattIBU, mad.
MADDENED , p. p. unmAditaH -tA -taM, unmattIkftaH -tA -taM, saMrabDaH -bDA -bDaM.
MADDENING , a. unmAdakaH -kA -kaM, unmAdajanakaH -kA -kaM, unmAdana -nA -naM.
Madder, s. maMjizWA, vikasA-zA, jiMgI, samaMgA, kAlameSi(zi)kA, maMqUkaparRI, maMqi-(qI)rI, BaMqI, yojanavallI.
MADDER: maYjizWA, dyed with m.: mAYjizWa (f. zWI), ka (f. kA), Vi.
MADDER , s. (The plant) maYjizWA, vikasA, vikazA, maRqUkaparRI, tAmra- vallI, yojanavallI, yojanaparRI, BaRqIrI, BaRqirI, BaRqI, jiNGI, samaNgA, kAlamezikA, citrANgI, kAlamakzikA.

MADE , p. p. kftaH -tA -taM, nirmmitaH -tA -taM, kalpitaH -tA -taM, prakalpitaH -tA -taM, racitaH -tA -taM, viracitaH -tA -taM, GawitaH -tA -taM, vihitaH -tA -taM; ‘made of,’ mayaH -yI -yaM, nirmmitaH -tA -taM, GawitaH -tA -taM in comp.; as, ‘made of wood,’ kAzWamayaH -yI -yaM, kAzWaGawitaH -tA -taM, kAzWanirmmitaH -tA -taM; ‘made known,’ niveditaH -tA -taM, AveditaH -tA -taM, sUcitaH -tA -taM, AKyAtaH -tA -taM, jYApitaH -tA -taM, vijYApitaH -tA -taM; ‘made ready,’ sajjIkftaH -tA -taM; ‘made favorable,’ prasAdIkftaH -tA -taM; ‘made up, as the mind,’ sTirIkftaH -tA -taM, sTiraH -rA -raM; ‘made up, reconciled,’ sanDitaH -tA -taM, SAntavivAdaH -dA -daM; ‘made up, settled,’ sidDaH -dDA -dDaM, sADitaH -tA -taM, nizpannaH -nnA -nnaM; ‘made over,’ saNkrAmitaH -tA -taM, saYcAritaH -tA -taM, pratipAditaH -tA -taM; ‘made light of,’ laGUkftaH -tA -taM; ‘made good,’ sADitaH -tA -taM; ‘made to do any thing,’ expressed by the caus. pass. part.; as, ‘made to pay,’ dApitaH -tA -taM; ‘made to go,’ gamitaH -tA -taM; ‘made to know,’ jYApitaH -tA -taM; ‘one who has made an agree- ment,’ kftasaNketaH -tA -taM.

MADE OF: (1) -mayaH (yI, yaM), m. of human bone: manuzyAsTimayaH (yI, yaM), S. p.;(2) nirmitaH, vi- (tA, taM), a monkey m. of gold: kapiH kanakanirmitaH, Shat.;(3) GawitaH (tA, taM), m. of fine thread: sUkzmatantuGawitaH (tA, taM), V. d.;(4) by a deriv., m. of mustard: sArzapaH (pI, paM), Bha.
MADEFACTION , s. ArdrIkaraRaM, kledanaM, saMkledanaM, samundanaM, klinnIkaraRaM.
Madefy, v. t. klid c., ArdrIkf 8 U.
To MADEFY , v. a. ArdrIkf, klid (c. 10. kledayati -yituM), saMklid, pariklid.
MADHOUSE: (1) vAtulASramaH;(2) unmattAlayaH (?).
MADHOUSE , s. unmattAlayaH, unmattapAlanagfhaM, unmattasTAnaM.
MADLY: I In madness: unmAdAt, K. ii.II Like a mad man: unmattavat; unmatta (f. ttA) iva.
MADLY , adv. unmattavat, sonmAdaM, mattavat, vAtulavat, cittaviBramAt, ci- ttaviplavAt, unmAdena, prAmAdyAt, pramadajanavat.
MADMAN , s. unmattajanaH, mattajanaH, pranadajanaH, unmAdakaH, vAtulaH.

MADNESS: I Lit.:(1) unmAdaH, m. is a mental disease: unmAdo mAnaso vyADiH, Sr.; treatment of m.: unmAdacikitsA, Bha.;(2) unmattatA (the state);(3) vAtulatA etc. (= 2).II Fig.:(1) unmAdaH;(2) vAyuH, possessed of the m. of alchemy: saYjAtaDAtuvAdavAyu (mfn.), K.III Of acts, etc.: mohaH: v. Folly, infatuation.

MADNESS , s. unmattatA, unmAdaH, sonmAdatA, mattatA, vAtulatA, vikziptatA, budDivikziptatA, budDivikzepaH, budDiBramaH, matiBramaH, cittaviBramaH, cittaviplavaH, budDinASaH, budDiBraMSaH, matiBraMSaH, madaH, pramadatA, prAmAdyaM, unmAdavAyuH m.
MADRIGAL: no equiv.: gopagItam.
MAENORRHAGIA , s. (A disease) yonyarSas n., pradaraH, pradarAmayaH.
Magazine, s. nAnAvizayasaMbadDaM pustakaM; ‘a m(agazine) of arms’ AyuDAgAraM, SastrAstrAgAraM. 2 BAM-qAgAraM.
MAGAZINE: I For arms: SastrAgAram and sim. comp.s.II A store-house: q. v.III A periodical: no equiv.: *kozaH or jYAnakozaH; patrikA (used in Bengali.).

MAGAZINE , s. (Storehouse) BARqAgAraM, BARqagfhaM, kozAgAraM. — (Of arms, ammunition, &c.) yudDadravyAgAraM, SastrAgAraM, astrAgAraM, yudDaBA- RqAgAraM, AyuDAgAraM. — (A miscellany published periodically) kAle kAle prakASito nAnAvizayasaNgrahaH or nAnAvastuvizayako granTaH.
Maggot, s. kfmiH, kIwaH. [Maggot]y, a. kIwamaya (yI f.), kIwapUrRa.
MAGGOT: I A worm: q. v.: kIwaH, -kaH.II A whim: q. v.
MAGGOT , s. kIwaH, kfmiH m., aliH m., kIwARqajaM.
MAGGOTY: I Lit.: kIwopasfzwaH (zwA, zwaM) and sim. comp.s.II Whimsical: q. v.
MAGGOTY , s. kIwapUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, kfmipUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, kfmimayaH -yI -yaM.
MAGI: *mAgayaH (m. pl.); pArasikapUrvapaRqitAH.
MAGI , MAGIANS, s. pl. pUrvvadeSIyapaRqitAH m. pl., prAgdeSIyavidvajjanAH.
MAGIAN: *mAgIyaH (yA, yaM).

Magic, s. iMdrajAlaM, mAyA, aBicArAH, maMtrayogaH, vaSakiyA, kuhakA-kaM, maMtraH, kArmaRaM, kusfti f., mohaH, yogaH. [Magic]al, a. EMdrajAlika-ABicArika-mAyika-kOsftika- (kI f.), mAyAmaya (yI f.), mohin, mAyA in comp. [Magic]ally, adv. iMdrajAlena, mAyayA, aBicAreRa. [Magic]ian, s. EM(iM)drajAlikaH, mAyA-vin m., mAyAkAraH, mAyin m. aBicArin m. kuhakaH, kuhakAjIvin m. kOsftikaH, yogin m., yogeSvaraH, sidDaH; ‘m(agician)ʼs brush’ picCikA.
MAGIC (subs.): (1) indrajAlam;(2) mAyA;(3) kArmaRam (rare).
MAGIC, -AL (adj.): EndrajAlikaH (kI, kaM); (2) mAyA- in comp.

MAGIC , s. aBicAraH, aBicAravidyA, mAyA, mAyAvidyA, yogaH, samprayogaH, vaSakriyA, mUlakarmma n. (n), citrakarmma n., jAlaM, jAlakarmma n., indra- jAlaM, aBimantraRaM, kArmmaRaM, kArmmaRatvaM, piSAcavidyA, kuvidyA, mohaH, kuhakaH, kusftiH f., saMvadanaM -nA, mantraH, mantramohanaM.

MAGIC , MAGICAL, a. ABicArikaH -kI -kaM, aBicArikaH -kI -kaM, aBi- cArI -riRI -ri (n), mAyAmayaH -yI -yaM, mAyI -yinI -yi (n), mA- yAvI -vinI &c., mAyikaH -kI -kaM, EndrajAlikaH -kI -kaM, mohI -hinI &c., kOsftikaH -kI -kaM.
MAGICALLY: (1) mAyayA;(2) indrajAlena; etc.
MAGICALLY , adv. aBicAreRa, aBicAravidyAnusArAt, mAyayA, sendrajAlaM.
MAGICIAN: (1) EndajAlikaH, m.'s brush: picCikA, D.(2) mAyAkAraH, mAyin or mAyAvin (gen. applied to demons etc. assuming illusive forms).

MAGICIAN , s. aBicAravid m., aBicAravidyAjYaH, mAyAkAraH, mAyAkft m., mAyI m. (n), mAyikaH, mAyAvI m. (n), mAyAjIvI m. (n), piSA- cavidyAjYaH, aBicArI m. (n), citrakarmmavid m., mUlakarmmavid m., indrajAlikaH, EndrajAlikaH, indriyamohI m. (n), kuhakaH, kuhakakAraH, kuhakajIvI m., yogI m. (n), yogeSvaraH, samprayogI m., kOsftikaH, sidDaH, citrakarmmA m. (n).
MAGISTERIAL: I Lit.: expr. by comp.II Imperious, proud: udDataH (tA, taM).

MAGISTERIAL , a. (Pertaining to a magistrate or magistracy) DarmmADikArasambanDI -nDinI &c., DarmmADyakzasambanDI &c., daRqanItisambanDI &c., ADikArikaH -kI -kaM, vEnayikaH -kI -kaM. — (Pertaining to a master) praBusambanDI &c., svAmisambanDI &c., praButvaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, ADikArikaH -kI -kaM. — (Imperious) AjYApakaH -kA -kaM, AdeSakaH -kA -kaM, DfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, SAsanarUpaH -pA -paM.

MAGISTRACY: daRqanAyakatvam or daRqanAyakADikAraH (??).

(s.) in comp., ADikArika (kI f.). 2 praButva, viSizwa, AjYApaka, sAvalepa, dfpta, pragalBa. [Magisterial]ly, adv. SAsanarUpeRa; sadarpaM, sAvalepaM.
MAGISTRATE: perh. daRqanAyakaH, D.

MAGNANIMITY: (1) mAhAtmyam;(2) mahAnuBAvaH; etc.

Magnanimous, a. mahAtman, mahAmanas, mahAmanaska, mahAnuBAva, udAra-DI-cetas-mati, udAra, mahecCa, mahASaya, udArAtman. 2 (Of acts) avadAta, udAra, OdAryapUrva. [Magnanimous]ly, adv. OdAryeRa, mAhAtmyena, mahAnuBAvAt, u-dAracetasA. Magnanimity, s. mAhAtmyaM, udArAtmatA, mahAtmatA, OdAryaM, mahAnuBAvaH, cittOdAryaM, udAramatitA, mahecCA, mahASayaH.
MAGNANIMOUS: I Of men:(1) mahAtman (mfn.);(2) mahAnuBAvaH (vA, vaM);(3) mahAmanas (mfn.);(4) udAracetas (mfn.); etc.II Of acts: udAraH (rA, raM).

MAGNANIMOUSLY: (1) OdAryeRa;(2) udAracetasA, etc.
MAGNANIMOUSLY , adv. OdAryyeRa, udAravat, mAhAtmyena, samAhAtmyaM, manomahattvAt, manomahimnA, mahAnuBAvAt, udAracittatvAt, mahecCayA, SUravat, mahASayavat, udAracetasA.
Magnate, s. utkfzwapadasTaH, uccapadasTaH, DuraM-DaraH, DurIRaH.
MAGNATE , s. utkfzwapadasTaH, uccapadasTaH, mahAkulInaH, rAjanyaH.
MAGNESIA , s. amlapittanASakaM SuklacUrRaM or cUrRAkAraM mfttikABasma n. (n).

MAGNETIC, -AL: by comp., m. needle: ayaskAntaSalAkA (?).

MAGNETIC , MAGNETICAL, a. AkarzikaH -kA -kaM, AkarzakaH &c., Aka- rzaRaguRaH -RA -RaM, AkarzaRaDarmmakaH -kA -kaM, lohacumbanaSIlaH -lA -laM, lohacumbanaDarmmakaH -kA -kaM, lohacumbakasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), loha- cumbakavizayaH -yA -yaM; ‘magnetic attraction,’ AkarzaH.
MAGNETICALLY , adv. AkarzaRaSaktidvAreRa, AkarzaRapUrvvaM, lohacumbanaSaktyA.

MAGNETIZE: *cumbakaSaktimantaM (tIM,-t) karoti.

[Magnificent]ly, adv. atitejasA, mapratApaM, viBUtyA, ESvaryeRa. Magnificence, s. mahiman m., pratApaH, SrIH, SoBA, tejas n., atipratApa-SoBA-praBA, ojasvitA, mahApratApaH, viBUti f., OjjvalyaM, viBavaH, ESvaryaM.
MAGNIFICENT: (1) rocizRu (mfn.): v. Splen- -did;(2) tejasvin (f. nI); v. Fiery;(3) mahat (f. tI): v. Great;(4) SrImat (f. tI): v. Beautiful.

MAGNIFICENT , a. mahApratApaH -pA -paM, pratApavAn -vatI -vat (t), mahAtejAH -jAH -jaH (s), pratApI -pinI -pi (n), atipratApI &c., tejasvI -svinI &c., atitEjasaH -sI -saM, SoBanaH -nA -naM, atiSoBanaH -nA -naM, supraBaH -BA -BaM, atikAntimAn -matI &c., ojasvI -svinI &c., ujjvalaH -lA -laM, mahApraBaH -BA -BaM, dedIpyamAnaH -nA -naM, viBUtimAn -matI &c.
MAGNIFICENTLY: expr. by adj. in comp. or by circumlo., m. dressed: ujjvalavezaH (zA, zaM), Mr.

MAGNIFIED , p. p. aDikIkftaH -tA -taM, vipulIkftaH -tA -taM, varDitaH -tA -taM, upacitaH -tA -taM, viSAlIkftaH -tA -taM, karAlIkftaH -tA -taM, karAlitaH -tA -taM, atyuktipUrvvaM varRitaH -tA -taM, bahulIkftaH -tA -taM, kIrttitaH -tA -taM.
MAGNIFIER: *bfMhaRayantram.
MAGNIFIER , s. varDakaH, vfdDikarttA m. (rttf), varDanakft m., ADikyakft. — — (Optical instrument) vipuladarSakakAcaH.

Magnify, v. t. vfD c., upa-ci 5 U, sPAy c. (sPAvayati), aDikIkf 8 U; See Increass 2 atyaMtaM varR 10, ut-saM-kFt 10. 3 atiSa-yoktyA vfD c. or vistF c. [Magnifi]er, s. varDakaH. 2 bfMhaRayaMtraM. [Magnify]ing, a. varDin, bfMhaRakArin.
MAGNIFY: bfMhayati (bfMh, c. 10.) or by circumlo., it m. ies objects: *anena padArTA bfhato dfSyante: v. To enlarge, extol.

MAGNIFYING , part. or a. varDI -rDinI -rDi (n), varDakaH -kA -kaM, aDi- kakArI -riRI &c., vipulakArI &c., vipuladarSakaH -kA -kaM. — (Glass) vipuladarSakakAcaKaRqaH -RqaM.
MAGNILOQUENCE: udDatoktiH, udDataM vacaH, Ki.; etc.
MAGNILOQUENCE , s. atyuktiH f., atiSayoktiH f., atiBAzaRaM, pragalBaBAzaRaM, prOQaBAzaRaM, citroktiH f., garvvitavAkyaM, garvvoktiH f., SabdamAtraM.
Magniloquent, a. prOQa-pragalBa-vAc, dfpta-Dfzwa-vAc. Magniloquence, s. prOQa-BAzaRaM, pragalBokti f., garvoktiH.
MAGNILOQUENT: (1) udDataH (tA, taM);(2) pragalBa (f. lBA);(3) prOQa (f. QA).
MAGNILOQUENT , a. prOQaBAzI -ziRI -zi (n), pragalBaBAzI &c., citra- BAzI &c., garvvitavAkyakArI -riRI &c.

(n), mahimA m. (n), urutA -tvaM, vikawatA, vEkawyaM, vistIrRatA.

MAHOGANY , s. nandikaH, tunnaH, tuRiH m.

MAHRATTA , s. (Country) mahArAzwraM. — (Dialect) mahArAzwrI.

MAID , MAIDEN, s. kanyA, kumArI, taruRI, yuvatI, bAlikA, bAlA, kanyikA, kanyakA, kumArikA, gOrI, gOrikA, DIdA, rohiRI, nagnikA, kanI. Some of these words refer to particular ages; as, ‘a maid of eight,’ gOrI -rikA; ‘of nine,’ kanyA, rohiRI; ‘of ten,’ lagnikA, nagrikA; ‘of from ten to twelve,’ kumArI -rikA; ‘of from sixteen to thirty,’ taruRI; ‘of the age of pu- berty,’ maDyA, maDyamA, mugDA. — (Unmarried woman, virgin) anUQA, avivAhitA, apariRItA, nivarA, avarA, adattA, aprattA, akzatA, akzatayoniH f., avidDayoniH f., puruzAspfzwA. — (Female servant) dAsI -sikA, cewI, paricArikA, sahacAriRI, karmmakarI, sEranDrI, sErinDrI.
MAID-SERVANT: (1) cewI;(2) paRyadAsI, D. ; (3) dAsI: v. Slave.
MAID-SERVANT , s. dAsI -sikA, cewI, prezyA, karmmakarI, prezyavaDUH f., pratIhArI, paricArikA, sevakI.
MAIDEN (adj.): Lit.: expr. by comp. II New, pure: q. v.: aBinavaH (vA, vaM).

(Pertaining to a maid) kOmAraH -rI -raM, kumArikAsambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), kanyAsambanDI &c., kumArikAvizayaH -yA -yaM, kanyA- vizayaH -yA -yaM. — (Consisting of maids) kanyAmayaH -yI -yaM, kumA- [Page476-a+ 51] rImayaH -yI -yaM. — (Fresh, unused) navaH -vA -vaM, aBinavaH -vA -vaM, apUrvvaH -rvvA -rvvaM, akftopaBogaH -gA -gaM, ajAtopaBogaH -gA -gaM, akzataH -tA -taM, aKaRqaH -RqA -RqaM.
MAIDENHAIR: a plant: *sukeSI.
MAIDENHEAD , MAIDENHOOD, s. kOmAraM, kOmAryyaM, kumArItvaM, kanyAtvaM, taruRItvaM, tAruRyaM, kumArIBAvaH, kumArIdaSA, kumArikABAvaH. — (Fresh- ness) navatvaM -tA, akzatatvaM, aKaRqatA.
MAIDENLIKE , MAIDENLY, a. kumArIyogyaH -gyA -gyaM, kumArIsadfSaH -SI -SaM, kanyAyogyaH -gyA -gyaM, kumArikocitaH -tA -taM, kanyocitaH -tA -taM, kumArikAnurUpaH -pA -paM, kumArItulyaH -lyA -lyaM.
MAIDENLY: kanyakocitaH (tA, taM) and sim. comp.s: v. Becoming.

[Mail]ed, a. sakavaca, kavacin, kavaca-DArin; kftasannAha, varmita, sannadDa, sajja, daMSita, vyUQakaMkawa.

MAIL , s. (Armour) kavacaH -caM, sannAhaH, varmma n. (n), lohavarmma n., ayovarmma n., kaYcukaH, tanutraM, tanutrARaM, sajjA, yudDasajjA, daMSanaM, daMsanaM, uraSCadaH, kaNkawakaH, kaNkawaH, jAgaraH, jagaraH, kAyabalanaM, urastrARaM, vakzastrARaM, AyasI, vARavAraH, vAravARaH -RaM. — (Post) patravAhanaM, leKyavAhanaM, rAjaniyogiBftaH patrakozaH, rAjaDAvakaBfto leKyakozaH.
MAILED: (1) varmitaH (tA, taM);(2) daMSitaH (tA, taM), saM-, pari-;(3) sannadDa (f. dDA).

Maim, v. t. vikalI-vyaMgI-kf 8 U, hInAMgIkf, vikalayati (D.). s. aMgavEkalyaM, hInAM-gatA, nyUnAvayavatvaM. [Maim]ed, a. vikalAMga (gI f.), vyaMga, hInAMga, vikala, aMgavikala.

MAIM , s. aNgavEkalyaM, vEkalyaM, vikalIkaraRaM, vyaNgIkaraRaM, aNgaCedaH.

[Main]ly, adv. muKyaSaH, bahuSaH, praDAnataH, muKyAMSena, BUyizWaM, bahutaraM, sAmAnyataH, viSezeRa, prADA-nyena.

MAIN , a. (Principal) muKyaH -KyA -KyaM, pramuKaH -KA -KaM, praDAnaH -nA -naM, paramaH -mA -maM, paraH -rA -raM, agraH -grA -graM, agryaH -gryA -gryaM, SrezWaH -zWA -zWaM, uttamaH -mA -maM, pravaraH -rA -raM, viSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, mUlikaH -kI -kaM. — (Most important) gurutamaH -mA -maM, garizWaH -zWA -zWaM, paramaH -mA -maM; ‘main evil,’ praDAnadUzaRaM, gurudUzaRaM; ‘main matter,’ gurukAryyaM, gurukaM; ‘main entrance,’ siMhadvAraM; ‘main stock,’ mUladravyaM.

(n), pitfkriyA, pitfvrataM, pitfkAryyaM, SrAdDakarmma n., SrAdDakriyA, vitfyajYaH, pitfmeDaH; ‘oblation to the manes,’ SrAdDaM, piRqaH -RqI, kavyaM, various forms of these oblations are pArva- RaSrAdDaM, ekoddizwaSrAdDaM, nityaSrAdDaM, nEmittikaSrAdDaM, kAmyaSrAdDaM, Ahni- kaSrAdDaM, vfdDiSrAdDaM, sapiRqanaSrAdDaM, udakumBaSrAdDaM, nAndISrAdDaM, nAndImuKaM, prItiSrAdDaM, hiraRyaSrAdDaM, AmaSrAdDaM, pATeyaSrAdDaM, tilatarpaRaM; ‘the offering of a cake,’ piRqadAnaM, piRqanirvapaRaM; ‘of water,’ udakadAnaM, udakakriyA; ‘gifts in honour of the manes,’ pitfdAnaM -nakaM, pitftarpaRaM; ‘one who makes the oblation,’ piRqadaH, SrAdDadaH, SrAdDakaraH, SrAdDakft m.; ‘day sacred to the manes,’ pitftiTiH m. f., pitfdivasaH; ‘heaven of the manes,’ pitflokaH, pitfpadaM, pitfsTAnaM. Oblations to the manes are made by the relations of the deceased soon after his death, and are repeated once, or, according to some, twice in every year, i. e. on the anniversary of the death, and on the same lunar day of the waning half of the month Bhādra. The latter are called mahAlayaH. These obsequial rites are supposed to be necessary to secure the residence of the souls of the deceased in a world appropriated to the manes.

MANSION , s. harmyaM, BavanaM, mandiraM, DAma n. (n), sadanaM, sODaM, SAlA, sadma n. (n), gfhaM, gehaM, veSma n. (n), niveSanaM, niketanaM, AyatanaM, vAsasTAnaM, nivAsasTAnaM, AlayaH, nilayaH, nivasatiH f. — (Lunar mansion) nakzatraM, viDupriyA, candrapriyA, dakzajA, candradArAH pl. The last of these words is applied to the twenty-seven lunar man- sions collectively, as in mythology they are supposed to be so many nymphs, daughters of Daksha, and wedded to the moon. The following are the names of the twenty- seven nakshatras in order: 1. aSvinI, 2. BaraRI, 3. kfttikA, 4. rohiRI, 5. mfgaSiras n., 6. ArdrA, 7. punarvasuH m., 8. puzyaH -zyA, 9. ASlezA, 10. maGA, 11. pUrvvaPAlgunI, 12. uttaraPAlgunI, 13. hastaH, 14. citrA, 15. svAtiH -tI f., 16. viSAKA, 17. anurADA, 18. jyezWA, 19. mUlaH -laM, 20. pUrvvAzAQA, 21. uttarAzAQA, 22. SravaRaH -RA, 23. DanizWA, 24. SataBizA, 25. pUrvvaBAdrapadA, 26. uttaraBAdrapadA, 27. revatI. Some add a twenty-eighth, aBijit. Astrologers divide the twenty-seven lunar mansions into three classes of nine each, called devagaRaH, rAkzasagaRaH, manuzyagaRaH.

PAlgunacEtraM, pUrvacEtraH. 2 gamanaM, yAnaM, yAtrA, prasTAnaM, pragamanaM, prayARaM, aBiniryARaM; ‘at a distance which is some daysʼ m(arch)’ di-vasakramagamye'Dvani (Ka. 258) ‘going by hasty (forced) m(arch)es’ avicCinnakEH prayARakErvahan (Ka. 340); ‘difficult m(arch)’ durgasaMcaraH, saMkramaH; ‘m(arch)ing with an army against the enemy’ aBizeRanaM; ‘a m(arch)ing army’ pracakraM, calitaM; ‘a hostile m(arch)’ aBikramaH, AsAraH Marches, s. deSasImA-paryaMtaH.

MARCH (subs.): I The month: uttaraPAlguna- pUrvacEtrasaMvAdIyurUpIyavarzasya tftIyo mAsaH.II Journey: (1) yAtrA (also fig.), obstructor of the m. of the world: lokayAtrAviGAtakaH, Mah.;(2) yAnam, pra-, broke off m. ing. for three nights: trirAtraM prayARa- BaNgamakarot, P. ;(3) prasTAnam (= setting out on a m.), just ascertain a day proper for our m.: nirUpyatAM tAvadasmAkaM prasTAnayogyadivasaH, Mu. iv. II As measure of distance:(1) prayARam, -kam, followed a few m. es: katicitprayARakAnyanuvavrAja, C. v.;(2) aDvan (m (= way), after three m. es: aDvasu trizu, R. xi. 57.

MARCH (v.): yAti, pra-, aBi-, aBipra-, (yA, c. 2.), let the whole army m.: prayAtu vAhinI sarvA, A. r.; (2) vrajati, aBi-, (vraj, c. l.); should m. against an enemy, drawing up the forces in battle-array: balaM vyUhya dvizato'BimuKaM vrajet, Ka. xviii. 2.;(3) calati, saM-, ut (cal, c. 1.) (= to move), the great army m. ed: mahAcamUSca- cAla, Ki.;(4) pratizWate (sTA, c. l (= to start), m. ed by land: pratasTe sTalavartmanA, R. iv. 60.
MARCH (v.t.): (1) nayati (nI, c. l (= to lead: q. v.);(2) expr. by intrans.

MARCH , s. (The month) PAlgunaH -nikaH, cEtraH -trikaH, PAlgunottarArdDaM, cEtrapU- rvvArdDaM, pUrvvacEtraH, uttaraPAlgunaH, tapasyaH, maDuH m., tftIyamAsaH. — (Move- ment of soldiers, &c.) gamanaM, yAnaM, yAtrA, sEnikagamanaM, sEnikayAtrA, gamaH, gatiH f., sEnikagatiH f., vrajyA, saraRaM, saMsaraRaM. — (Marching onwards, progression) prayARaM, prasTAnaM, prasTitiH f., pragamanaM, [Page483-a+ 51] agragamanaM. — (Marching against) aBizeRanaM, aBiniryAnaM; ‘set- ting out on a march,’ yAtrAkaraRaM; ‘toilsome march,’ durgasaYcaraH, durgasaYcAraH, saYcAraH.

To MARCH , v. n. yAtrAM kf, gamanaM kf, sEnikavad gamanaM kf or pragam (c. 1. -gacCati -gantuM) or prayA (c. 2. -yAti -tuM) or prasTA (c. 1. -tizWati -te -sTAtuM) or vraj (c. 1. vrajati -jituM) or car (c. 1. carati -rituM) or cal (c. 1. calati -lituM) or pracal; ‘to march against,’ aBi- niryA (c. 2. -yAti -tuM), aBiprayA, prativraj, aBiprasTA, pratyABiprasTA, aBigam, pratigam; ‘one who marches slow,’ mandagAmI m. (n), manTaraH; ‘fast,’ atijavaH, jaMGAlaH, jaMGilaH.

To MARCH , v. a. aBizeRa (nom. aBizeRayati -yituM), senAM prasTA in caus. (-sTApayati -yituM) or cal (c. 10. calayati -yituM) or pratigam (c. 10. -gamayati -yituM), yAtrAM kf (c. 10. kArayati -yituM).
MARCHES: prAntAH (m. pl.): v. Boundary.

II Characteristic:(1) cihnam;(2) lakzaRam; (3) vyaYjanam.III Butt.: lakzyam(kzam), hitting (lit. piercing) the m.: lakzyaBedaH.IV A coin: mudrAviSezaH. Ph.: (a man) of m.: labDavarRa (f. rRA); to make a m.: *lakzaRaM sTApayati (c. of sTA).

MARK , s. (Sign, token by which a thing is known) cihnaM, lakzaRaM, lAYCanaM, liNgaM, aNkaH -NkaM, aBijYAnaM, vyaYjanaM, vyaYjakaH -kaM, lakzyaM, lakzma n. (n), lakzmaRaM, lalAmaM. — (Spot) kalaNkaH, aNkaH, cihnaM, vinduH m., vipluw (z), vipruw, gaRqaH. — (Mark on the body) sAmudraM, sAmudracihnaM, sAmudrikalakzaRaM, tilaH -lakaH, tilakAlakaH; ‘an interpreter of marks on the body,’ sAmudrikaH; ‘an auspicious mark,’ sulakzaRaM, sucihnaM; ‘having auspicious marks,’ sulakzaRI -RinI -Ri (n), sulakzaRikaH -kA -kaM; ‘having thirty-two auspicious marks,’ dvAtriMSallakzaRopetaH -tA -taM; ‘an inauspicious [Page483-b+ 51] mark,’ kulakzaRaM, apalakzaRaM, durlakzaRaM, duScihnaM; ‘having in- auspicious marks,’ kulakzaRI -RinI &c., kulakzaRaH -RA -RaM. — (Butt for shooting at) lakzyaM, vARalakzyaM, lakzaM, veDyaM, vyaDyaH, SaravyaM, dfzwiguRaH, pratikAyaH; ‘hitting the mark,’ lakzyaBedaH; ‘to hit the mark,’ lakzyaM Bid (c. 7. Binatti, BettuM) or vyaD (c. 4. viDyati, vyadDuM), lakzyaveDanaM kf. — (Line) reKA, leKA.

MARRIAGE , s. vivAhaH, udvAhaH -hanaM, udvahanaM, pariRayaH -yanaM, pARigrahaH -haRaM, pARigrAhaH, pARipIqanaM, hastekaraRaM, dAraparigrahaH, dArasaNgrahaH, dArakriyA, dArakarmma n. (n), dArADigamanaM, upayamaH, upayAmaH, lagna- kAryyaM, mETunaM, vADukyaM, niveSaH; ‘marriage-rite,’ vivAhaviDiH m., vivAhakriyA, vivAhasaMskAraH; ‘giving in marriage,’ dArikAdAnaM, dArikApradAnaM; ‘marriage-contract,’ vANniScayaH; ‘marriage- settlement,’ SulkaH -lkaM; ‘auspicious season for marriage,’ lagnatiTiH f., lagnamuhUrttaH -rttaM; ‘marriage-string, or ring hung round the neck of the bride, who wears it till she be- comes a widow, when it is broken,’ maNgalasUtraM, mANgalyatantuH m., sOBAgyatantuH m., kOtukaM; ‘marriage gifts,’ yOtakaM, OdvAhikaM, pAriRAyyaM, haraRaM, sudAyaH -yaM; ‘marriage festival,’ vivAhotsavaH, vivAhamahotsavaH; ‘ablution at marriage,’ maNgalasnAnaM; ‘com- pliments at marriage,’ jambUlaH, jambUlamAlikA; ‘second mar- riage,’ dvitIyavivAhaH, dvitIyasambanDaH. The following are diffe- rent forms of marriage, explained in Manu, chap. iii. verses 27 et seq.: AsuravivAhaH, ArzavivAhaH, ganDarvvavi- vAhaH, dEvavivAhaH, pESAcavivAhaH, prAjApatyavivAhaH, brAhmavivAhaH, rAkzasavivAhaH, prItivivAhaH. The svayaMvaraH is a form of mar- riage in which a girl chooses her own husband.
MARRIAGEABLE: vivAhayogya (f. gyA), and sim. comp.s, of m. age: vivAhayogyavayas (mfn.), M. n.; and that his son was of m. condition: dArakriyAyogyadaSaYca putram, R. v. 40.

MARRIAGEABLE , a. vivAhyaH -hyA -hyaM, udvAhyaH &c., voQavyaH -vyA -vyaM, vivAhayogyaH -gyA -gyaM, vivAhocitaH -tA -taM, vivAhopayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, vivAhakAlaprAptaH -ptA -ptaM, vivAhavayaskaH -skA -skaM, pariReyaH -yA -yaM; ‘as a girl,’ dfzwarajAH f. (s), saYjAtArttavA, AgatArttavA, ftuyuktA, ftumatI, maDyamA, maDyA, patIyantI.
MARRIED (adj.): vivAhitaH (tA, taM). Of men: kftodvAhaH and sim. expr.s.

MARRIED , p. p. vivAhitaH -tA -taM, udvAhitaH -tA -taM, UQaH -QA -QaM, upoQaH -QA -QaM, samUQaH -QA -QaM, kftavivAhaH -hA -haM, jAtavivAhaH -hA -haM, kftodvAhaH -hA -haM, kftadAraparigrahaH -hA -haM, pariRItaH -tA -taM, kfto- payamaH -mA -maM, jAtopayamaH -mA -maM, nirvizwaH -zwA -zwaM, prattaH -ttA -ttaM; ‘a married man,’ saBAryyaH, sapatnIkaH, strImAn m. (t), kftadAraH, sadAraH, kftadAraparigrahaH, kuwumbI m. (n), sakuwumbaH, BAryyoQaH; ‘a married woman,’ saBarttfkA, sapatikA, pativatnI, saDavA, suvAsinI; ‘newly married woman,’ navavaDUH f., navavarikA; ‘twice-married woman,’ punarBUH f., diDizUH f., diDIzUH f., diDizuH f.; ‘one who is married before his elder brother,’ parivettA m. (ttf).

Marrow, s. medas n., majjA, vapA, vasA, asTi-deha-sAraH, asTijaM, snigDA. 2 sAraH-raM, garBaH, muKyAMSaH; ‘he has knocked the m(arrow) out in no time’ acirAdeva tena sarvasya sAraH nizkfzwaH-gfhItaH. [Marrow]less, a. majjA-medo-hIna, a-niH-sAra. [Marrow]y, a. medasvin, sAravat, sasAra.
MARROW: majjA, m. -place: majjAsTAnam, Bha.

MARROW , s. majjA, vapA, vasA, medas n., medaH, majjA m. (n), majjanaM, sAraH, asTisAraH, dehasAraH, vIjaM, snigDA, vapAkft m., asTikft, asTijaM, asTijYaH, haqqajaM, SukrakaraH, tejas n., maDuraM, jIvanaM, maRiCidrA. — (Pith, essence) sAraH, garBaH, sAratA, SrezWAMSaH.
MARROW-BONE: majjAbahulamasTi (?).

MARROWLESS , a. majjAhInaH -nA -naM, medohInaH -nA -naM, vapASUnyaH -nyA -nyaM, gatasAraH -rA -raM, asAraH -rA -raM, niHsAraH -rA -raM.
MARROWY: majjAbahulaH (lA, laM).
MARROWY , a. majjAvAn -vatI -vat (t), sAravAn &c., medasvI -svinI -svi (n).

Marry, v. t. vi-ud-vah 1 P, pari-RI 1 P, upa-yam 1 A, prati-pari-grah 9 P. 2 (Take for husband) (patiM) vid 6 U or laB 1 A or aDigam 1 P, vf 5 U, 10 (varayati), vF 9 U, patyA saMyuj pass. 3 (Give in marriage) vivAhaM kf c., pARiM grah c., pra-dA 3 U, pARigrahaRaM saM-pad c.; vivAhena saMyuj 7 U, 10 or saMbaMD 9 P. adv. nUnaM, Kalu; See Indeed. [Marri]age, s. vivAhaH, udvAhaH, upayamaH, pariRayaH, pARigrahaH-haRaM, pARi-pIqanaM, dAraparigrahaH-aDigamanaM-kriyA; ‘give in m(arriage)’ vivAhaviDinA dA or pratipad c.; ‘m(arriage)-contract’ vANniScayaH; ‘m(arriage)-price’ SulkaH-lkaM; ‘m(arriage)-gifts’ yOtakaM, OdvA-hikaM, pAriRAyyaM, sudAyaH. ‘m(arriage)-string’ (vivAha-)kOtukaM, maMgalasUtraM. [Marri]ageable, a. vivAhayogya, pariReya, vivAhavayaska, udvA-hocita. [Marri]ed, a. UQa, pariRIta, upayata, kftavivAha, jAtopayama, nivizwa; ‘a m(arried) man’ strImAn, kuwuMbI, saBAryaH, kftadAraH, sapatnIkaH; ‘a m(arried) woman’ saBartfkA, pati-patnI, saDavA, suvAsinI; ‘twice m(arried)’ pu-narBUH, diDizuH-zUH; ‘one m(arried) before his elder brother’ parivettf; ‘the sin of such marriage’ pArivedyaM.

MARRY (v.): I To take a wife:(1) ut- vahati, vi-, samut- (vah, c. l.), who m. ies such a girl: yastAM samudvahet kanyAm, Ph.:(2) pariRayati, (nI, c. l.), when (Śiva) will m. Pārvatī: pariRezyati pArvatIM yadA, Ku.;(3) upayacCate (yam, c. l.), m. ed according to rite and took the girl: viDivadupayamya kanyAM ninye, D. ;(4) pARiM gfhnAti (grah, c. 9.), (with gen.);(5) by subs., at the time of m. ing another woman: stryantaravivAhakAle, Mit.II To take a husband:(1) pARiM grAhayati (c. of grah), with- out considering this how could I m.: avigaRayyEtat kaTaM pARiM grAhayizyAmi, K. ;(2) patiM gfhRAti, pari-, prati-, (grah, c. 9.) or yAti, upa-, (yA, c. 2.), or BartAraM samBAvayati (c. of BU), R. etc.;(3) vfRIte or varayati (vf, c. 9. and 10 (to select). III To cause to m.(1) yojayati, saM- (yuj, c. 10.), m. ed Rājavāhana with Avantisundarī: rAjavAhanenAvantisundarIM saMyojayAmAsa, D. ;(2) pARi- grahaRaM sampAdayati (c. of pad) (with gen.), R. ; (3) vivAhaM kArayati (c. of kf) (with gen.), M. n.; etc.IV To give away in [Page437] marriage:(1) dadAti or yacCati, pra-, (dA, c. 3. and l.): v. To give;(2) grAhayati (c. of grah), could not m. his daughter to the god of gods: devadevaM sutAM grAhayituM na SaSAka, Ku.
MARRY (interj.): satyam: v. Indeed.

To MARRY , v. a. (Unite a man and woman in wedlock) vivAha- saMskAreRa strIpuruzO saMyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yoktuM, c. 10. -yojayati -yituM) or sambanD (c. 9. -baDnAti -bandDuM) or vivAhasaMyuktO kf, vivAhasaMskAraM kf. — (Take for wife) vivah (c. 1. -vahati -te -voQuM), udvah, samudvah, udAvah, pariRI (c. 1. -Rayati -RetuM), upayam (c. 1. -yacCate -ti -yamate -yantuM), pARiM grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM), kanyAM parigrah or pratigrah or saNgrah, dAraparigrahaM kf, dArasaNgrahaM kf, dArADigamanaM kf, kanyApariRayaM kf, BAryyAM vid (c. 6. vindate -ti, vettuM) or anuvid; ‘he should marry a wife,’ kanyAM vivahet or upayacCeta, kanyAyAH pARiM gfhlAtu. — (Take for husband) patiM vid or vf (c. 5. vfRoti, varituM -rItuM), BartrA saMyuj in pass. (-yujyate), pativaraRaM kf, BarttfvaraRaM kf. — (Dispose of in marriage) vivAhArTaM kanyAM dA or pradA.
To MARRY , v. n. BartrA or BAryyayA saMyuj in pass. (-yujyate) or yuj, vivAhaM kf, udvAhaM kf, pariRayaM kf, pARigrahaRaM kf, dAraparigrahaM kf, upayamaM kf.

Mars, s. maMgalaH, BOmaH, aMgArakaH, BU-mahI-sutaH, lohitaH, ruDiraH, kujaH, lohitAMgaH. 2 kumAraH, kArtikeyaH, guhaH, skaMdaH, SaktiDaraH, zaqAnanaH, mahAsenaH, Sarajanman m., senAnIH, agniBUH, viSAKaH, zARmAturaH.

(The planet, fabled as the son of the earth) maNgalaH, maNgalagrahaH, BOmaH, aNgArakaH, kujaH, BUmijaH, BUsutaH, mahIsutaH, kziti- sutaH, AvaneyaH, DarAtmajaH, DarAsutaH, DarAputraH, navadIDitiH m., AzA- QaBavaH, SivaDarmmajaH, gagaRolmukaH, KolmukaH, lohitaH -takaH, lohitANgaH, raktANgaH, ruDiraH, AraH, GaRweSvaraH, fRAntakaH, caraH, jYaH. (In my- thology, the god of war). See KĀRTIKEYA.
Marsh, s. anUpadeSaH, kacCaH, kacCaBU-BUmi f., sajala-jalAQya-BUmiH. [Marsh]y, a. anUpa, AnUpa (pI f.), jalAQya, jalapUrRa, sajala, jalamaya (yI f.).

MARTEN: nakulajAtIyajantuBedaH.

MARTIAL , a. (Relating to war) yudDasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), raRa- sambanDI &c., yudDavizayaH -yA -yaM, raRavizayakaH -kA -kaM, sANgrAmikaH -kI -kaM, sAmarikaH -kI -kaM, sAmparAyikaH -kI -kaM. — (Suited to war) raRayogyaH -gyA -gyaM, yudDopayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, raRopayogI -ginI &c. — (Given to war) raRapriyaH -yA -yaM, raRAsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, raRavIraH -rA -raM, raRakAmI -minI &c.; ‘martial music,’ raRavAdyaM.

Martingal, s. talikA, aDobaMDanaM.
MARTINGAL , MARTINGALE, s. talikA, talasArakaH, aDobanDanaM.

MARTYR: svaDarmanyastajIvanaH (nA, naM) (?) and sim. comp.s.

MARTYROLOGY , s. sAkzicaritraSAstraM, svaDarmmArTaM prARatyAginAM caritravi- varaRaM or caritraliKanaM.

MARVELLOUS: AScarya (f. ryA): v. Wonderful.

AScaryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM, adButaH -tA -taM, vismayajanakaH -kA -kaM, vismayotpAdakaH -kA -kaM, AScaryyakaraH -rA -raM, AScaryyakArakaH -kA -kaM, AScaryyajanakaH -kA -kaM, camatkArajanakaH -kA -kaM, citraH -trA -traM, vicitraH -trA -traM, tAtaH -tA -taM; ‘a marvellous tale,’ citroktiH f.; ‘a marvellous action,’ adButakarmma n. MARVELLOUSNESS , s. adButatA -tvaM, AScaryyatvaM, vicitratA, sAScaryyatvaM, vEcitryaM, vismayajanakatA, apUrvvatvaM.
MARWAR , s. (The province) maruH m., maruBUH f. — (The inhabitants) maravaH m. pl., maruBuvaH m. pl.
Mascot, [Masco]te, SuBavastu n.

(puMs), puruzaH; ‘a masculine woman,’ fzaBI.

MASCULINENESS , s. puMstvaM, puruzatvaM -tA, pOruzaM, pOruzatA, puruzaSIlatA, puruzasvaBAvaH, puruzaprakftiH f.
Mash, v. t. saMpiz 7 P, saM-mfd 9 P, kzud 7 U, cUrR 10. s. saMpezaH, saMcUrRanaM udapezaH.

B. 141). s. sADanaM, upakaraRaM, dravyaM, kAraRaM, upAdAnaM, prakftiH, padArTaH, sADanavastu; ‘all m(aterial)s’ sAmagrI, sajjA, saMBAraH, dravya or upakaraRa-sAmagrI or saMBAraH; ‘writing m(aterial)s’ lipi-sajjA, leKanasADanAni; ‘the m(aterial) of cloth’ vastrayoniH-prakftiH. [Material]ism, s. lokA-yataM, anAtmavAdaH, cArvAkamataM. [Material]ist, s. lo-kAyatikaH, anAtmavAdin m.; vizayin m. [Material]ity, s. BOtikatvaM, mUrtimattvaM, &c. (n), kAryyaM, vizayaH, vyApAraH, arTaH, prayogaH. — (Pus, purulent matter) pUyaM, pUyaraktaM, pUyaSoRitaM dUzyaM, malajaM, kzatajaM, prasitaM, avakledaH.

To MATURATE , v. a. pac (c. 1. pacati, paktuM, c. 10. pAcayati -yituM), pAkaM kf or jan (c. 10. janayati -yituM), sapUyaM -yAM kf.

(Ramayati), pakvatAM-pAkaM-utpad c., pac c.; saM-pad c., sAD c., sidDIkf 8 U, kaWorIkf; kalAkalApAlocanakaWora-matiBiH (Ka. 7) ‘whose mind was m(atur)ed by studying &c.’ v. i. pac pass., pariRam 1 P, pAkaM-pariRAmaM-i or yA 2 P or gam 1 P; kaWorI-prOQI-BU 1 P; pariRataprajYasya kavervARIM (U. 7) ‘of m(atur)ed intellect’. MATURE (v.): paripAkaM nayati (nI, c. l.): v. To ripen, perfect.

To MATURE , v. a. pac (c. 1. pacati, paktuM, c. 10. pAcayati -yituM), pakvaM -kvAM kf, pakvIkf, paripakvaM -kvAM kf, paripakvIkf, pAkaM kf or jan (c. 10. janayati -yituM), pakvatAM or paripAkaM kf or jan, pariRAmaM kf or jan, sidDaM -dDAM kf, sidDIkf, sAD (c. 10. sADayati -yituM), sampannaM -nnAM kf, sampad (c. 10. -pAdayati -yituM).

(pacyate), paripac, pakvatAM or pakvadaSAM or pariRAmaM yA (c. 2. yAti -tuM) or i (c. 2. eti -tuM) or gam (c. 1. gacCati, gantuM), pariRataH -tA -taM BU, pAkonmuKaH -KA -KaM BU, sidDaH -dDA -dDaM BU, sampannaH -nnA -nnaM BU.
MATURED , p. p. pakvaH -kvA -kvaM, paripakvaH -kvA -kvaM, pariRataH -tA -taM, pakva- tApannaH -nnA -nnaM, sidDaH -dDA -dDaM, prOQaH -QA -QaM, sampannaH -nnA -nnaM, sampUrRaH -rRA -rRaM.
MATURELY: (1) expr. by adj.:(2) pariRatam: v. Also completely.
MATURELY , adv. sapAkaM, sapariRAmaM, paripakvaM, sampannaM, sampUrRaM. — (With full deliberation) susamIkzya, suvimfSya, suvicAryya.
MATURENESS, MATURITY: I Ripeness: pAkaH, pari-.II Perfection, completion: q. v.: pariRAmaH.
MATURESCENT , a. pAkonmuKaH -KA -KaM, ApakvaH -kvA -kvaM, pariRAmonmuKaH &c., pacatikalpaH -lpA -lpaM, pacatideSIyaH -yA -yaM, pacatideSyaH -SyA -SyaM.

MATURITY , MATURENESS, s. pAkaH, paripAkaH, pakvatA, paktiH f., paripakvatA, vipAkaH, supakvatA, supaktiH, pariRatiH f., pariRAmaH, pariRatatA -tvaM, pakvaBAvaH, pakvadaSA, pakvAvasTA, pariRatAvasTA, pacA, pAcA -cikA, prOQiH f., prOQatA, sidDatA, sidDiH f., sampannatA, sampUrRatA.
Matutinal, Matutine, a. prAtaHkAlika-prABAtika- (kI f.), pragetana (nI f.), uzasya, prAtar in comp.

MATUTINE, MATUTINAL: pragetanaH (nI, naM): v. Morning.
Maudlin, a. Amatta, mattaprAya-kalpa.
MAUDLIN: Drunk, intoxicated: q. v.: kzIvaH (vA, vaM). II Silly, foolish: q. v.: mUQaH (QA, QaM).
MAUDLIN , a. IzanmattaH -ttA -ttaM, mattakalpaH -lpA -lpaM, mattadeSIyaH -yA -yaM.
Maul, s. sTUlamudgaraH, GanaH. v. t. mudgareRa-laguqena pra-hf 1 P or taq 10. 2 vi-rUp 10, vikf 8 U.
MAUL (v.): laguqena tAqayati (taq, c. 10.), praharati (hf, c. l.), etc.
MAUL , s. vfhanmudgaraH, kAzWamudgaraH, sTUlamudgaraH, GanaH.
To MAUL , v. a. sTUlavetreRa taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM) or Ahan (c. 2. -hanti -ntuM) or prahf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM), vetrAGAtaM kf, vetrAGAtena kzatavikzatIkf.
MAULED , p. p. vetrAdiprahAreRa parikzataH -tA -taM or atikzuRRaH -RRA -RRaM.

MAUVAISE-HONTE , s. saBABItiH f., saBAkampaH, janaBItiH, lokaBItiH, janalajjA.

Mawkish, a. arasa, nIrasa, niHsattva; bI-Batsa, jugupsAvaha.

Maxillar, [Maxillar]y, a. hanusaMbaMDin, hanu in comp.

MAXIMUM: expr. with sarvvocca (f. ccA).
MAXIMUM , s. uttamasaMKyA, paramasaMKyA, aDikasaMKyA, uttamaparimARaM.

May, s. Gen. ex. by Potential of verbs. 2 (Showing wish or blessing) ex. by Benedictive or Imperative, ‘m(ay) god Siva protect you’ pAtu devaH Sivo vaH; ‘m(ay) I be satisfied’ kftArTo BUyAsaM. 3 (Liberty) gen. ex., by Pot.; See Liberty. 4 (Contingency) by Pot., with or without kadAcit. s. vESAKajyezWaM.
MAY (subs.): uttaravESAKapUrvajyEzWasaMvAdIyurupIyavarzasya paYcamo mAsaH.

MAY (v.): I = can: q. v.: by viDiliN, you m. carry the burden: tvaM BAraM vaheH, S. k.II Ex- -pressing desire or wish:(1) by ASIrliN, m. people live a man's life: jIvyAjjanaH puruzAyuzam, Vi.;(2) by low, m. you have a good journey: tava vartmani vartatAM Sivam, N.III. Denoting con- -tingency or liability: by viDiliN, an appli- cant m. or m. not get fortune: laBeta vA prArTayitA na vA Sriyam, Sa.; I might have disregarded this wretched life: kuryAmupekzAM hatajIvite'smin, R. Ph.: m. be (= perhaps: q.v.): expr. by viDiliN.
MAY , s. (The month) vESAKottarArdDaM, jyezWapUrvvArdDaM, vESAKaH, mADavaH, rADaH, jyEzWaH, SukraH, paYcamamAsaH.

MAY , v. auxil. (Be possible) samBU, Sak in pass. (Sakyate), SakyaH -kyA -kyaM BU or expressed by the potential. — (Have liberty, be allowed) expressed by the potential; as, ‘he may do that,’ sa tat kuryyAt. See also PERMITTED, ALLOWED, &c. (May be) syAt.
MAY-BUG: gomayotTABedaH.
MAY-DAY: memAsasya praTamadivasaH.
MAY-DAY , s. pUrvvoktapaYcamamAsasya praTamadivasaH.

MAY-QUEEN: *memAseSvarI.
Mayor, s. nagarADyakzaH, purAgraRIH. Mayoralty, s. purADyakzatA, nagarADikAraH.
MAYOR: *aDinAyakaH. M. ess: *aDinAyikA.
MAYOR , s. nagarADyakzaH, purADyakzaH, nagarADikArI m. (n).

Maze, s. gahanaM, kuMwilamArgaH, sugahanasTAnaM, durnirgamaM sTAnaM. 2 vakratA, gahanatA, kOwilyaM, vEzamyaM. [Maz]y, a. gahana, durnirgama, kuwila, jihma, ativakra.
MAZE (subs.): gahanam (?): v. Labyrinth
MAZE (v.): Akulayati: v. To disturb, amaze.

MAZY: gahanaH (nA, naM) (?); ati-, su-.
MAZY , a. gahanaH -nA -naM, sugahanaH -nA -naM, durnirgamaH -mA -maM, vakraH -krA -kraM, ativakraH -krA -kraM, BramajanakaH -kA -kaM, BrAntijanakaH -kA -kaM, duHSoDyaH -DyA -DyaM.
ME , pron. acc. c. mAM; ‘by me,’ mayA; ‘to me,’ mahyaM; ‘of me,’ mama.
MEACOCK , s. gehaSUraH, gehanardI m. (n), kApuruzaH, strIviDeyaH.
Mead, s. maDu, maDupAnIyaM. 2 Meadow, q. v.

MEAD , s. maDu n., maDupAnIyaM, maDunIraM, maDupayas n.
MEAD , MEADOW, s. kzetraM, kedAraH, yavasasTAnaM, SAqvalasTAnaM, gocaraH, gopra- cAraH; ‘meadow-grass,’ yavasaH, kzetriyaM; ‘relating to a meadow,’ kEdAraH -rI -raM, kzetrikaH -kI -kaM.
Meadow, s. kzetraM, gopracAraH, kedAraH. 2 sTalI, vanasTalI, SAdvalaM, yavasasTAnaM; ‘m(eadow) grass’ yavasaM. [Meadow]y, a. SAdvala, yavasIya.
MEADOW (1) kzetram (= field);(2) gopracAraH (= pasture land). M. -grass: yavasa (mn). M. -sweet: gulmapraBedaH.
MEADOWY , a. yavasamayaH -yI -yaM, yavasIyaH -yA -yaM, SAqvalaH -lA -laM.

MEAGER , MEAGRE, a. kfSaH -SA -SaM, parikfSaH -SA -SaM, kfSANgaH -NgI -NgaM, kzIRaH -RA -RaM, kzIRaSarIraH -rA -raM, kzIRamAMsaH -sA -saM, SuzkamAMsaH -sA -saM, SuzkANgaH &c., kzAmaH -mA -maM, kzAmaSarIraH &c., apuzwaH -zwA -zwaM, vipuzwaH -zwA -zwaM, tanuH -nuH -nvI -nu, vitanuH &c., pratanuH &c., SAtaH -tA -taM. — (Barren as soil) rukzaH -kzA -kzaM, banDyaH -nDyA -nDyaM; ‘a barren soil,’ marusTalaM -lI. — (As style) virasaH -sA -saM, PalguH -lguH -lgu.
MEAGERLY , adv. parikfSaM, sakArSyaM, kArSyena, kzIRatayA, rukzaM.

Meagre, a. kzAma, kfSa, kzIRa; See Lean. 2 asAra, virasa, nIrasa, Palgu, (style); baDyaM, rUkza (soil). 3 apUrRa, svalpa, tanu, stoka. [Meagre]ly, adv. kArSyena, svalpaM; ‘m(eagrely) attended’ tanuparivAra. [Meagre]ness, s. kfSatA, kzIRatA, kzAmatA, rUkzatA, tanutA, svalpatA, &c.
MEAGRE: I Thin, lean: q. v.: kfSaH (SA, SaM).II Scanty, insufficient: svalpa (f. lpA). III Wanting in richness:(1) Palgu (mfn.); (2) asAraH (rA, raM).
MEAGRELY: i. e. not richly: (1) Palgu;(2) asAram.
MEAGRENESS: I Leanness: q. v.: kfSatA.II Poorness:(1) asAratA;(2) apakfzwatA (= bad- -ness).III Scantiness: svalpatA.

Meal, s. saktu (m. pl.), kzodaH, cUrRaM, pizwaM. 2 BojanaM, aSanaM; AhAraH, AhAraviDiH; ‘took his m(eal)s’ AhAraviDimakarot, BojanaM nirvartayAmAsa, SarIrasTitiM samapAdayat ‘good m(eal)’ suBojanaM; ‘morning m(eal)’ prAtarASaH. [Meal]y, a. sacUrRa, kzodamaya (yI f.), 2 komala, masfRa, mfdu, cUrRasadfSa (SI f.); ‘m(ealy) mouthed’ mfduBAzin, komalavAc.
MEAL (subs.): I Flour: q. v.: cUrRam.II A repast:(1) Bojanam, one day taking a m. at night: ekAhaM rAtriBojanaH, Pa.;(2) Baktam, one day taking one m.: ekAham ekamaktASI, Pa. M. time: BojanavelA.

MEAL , s. (Flour) SaktuH m., kzodaH, pizwaM, cUrRaM, goDUmacUrRaM, goDUmakzodaH, apUzyaH, kzoditaM, guRqikaH -kA, samIdaH; ‘barley-meal,’ yavakzodaH. — (Repast) AhAraH, BojanaM, BakzaRaM, BakzikA, aSanaM, prASanaM, aByAhAraH, annaM; ‘good meal,’ suBojanaM, icCABojanaM; ‘poor meal,’ kuBojanaM; ‘light meal,’ laGvAhAraH, alpAhAraH, PalAhAraH; ‘morn- ing meal,’ prAtarBojanaM, prAtaraSanaM, prAtarASaH; ‘meal at noon,’ mADyAhnikaM; ‘at night,’ rAtriBojanaM; ‘meal supplied by another,’ parAnnaM; ‘row or party at a meal,’ paMktiH f.; ‘to make a meal,’ AhAraM kf, BojanaM kf; ‘one who has made a meal,’ kftAhAraH -rA -raM, kftaBojanaH -nA -naM; ‘making one's meals at irregular hours,’ vizamaBojanaM; ‘meal-time,’ Bojana- kAlaH, annakAlaH.
MEALINESS: cUrRamayatA etc.: v. Mealy.
MEALINESS , s. sacUrRatA -tvaM, kzoditatvaM, komalatA, SaktupUrRatA, mfdutA.
MEALMAN , s. SaktuvikrayI m. (n), cUrRavikretA m. (tf), kzodavikrayopajIvI m.
MEALY: I Consisting of meal: cUrRamayaH (yI, yaM) etc.II Like meal: cUrRasadfSaH (SI, SaM), etc. III Soft: q. v.: mfdu (f. dvI), m.-mouthed: mfduBAzin (f. RI) and sim. comp.s.
MEALY , a. cUrRamayaH -yI -yaM, kzodamayaH -yI -yaM, sacUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, SaktupUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, komalaH -lA -laM, mfdulaH -lA -laM, masfRaH -RA -RaM.
MEALY-MOUTHED , a. mfduBAzI -ziRI -zi (n), komalamuKaH -KI -KaM, mfdumuKaH &c.

Mean, a. maDya, maDyaparimARa-pramARa, maDyama. 2 maDya, maDyama, maDyasTita, vyavahita, maDyavartin, aMtargata; ‘in the m(ean)-while’ ‘in the m(ean)-time’ atrAMtare. 3 nIca, apa-ni-kfzwa, aDama, jaGanya, kadarya, kutsita, ni-, hIna, anArya, Kala, duzwa, vivarRa, pAmara, prAkfta, apasada, kzullaka, yApya, avama, avadya, garhya, laGu, kupUya, Kewa in comp., aRaka, rePa; tucCa, kzudra, kfpaRa, dIna, (mind &c.); (in birth) hIna-nIca-jAti, aMtyajAtIya, akulIna, ku or kA in comp.; ‘m(ean)-spirited’ laGucetas, kzudramAnasa, kfpaRabudDi, kApuruza, aDamavftti. v. t. uddiS 6 P, iz 6 P, aBipra-i 2 P; oft. ex. by desid. forms, or by kAma or manas in comp. with inf.; ‘now what do you m(ean) to do’ aTa BavAn kiM kartumanAH or kiM cikIrzati; See Intend. 2 gam c. To MELT , v. a. vilI in caus. (-lAyayati -lApayati -yituM), vidru (c. 10. -drAvayati -yituM), dravIkf, gal (c. 10. gAlayati -yituM), vidrAvaRaM kf, gAlanaM kf, vidrutIkf, vilInIkf, ArdrIkf, sArdrIkf. — (Soften to love or tenderness) karuRArdrIkf, dayArdrIkf, BAvArdrIkf, sArdrIkf, ArdrIkf, vatsala (nom. vatsalayati -yituM), vatsalIkf.

Of a family: parivArAH (m. pl.); aNgam: v. Limb (II).VI Of an equation: pakzaH, Vij.

MEMBER , s. Mental, a. mAnasika (kI f.), mAnasa (sI f.), manaHsTa, cittagata, cittaja, manoBava; gen. by manas or citta in comp.; ‘m(ental) distrese’ manastApaH. [Mental]ly, adv. manasA, budDyA.

MENTION , s. aBiDAnaM, aBiDA, AKyAnaM, kaTanaM, upAdAnaM, grahaRaM, nAmagrahaRaM, nAmanirdeSaH, nivedanaM, kIrttanaM, saNkIrttanaM, uccAraRaM, uddeSaH, ulleKaH -KanaM, SrutiH f.; ‘no mention whatever,’ na ganDaleSaH; ‘to make mention.’ See the next.

See QUICKSILVER. (A preparation of mercury used in medicine) GanasAraH, candrodayaH, caturmuKaH; ‘Calx or oxid of mercury,’ rasaBasma n. (n), pAradaBasma n.; ‘white sublimate or muriate of mercury,’ rasakarpUraH; ‘sulphuret of mercury,’ kajjalI. — (Interpreter or preceptor of the gods) vfhaspatiH m.

Mercy, s. dayA, kfpA, karuRA, anukaMpA, anu-kroSaH, kAruRyaM, GfRA, dayA, kfpASIlatA, dayAlutA, kzamASIlatA, dayA-kfpA-budDi f. 2 prasAdaH, anugrahaH. 3 kzamA, titikzA ‘fountain of m(ercy)’ karuRAkaraH, dayAsAgaraH; dayA-niDiH, ‘an object of m(ercy)’ kfpApAtraM-BA-janaM, anukaMpya, anugrAhya, tapasvin; ‘to show m(ercy)’ day 1 A (with gen.), anu-kaMp 1 A (with acc.), dayAM kf 8 U (with loc.); ‘m(ercy), Oh king’ kzamasva rA-jan. [Merci]ful, a. dayAlu, kfpAlu, kfpA-dayA-karuRA-SIla, karuRArdra, dayArdra, anukaMpin, sadaya, sakaruRa, sAnukroSa, kzamASIla; vatsala, dayAbudDi-dfzwi; See Kind. [Merci]fully, adv. sadayaM, sakaruRaM, sAnukaMpaM, dayayA, karuRayA, sAnukroSaM. [Merci]fulness, s. dayA, kfpA, GfRA, dayASIlatA, anukaMpA, vAtsalyaM; See (s.). [Merci]less, a. nirdaya, nizkaruRa, nirGfRa, akaruRa, kaWora, nizkfpa, nizWura, nfSaMsa. [Merci]lessly, adv. nirdayaM, nizkfpaM, nirGfRaM, nizWuraM.

MERCY: (1) kfpA, do not talk of m.: kfpeti cedastu, Ki. xiv. 16.;(2) karuRA (= pity), m. does not check you: tvAM karuRA ruRadDi na, N. i. 135;(3) dayA (= kindness), to have m.: dayAM karoti, K. : (4) anukampA (= compassion);(5) dayAlutA; (7) GfRA.

MERCY , s. (Disposition to forgive, clemency) dayA, kfpA, dayA- SIlatA, kfpASIlatA, kzamASIlatA, dayAlutA, kfpAlutA, dayAbudDiH f., kzamAbudDiH f. — (Compassion) anukampA, kAruRyaM, karuRA, GfRA, anukroSaH, kfpA, dayA. — (Grace, favor) anugrahaH, prasAdaH, prasannatA, anuroDaH. — (Pardon) kzamA, pApamArjanaM, pApaSudDiH f., nizkftiH f.; ‘ocean or fountain of mercy,’ dayAsAgaraH, dayAsamudraH, dayAniDiH m., karuRAkaraH; ‘vessel or recipient of mercy,’ dayApAtraM, kfpApAtraM, dayABAjanaM, anukampanIyaH -yA, anugrAhyaH -hyA; ‘to shew or have mercy,’ dayAM kf, anukamp (c. 1. -kampate -mpituM), day (c. 1. dayate -yituM), kzam (c. 1. kzamate -mituM, kzantuM); ‘mercy!’ trAhi, trAyasva, kzamasva, kzamyatAM.
MERCY-SEAT: kfpAsTAnam, and sim. comp.s (?. comp. kfpAsinDuH).
MERCY-SEAT , s. karuRAsanaM, ISvarAsanaM, parameSvarAsanaM, ISvaraprasAdAsanaM.

Mere, a. kevala, SudDa; gen. ex. by eva, or mAtra in comp.; ‘by m(ere) touch’ sparSamA-treRa; ‘a m(ere) fool’ mUrKa eva, kevalamUrKaH. s. saras n., hradaH; See Lake. 2 paryaMtaH, sImA; See Boundary. [Mere]ly, adv. kevalaM, eva, mAtra in comp.; ‘by m(erely) advising’ upadeSa-mAtrAt, upadeSAdeva, &c.
MERE (subs.): I A lake: q. v.: saras (n.). II A boundary: q. v.

MERE (adj.): (1) kevalaH (lA, laM) (= bare), m. policy is cowardice: kAtaryaM kevalA nItiH, R. xvii. 47.; not of m. milk: na kevalAnAM payasAm, R. ii. 63.;(2) with eva (to emphasize = absolute), with your m. look: vilokanenEva tava, Si. i. 29.;(3) SudDaH (dDA, dDaM) (= pure, unmixed), from a m. bath: SudDasnAnAt, Me. ii. 30.;(4) mAtra, in comp. (= simply), on account of m. caste: jAtimAtreRa, H. i. 57.

MERE , a. (Only, pure) mAtra in comp., mAtrakaH -kA -kaM, kevalaH -lA -lI -laM, kevalI -linI -li (n), SudDaH -dDA -dDaM; ‘a mere man,’ manuzyamAtraH; ‘mere touch,’ sparSamAtraM; ‘mere words,’ vANmAtraM; ‘by mere talk,’ vAkyamAtreRa; ‘a mere grammarian,’ kevalavE- yAkaraRaH; ‘a mere logician,’ kevalanEyAyikaH.
MERE , s. (A lake) saras n., hradaH, sarovaraH, payorASiH m. — (Boun- dary) sImA, parisImA, antaH, samantaH, paryyantaM.
MERELY: (1) by adj.;(2) kevalam (= only, barely).
MERELY , adv. mAtraM, mAtreRa -trAt, kevalaM, kuwwAraM, Kalu; ‘by merely inspecting,’ nirIkzaRamAtreRa; ‘from caste merely,’ jAtimAtrAt.
Meretricious, a. kftrimaSoBAmaya (yI f.), bAhyarucira, kftrimarAgavat, miTyASoBana. 2 paRyAMganIya, veSyAsaMbaMDin. [Meretricious]ly, adv. mi-TyASoBayA.
MERETRICIOUS: I Lit.:(1) vESikaH (kI, kaM); (2) by comp.: v. Harlot.II Fig.: vESikaH (kI, kaM): v. Showy, gaudy.

MERETRICIOUS , a. (Relating to harlots) veSyAsambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), vArANganIyaH -yA -yaM, paRyANganIyaH -yA -yaM. — (Having a false show, gaudy) kftrimaSoBAvAn -vatI -vat (t), kftrimaSoBAmayaH -yI -yaM, miTyASoBanaH -nA -naM, kftrimAlaNkAramayaH -yI -yaM, miTyAlaNkAravAn &c., miTyArAgI -giRI &c.
MERETRICIOUSLY , adv. veSyArUpeRa, kftrimaSoBApUrvvaM, miTyASoBApUrvvaM.
MERETRICIOUSNESS: vESikam, -tA: v. Also gaudiness.

Merge, v. i. ni-, masj 6 P, avagAh 1 A (lit); nipAgras- pass., pra-vi-lI 4 A, vi-lup pass., naS 4 P, (fig.); ‘one fault m(erge)s in a collection of good qualities’ eko hi dozA guRasannipAte nimajjati (K. i. 3). v. t. masj c., (majjayati), avagAh c. 2 naS c., vi-lup 6 P or c., gras 1 A, ni-pA 1 P, pra-vi-lI c. Mersion, s. majjanaM, avagAhaH-hanaM.
MERGE: I Trans.: majjayati, ni-, (c. of masj): v. To immerse.II Intrans.: majjati, ni-, (masj, c. 1.), Ku. i. 3.

To MERGE , v. a. (Immerge) majj (c. 10. majjayati -yituM), nimajj, magnaM -gnAM kf, avagAh (c. 10. -gAhayati -yituM), gAh. — (Cause to be swallowed up or lost) grastaM -stAM kf, vilInaM -nAM kf, nipItaM -tAM kf, naS (c. 10. nASayati -yituM), nazwaM -zwAM kf.

To MERGE , v. n. majj (c. 6. majjati -jjituM, maMktuM), avagAh (c. 1. -gAhate -hituM -gAQuM), grastaH -stA -staM BU, nipItaH -tA -taM BU, naS (c. 4. naSyati [Page496-b+ 51] -SituM), magnaH -gnA -gnaM BU, vilI (c. 4. -lIyate -letuM).
MERGED , p. p. magnaH -gnA -gnaM, nimagnaH -gnA -gnaM, avagAQaH -QA -QaM, lInaH -nA -naM, vilInaH -nA -naM, nilInaH -nA -naM, luptaH -ptA -ptaM.

Meridian, s. maDyAhnaH, dinamaDyaM, maDyAhna-kAlaH-samayaH. 2 KamaDyaM; ‘distance from the first m(eridian)’ reKAMtaraM; ‘the sun is on the m(eridian)’ naBaso maDyamalaMkaroti BAnuH. 3 parA kowiH-kAzWA, utkarzaH. a. mADyAhnika (kI f.). 2 KamaDyasaMbaMDin. 3 uttama, parama; oft. ex. by parA kowiH, parA kAzWA.

MERIDIAN (subs.): I Mid-day: q. v.II Climax: q. v.III In astro.: (UrdDaM) [Page445] yAmyottaravfttam (the circle). Ph.: when the sun is on the m.: samArUQe maDyamahRaH savitari, K. ; maDyagato BAnuH, B.
MERIDIAN (adj.): I Mid-day: q. v.II Highest: expr. by parA kowiH (with gen.): v. Acme.

MERIDIAN , s. (Midday, noon) maDyAhnaH, maDyAhnakAlaH, maDyandinaM, dina- maDyaM. — (Meridian of the place in geography and astronomy) yAmyottaravfttaM, KamaDyaM; ‘meridians of right ascension,’ krAnti- sUtrARi n. pl.; ‘distance from the first meridian,’ reKAntaraM, deSAntaraM; ‘distance between the meridians,’ spazwapariDiH m. — (Height, highest point) uccatA, uccapadaM, agraM, maDyaM.

MERIDIAN , a. (Relating to midday) mADyAhnikaH -kI -kaM, mADyandinaH -nI -naM, maDyAhnakAlInaH -nA -naM. — (Pertaining to the meridian line) yAmyottaravfttasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), KamaDyasambanDI &c. — (Highest) uccatamaH -mA -maM, uttamaH -mA -maM.
Meridional, a. dakziRadeSIya; dakziRABimuKa (KI f.).
MERIDIONAL: yAmya (f. myA): v. Southern.
MERIDIONAL , a. dakziRadiksTaH -sTA -sTaM, dakziRamuKaH -KA -KaM, dakzi- RABimuKaH &c., dAkziRikaH -kI -kaM, dakziRadeSIyaH -yA -yaM.

Merit, s. guRaH, yogyatA, pAtratA, utkarzaH, SrezWatA, viSizwatA, viSezaH, guRotkarzaH, guRa-vattA. 2 (‘M(erit)s’) guRAguRO, guRadozO, DarmA-DarmO. 3 puRyaM, DarmaH, sukftaM, Sreyas n., vfzaH; ‘acquired by m(erit)’ puRyArjita; ‘efficacy of m(erit)’ puRyapratApaH-praBAvaH; ‘one possessing many m(erit)s’ puRyaniDiH-rASiH-sAgaraH, puRyA-tmA. v. t. arh 1 P, arh-yogya- in comp.; See Deserve; ‘m(erit)ing censure’ niMdya, garha-RIya, niMdApAtraM. [Merit]ed, a. yukta, ucita, yogya; See Proper. Meritorious, a. praSasya, SlAGya, praSasta, SlAGArha, praSaMsArha. 2 guRin, guRavat, guRasaMpanna, guRopeta, guRAnvita. 3 puRyavat, puRyaSIla, puRyAtman, puRyAtmaka, puRyaSAlin; puRya, puRyarUpa, avadAta (deed); ‘a m(eritorious) deed’ puRyaM, DarmaH, sukftaM, avadAtaM karma. [Meritorious]ly, adv. SlAGyatayA, praSasyaM. [Meritorious]ness, s. guRavattA, pAtratA, yogyatA, &c.
MERIT (subs.): (1) guRaH, not to enumerate your m.s: na guRAnAmiyattayA, R. x. 32.; according to (our) m.s: guRadozataH, Mal.;(2) utkarzaH (= ex- -cellence).
MERIT (v.): arhati (arh, c. l.): v. To deserve, earn.

MERIT , s. (Desert) guRaH, yogyatA, upayogaH, upayuktatA, pAtratA. — — (Excellence, great merit) guRotkarzaH, guRaprakarzaH, guRavESezyaM, guRitA, guRapUgaM, saguRatA, guROGaM, guRavattA, guRatA, guRamahat n., utkarzaH, utkfzwatA, SrezWatA, SasyaM, praSasyaM, sAratA -tvaM; ‘appreciating merit,’ guRagrahaRaM; ‘one who does so,’ guRagrAhI m. (n), guRa- grAhakaH, guRajYaH. — (Merits, good or bad) guRAguRaM, guRadozO m. du., guRadozaM, sArAsAraM, puRyApuRyaM, DarmmADarmmaM; ‘testing one's merits,’ guRAguRaparIkzA, guRadozaparIkzaRaM. — (Merit acquired through works, according to the Hindu notion) puRyaM, Sreyas n., sukftaM, DarmmaH, vfzaH, tapas n., niyamaH, puRyasAmagrI, saYcitaM; ‘acqui- sition of merit,’ puRyArjanaM, puRyasampAdanaM, SreyaHsampAdanaM; ‘acquired by merit,’ puRyArjitaH -tA -taM, puRyavijitaH -tA -taM; ‘reward of merits,’ puRyaPalaM; ‘good fortune, as the result of merits,’ puRyodayaH; ‘merit acquired in some former birth,’ pUrvvapuRyaM; ‘mightiness of merit,’ puRyapratApaH; ‘person of great merit,’ puRyaniDiH m., SreyoniDiH m., puRyasAgaraH, puRyarASiH m., puRyAtmA m. (n), puRyajanaH; ‘a work giving an account of the merits of any holy place or object,’ mAhAtmyaM.

To MERIT , v. a. arh (c. 1. arhati -te -rhituM), arhaH -rhA -rhaM or upayuktaH -ktA -ktaM or yogyaH -gyA -gyaM or ucitaH -tA -taM BU or as; ‘he merits a kingdom,’ rAjyam arhati; ‘he merits punishment,’ daRqArho Bavati or asti; ‘to merit confidence,’ viSvAsapAtraM BU. See To DESERVE.
MERITED (adj.): upayukta (f. ktA): v. Proper, fit.
MERITED , p. p. upayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, yogyaH -gyA -gyaM, arhitaH -tA -taM.
MERITORIOUS: praSasta (f. stA): v. Praiseworthy, good.

MERITORIOUS , a. (Deserving a reward) vetanArhaH -rhA -rhaM, dakziRArhaH &c., pratiPalArhaH &c. — (Deserving of honor) SlAGyaH -GyA -GyaM, SlAGanIyaH -yA -yaM, praSaMsanIyaH -yA -yaM, SaMsyaH -syA -syaM, praSastaH -stA -staM, SlAGArhaH -rhA -rhaM, praSaMsArhaH &c. — (Having great merit) guRavAn -vatI -vat (t), guRasampannaH -nnA -nnaM, guRI -RinI -Ri (n), guRAnvitaH -tA -taM, SrezWaH -zWA -zWaM, uttamaguRaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM. — (Having great religious merit) puRyavAn -vatI &c., puRyaSAlI -linI &c., puRyarUpaH -pA -paM, puRyAtmakaH -kA -kaM, kftapuRyapuYjaH -YjA -YjaM; ‘meritorious act,’ puRyakaM, vrataH -taM, niyamaH, tapas n.
MERITORIOUSLY: (1) praSastam;(2) SoBanam: v. Well.
MERITORIOUSLY , adv. yaTA vevanam or pratiPalam arhati taTA, SlAGanIyaM.
MERITORIOUSNESS , s. yogyatA, upayuktatA, vetanArhatA, vetanayogyatA, upayogitA, pAtratA, guRitA, guRasampannatA, SlAGyatA, puRyatA, puRyavattvaM.
MERL, MERLE (subs.): kfzRavarRaH pakziBedaH.
MERLIN , s. (Kind of hawk) SyenaBedaH, kapotAriH m.
Mermaid, s. matsyAMganA, matsyastrI.
MERMAID: (1) matsyakumArI (?);(2) matsyakanyA (?);(3) jalanArI.
MERMAID , s. matsyakanyA, matsyakumArI -rikA, kavikalpitaH kanyordDvakAyo matsyADaHkAyo jantuviSezaH, samudrIyastrI.
MERMAN: *matsyapuruzaH; jalanaraH.
MERRILY: (1) saharzam;(2) sAnandam;(3) sollAsam.
MERRILY , adv. saharzaM, sAnandaM, ullAsena, ullasitaM, sahAsaM, sahAsyaM, sahasitaM, parihAsena, hfzwamanasA, sakOtukaM, praPullamanasA, ullasavat, hfzwavat, pramodena.

MERRIMENT , s. ullasatA, ullAsaH, harzaH, praharzaH, AnandaH, sAnandatA, praPullatA, hAsyaM, prahasanaM, hAsikA, parihAsaH, parIhAsaH, AhlAdaH, mudA, pramodaH, kOtukaM, prahfzwatA, hfzwatA, krIqA, krIqAkOtukaM, vilAsaH, lIlA, KelA, hAsyavinodaH, utsavaH, carBawI.
MERRINESS , s. hfzwatA, prahfzwatA, ullasatA, ullAsitA, hAsyamuKatA, hAsya- vfttiH f., sAnandatA, praPullatA, sadAnanditA.

Merry, a. pra-, hfzwa, sAnaMda, sollAsa, protPulla, pramudita, prahfzwacitta; AnaMda-ullAsa-hAsya-vftti, prasannavadana, vilAsin, vinodin, parihAsaSIla. 2 hAsyakara (rI f.), vino-daka; ‘to make m(erry)’ utsavaM kf 8 U; ‘to be m(erry)’ ullas 1 P, mud 1 A; See Delight. ‘m(erry) andrew’ BaMqaH, vEhAsikaH, vidUzakaH. ‘m(erry)-making’ AnaMdotsavaH, utsavakaraRaM. [Merri]ly, adv. saharzaM, sollAsaM, sAnaMdaM, hfzWamanasA. [Merri]ment, s. pra-, harzaH, ullAsaH, pra-, modaH, AnaMdaH, AhlAdaH; hAsyaM, parihAsaH, utsavaH, kOtukaM, vilAsaH, vinodaH; lIlA, KelA; ‘what is said in m(erriment)’ hAsyavinodaH; narmAlApaH, vinodokti f. [Merry]ness, s. hfzwatA, sAnaMdatA, AnaMdavftti f.
MERRY: I Cheerful, joyful:(1) hfzwa (f. zwA), pra-;(2) sAnanda (f. ndA);(3) hfzwamanas (mfn.); (4) ullasaH (sA, saM).II Causing mirth: hAsakaraH or hAsyakaraH (rI, raM).

MERRY , a. hfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, hfzwahfdayaH -yA -yaM, prahfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, prahfzwacittaH -ttA -ttaM, ullasaH -sA -saM, ullAsI -sinI -si (n), ullAsavfttiH -ttiH -tti, parihAsaSIlaH -lA -laM, hAsyavfttiH -ttiH -tti, hAsyamuKaH -KI -KaM, hAsyavadanaH -nA -naM, suhasAnanaH -nA -naM, AnandI -ndinI &c., Ana- ndavfttiH -ttiH -tti, hAsI -sinI &c., pramodI -dinI &c., mudAnvitaH -tA -taM, muditaH -tA -taM, vilAsI &c., vinodI &c., sumanAH -nAH -naH (s), kOtukI &c., upajAtakOtukaH -kA -kaM. — (Causing mirth) hAsyajanakaH -kA -kaM, hAsyotpAdakaH -kA -kaM, vinodakaH -kA -kaM; ‘to make merry,’ utsavaM kf; ‘to be merry,’ ullas (c. 1. -lasati -situM), sumana (nom. sumanAyate), kOtukaM kf.
MERRY-ANDREW: pIWamardaH (?): v. Buffoon.
MERRY-ANDREW , s. BaRqaH, vEhAsikaH, vidUzakaH, parihAsavedI m. (n).
MERRY-MAKING, MERRY-MEETING: AnandotsavaH, and sim. comp.s.
MERRY-MAKING , s. utsavaH, utsavakaraRaM, mahotsavaH, vilAsakaraRaM.
MERRY-THOUGHT: kukkuwasya dviSUlamuro'sTi.
MERSION , s. majjanaM, pramajjanaM, nimajjanaM, vigAhaH -hanaM, avagAhanaM.
Meru, s. meruH, sumeruH, hemAdrI, ratnasAnuH, surAlayaH.

MERU , s. (The sacred mountain, in the centre of the seven continents, at the extremity of the world's axis, where the gods reside, corresponding to Mount Olympus of the Greeks) meruH m., sumeruH m., surAlayaH, devAlayaH, hemAdriH m., ratnasAnuH m.
MESEEMS: manye: v. To think.
MESENTERIC , a. antrapeSIsambanDI -nDinI &c., maDyAntrikaH -kI -kaM.
Mesentery, s. aMtrapeSI.
MESENTERY: antrapeSI (?); antrakozaH (?).
MESENTERY , s. antrapeSI, antrAvaraRatvak f. (c), maDyAntrAvaraRatvak f., maDyAntrabanDanatvak f.; ‘enlargement of the mesentery,’ plIhA m. (n).
Mesh, s. jAlaraMDraM-CidraM-aMtaraM. v. t. jAle pat c. or baMD 9 P. [Mesh]y, a. jAlarUpa, jAlAkAra.
MESH: I Net: pASaH.II Its interstice: Cidram.
MESH , s. (Interstice of a net) jAlAntaraM, jAlaCidraM, jAlaranDraM.
To MESH , v. a. jAle or pASe pat (c. 10. pAtayati -yituM), jAle pAtayitvA banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDuM), jAlabadDaM -dDAM kf.
MESHY: jAlAkAraH (rA, raM), and sim. comp.s.
MESHY , a. jAlarUpaH -pA -paM, jAlAkAraH -rA -raM, jAlamayaH -yI -yaM, jAlavannirmitaH -tA -taM jAlavad bahuCidramayaH -yI -yaM.
Meslin, s. miSraDAnyaM, DAnyamiSraRaM. a. miSraDAnyakfta.
MESLIN , s. (Mixture of grain) miSraDAnyaM, DAnyamiSraRaM, miSrAnnaM.
MESMERIZE: *masmarayati (nomi.); hastacAlanAdinA vivaSIkaroti.

Mess, s. annaM, annapAtraM. 2 gaRAnnaM, sahaBojanaM; sahaBojinaH, paMktiBojinaH (pl.); saha-BojipaMkti f. gaRaH, gaRAnnapaMktiH. 3 saMkaraH, pra-saM-kIrRakaM, sannipAtaH, saMmiSraRaM, saMkulaM; ‘m(ess)-mate’ saha-paMkti-Bojin m. v. i. saha-ekatra-Buj 7 A or aS 9 P, paMktiBojanaM kf 8 U. v. t. saMmiSr 10, saMkF 6 P.
MESS (v.): saha or ekatra Bojanam or AhAraM karoti.
MESS (subs.): I A dish or quantity of food: not expr.II Of persons: expr. with, ekapAkaBojin (m.), Mit.III A medley: saNkaraH, Mah. 69. 77.

MESS , s. (Dish or quantity of food) annaBAgaH, annapAtraM, annaM, sidDAnnaM, yat KAdyadravyam ekapuruzasya parivezyate. — (Food prepared for a number of persons in common) gaRAnnaM. — (Set of persons who eat together) paMktiH f., sahaBojipaMktiH f., sahaBoja- napaMktiH f., gaRAnnapaMktiH f., jagDipaMktiH f., sahaBojigaRaH, sahaBojinaH m. pl., paMktiBojinaH m. pl., gaRacakrakaM, gaRacakraM; ‘not admissible into the same mess,’ apAMkteyaH -yA -yaM, apAMktaH -ktA -ktaM, apAMktyaH -ktyA -ktyaM. — (Medley, litter) saNkaraH, nAnAdravyasANkaryyaM, nAnAdravyasannipAtaH, nAnAdravyasammiSraRaM, saNkIrRakaM, saNkulakaM. — (Plight) durdaSA, durgatiH f., kardamaH; ‘in a mess,’ durdaSAgrastaH -stA -staM.
To MESS , v. n. (Eat in company) paMktiBojanaM kf, ekapaMktiBojanaM kf, sahaBojanaM kf, ekatra BojanaM kf or AhAraM kf.
To MESS , v. a. (Make into a mess) saNkarIkf, sammiSrIkf.

Message, s. saMdeSaH, vAcikaM, saMdeSavAc f., vArtA, SAsanaM; ‘bearing a m(essage)’ dOtyaM, dUtyaM, prezyaBAvaH; ‘sending on a m(essage)’ pratiSAsanaM. MESSED , p. p. saNkarIkftaH -tA -taM, sammiSritaH -tA -taM, sannipatitaH -tA -taM.
MESSENGER: (1) sandeSaharaH;(2) vArttAvahaH;(3) vEvaDikaH (rare).

MESSENGER , s. dUtaH, sandeSaharaH, vArttAharaH, vArttAyanaH, vAcikaharaH, AKyAyakaH, aDvagaH, prayojyaH, saYcArakaH, cAraH, DAvakaH, samAcAradAyakaH, kAryyaNkaraH, nisfzwArTaH; ‘female messenger,’ dUtI -tiH -tikA, saYcArikA.
MESSIAH: *trARABiziktaH. M.-ship: *trARABiziktatA.
MESSIAH , s. (The Anointed) aBiziktaH, aBiziktatrAtA m. (tf).
MESSMATE: (1) ekapAkaBojin (m.):(2) ekasTAlI, Mit.
MESSMATE , s. paMktiBojI m. (n), ekapaMktiH m., samapaMktiH, sahaBojI m.

MESSUAGE , s. vAsagehaM -haH, vAsagfhaM, gfhavAwikA, vAstuvAwI.

Metacarpus, s. karaBaH, pIluH.
METACARPUS , s. karaBaH, pIluH m., karaBAsTi n., prapARiH m., prahastaH.
Metachronism, s. nyUnakAlanirUpaRaM.
METACHRONISM , s. nyUnakAlanirUpaRaM, nyUnanirUpitakAlaH.

Metal, s. DAtuH, lohaH-haM, tEjasaM; ‘base m(etal)’ kupyaM; ‘fused m(etal)’ rasaDAtuH, DAturasaH; ‘inferior m(etal)’ upaDAtuH. [Metal]lic, [Metal]lical, a. DAtusaMbaMDin. 2 DAtumaya (yI f.), DAturUpa, lOha (hI f.), DAtu-loha- in comp. [Metal]list, s. DAtujYaH, DAtukarmakAraH. Metalliferous, a. DAtuprada. Metalliform, a. DAtusadfSa (SI f.). Metallography, s. DAtu-SAstraM-vidyA. Metallurgy, s. DAMtuSoDanaM.
METAL (subs.): (1) DAtuH;(2) lohaH (rare).

METAL , s. DAtuH m., lohaH, tEjasaM, suvarRarUpyAdi n.; ‘base metal,’ kupyaM; ‘factitious metal,’ kftrimaDAtuH m.; ‘fused,’ rasaDAtuH m., rasaH; ‘inferior,’ upaDAtuH m.; ‘melting metals together,’ Avarttana; ‘the metals collectively,’ DAtujAtaM, azwaDAtu n. The eight metals are, ‘gold,’ suvarRaM; ‘silver,’ rUpyaM; ‘copper,’ tAmraM; ‘brass,’ pittalaM; ‘bell-metal, or a kind of pewter,’ kAMsyaM; ‘tin,’ trapu; ‘lead,’ sIsakaM; ‘iron,’ lohaH. Some make ‘steel,’ tIkzRAyasaM, one of the eight metals, instead of kAMsyaM.
METALLIC: expr. by comp., m. property: GAtuguRaH.

METALLIC , METALLICAL, a. (Pertaining to metals) DAtusambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), lohasambanDI &c. — (Consisting of metal) DAtumayaH -yI -yaM, lohamayaH -yI -yaM, lOhaH -hI -haM, DAturUpaH -pA -paM, DAtunirmitaH -tA -taM, sidDarasaH -sA -saM, tEjasaH -sI -saM, DAtuguRakaH -kA -kaM, DAtu or loha in comp.
METALLIFEROUS: DAtugarBa (f. rBA) and sim. comp.s.
METALLIFEROUS , a. DAtUtpAdakaH -kA -kaM, DAtujanakaH -kA -kaM.
METALLIST , s. DAtuparIkzakaH, DAtujYaH, DAtuvid m., DAtukarmmakArI m. (n).
METALLOGRAPHY , s. DAtuvarRanaM, DAtuvivaraRaM, DAtuvivaraRavidyA.
METALLURGIST , s. DAtukarmmakArI m. (n), DAtuSoDakaH, DAtuSoDanakft m.
METALLURGY: *DAtunizkarzaH, DAtuSoDanAdikalA.
METALLURGY , s. DAtuSoDanaM, DAtuSoDanavidyA, DAtukarmma n. (n).

METAMORPHOSE: m. d: parivfttaSarIraH (rA, raM): v. To change.
To METAMORPHOSE , v. a. rUpapariRAmaM kf, pariRatarUpaM -pAM kf, SarIra- pariRAmaM kf, AkArapariRAmaM kf, rUpAntaraM kf, dehAntaraM kf, rUpavikAraM kf, rUpaBedaM kf.

METAMORPHOSED , p. p. pariRatarUpaH -pA -paM, pariRataSarIraH -rA -raM, pariRatAkAraH -rA -raM, pariRatAkftiH -tiH -ti, rUpAntarIkftaH -tA -taM, vikftAkAraH -rA -raM, pariRataH -tA -taM, vikftaH -tA -taM, BinnarUpaH -pA -paM.
METAMORPHOSIS: SarIraparivfttiH and sim. comp.s. (??).
METAMORPHOSIS , s. rUpapariRAmaH, rUpAntaraM, dehAntaraM, AkArapariRAmaH, rUpavikAraH, rUpaBedaH, SarIravikAraH, pariRAmaH, vikAraH, vikftiH f.

Metaphor, s. rUpakaM, lakzaRA, AropaH, upa-cAraH. 2 dfzwAMtaH, nidarSanaM. [Metaphor]ic, [Metaphor]ical, a. OpacArika-lAkzaRika (kI f.), sarUpaka, Aropita; ‘m(etaphorical) use’ upacAraH. [Metaphor]ically, adv. lakzaRayA, upacAreRa, sAropaM; ‘to use m(etaphorically)’ upacar 1 P; See Figuratively.
METAPHOR: rUpakam, Kav. x. 7.

METAPHOR , s. rUpakaM, vyaYjanaM -nA, vyaYjakaH, lakzaRA, upalakzaRaM, DvaniH m., samAsoktiH f., AropaH, upamA, upamitiH f., dfzwAntaH, utprekzA, nidarSanaM, jahallakzaRA, jahatsvArTA, rUpakAlaNkAraH, upacAraH, upakzepaH.

METAPHORIC , METAPHORICAL, a. lAkzaRikaH -kI -kaM, upalakzitaH -tA -taM, sarUpakaH -kA -kaM, savyaYjakaH -kA -kaM, vyaYjakaH -kA -kaM, AropitaH [Page498-a+ 51] -tA -taM, DvanitaH -tA -taM, gORaH -RI -RaM, OpacArikaH -kI -kaM; ‘me- taphorical sense,’ gORatvaM.
METAPHORICAL: rUpaka- in comp.: v. Figu- -rative.
METAPHORICALLY: lakzaRayA (?): v. Figura- -tively.
METAPHORICALLY , adv. sarUpakaM, savyaYjanaM, rUpakapUrvvaM, rUpakakrameRa, upala- kzaRapUrvvaM, upalakzaRatas, lAkzaRikaM, DvanitaM.
METAPHRASE , s. yaTASabdaM, BAzAntaraM, yaTASabdaBAzAntaraM.
METAPHRAST , s. yaTASabdaBAzAntarakarttA m. (rttf).

Metaphysic, [Metaphysic]al, a. AnvIkzika-ADyAtmika (kI f.), Atmavizaya, AtmajYAnapara. [Metaphysic]ally, adv. AtmavidyAnusAreRa. [Metaphysic]ian, s. AnvIkzikIjYaH. Metaphysics, s. A-nvIkzikI, Atma-aDyAtma-vidyA, Atmaviza-yakaM jYAnaM, AtmatatvavidyA-SAstraM.

METAPHYSIC , METAPHYSICAL, a. AnvIkzikaH -kI -kaM, AnvIkzikI- sambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), mAnasaDarmmavizayaH -yA -yaM, AtmavizayaH -yA -yaM, AnvIkzikIvizayaH -yA -yaM, AtmajYAnasambanDI &c., aDyAtmavidyA- sambanDI &c., mAnasaH -sI -saM, ADyAtmikaH -kI -kaM, nEyAyikaH -kA -kaM.

METAPHYSICALLY , adv. mAnasaDarmmAnusAreRa, AtmavidyAnurUpeRa.
METAPHYSICIAN , s. AnvIkzikIjYaH, mAnasaDarmmajYaH, mAnasavidyAjYaH, aDyAtma- vidyAjYaH, nEyAyikaH, arTatattvavettA m. (ttf).
METAPHYSICS: AnvIkzikI; samayavidyA (rare), D. ii.

METAPHYSICS , s. AnvIkzikI, AnvIkzikI vidyA, mAnasaDarmmavizayakA vidyA, mAnasaDarmmaH, AtmavizayakaM jYAnaM, AtmaDarmmavizayakA vidyA, amUrtta- vizayajYAnaM, AtmavidyA, aDyAtmavidyA, mAnasavidyA, AtmatattvavidyA, AtmatattvaSAstraM, arTatattvaSAstraM, arTatattvavidyA, AtmatattvavicAraH.
Metastasis, s. rogasTalAMtaraM.
METASTASIS , s. rogasTAnAntaraM, rogasTalAntaraM.
METATARSAL , a. prapadInaH -nA -naM, prapadIyaH -yA -yaM, prapadasambanDI &c.
Metatarsus, s. prapadaM.
METATARSUS , s. prapadaM, pAdasya maDyaBAgaH.
Metathesis, s. akzara-varRa-viparyAsaH-vyatyAsaH-vyatyayaH.
METATHESIS , s. akzaraviparyyayaH, varRavyatyayaH, akzaraparivarttanaM.

METE (v.): mApayati (c. of mA): v. To measure.
To METE , v. a. mA (c. 2. mAti -tuM, c. 10. mApayati -yituM), parimA, mApanaM kf.
METED , p. p. mitaH -tA -taM, sammitaH -tA -taM, parimitaH &c., nirmmitaH &c.

METEOR: ulkA, fall of m.: ulkApAtaH.
METEOR , s. ulkA, KolkA -lkaH, agnyutpAtaH, ketutArA, SiKAvajjyotis n., agnireKAkAri gagaRAtpatajjyotis, upAhitaH, upagrahaH, utpAtaH, divyotpAtaH.
METEORIC: by comp. or circumlo, m. -stone: *ulkAsTaprastaraH.

METEOROLOGIC , METEOROLOGICAL, a. vidyudulkAdivizayakaH -kA -kaM, AkA- SodBavavastusambanDI &c., divyudBavavizayasambanDI &c., AkASIyaH -yA -yaM.
METEOROLOGICAL: AkASIyaH (yA, yaM) (??); or by comp.
METEOROLOGY: *vAyuvidyA; naBovidyA.
METEOROLOGY , s. vidyudulkAdividyA, AkASodBavavastuvidyA, antarIkzajavi- zayavidyA, AkASavidyA, antarIkzavidyA, sAmAnyavAyuvizayakA vidyA, vAyucakraSAstraM.
METEOROUS , a. ulkAguRakaH -kA -kaM, ulkADarmmakaH -kA -kaM.
Meter, s. mApakaH.
METER , s. mApakaH, parimApakaH, mApanakarttA m. (rttf), mAnanirUpakaH.
METHEGLIN , s. (Kind of mead) maDu n., maDupAnIyaM, maDunIraM.
Methinks, v. imp. manye, tarkayAmi, SaMke; DruvaM.
METHINKS: manye; tarkayAmi, etc.: v. To think, fancy.
METHINKS , v. impers. manye, iti manye, iti tarkayAmi.

Method, s. rIti f., prakAraH, mArgaH, viDA, viDiH; padDati f.; See Manner. 2 vyavasTA, kramaH, anukramaH, paryAyaH, AnupUrvI-rvyaM, pari-pAwi-wI f., Avft f., paraMparA; vyavasTayA racanaM-nA, vyUhanaM, vinyAsaH, saMviDAnaM, krameRa sTApanaM, niyamaH. [Method]ical, a. vyavasTita, yaTA-krama, sakrama, anupUrva, sUtrita, yaTAparyAya. 2 (Of persons) kramAnusArin, kramAnugata, krama-niyama-SIla. [Method]ically, adv. yaTAkramaM, anupUrvaSaH, AnupUrvyeRa, krameRa, kramaSaH, paryA-yeRa, anukrameRa, yaTAniyamaM. [Method]icalness, s. vyavasTA, kramaSIlatA, &c. [Method]ism, s. niyama-nizWA. [Method]ist, s. niyama-karma-nizWaH. [Method]ize, v. t. vyavasTA c. (sTApayati), krameRa sTA c. or vi-DA 3 U or virac 10 or vinyas 4 U.
METHOD: (1) praRAlI;(2) rItiH: v. Way, manner.

METHOD , s. (Regular arrangement) kramaH, anukramaH, paryyAyaH, vyava- sTA, vyavasTApanaM, krameRa sTApanaM, AnupUrvaM -rvyaM, AnupUrvI, paripAwiH -wI f., pAripAwyaM, paramparA, pAramparyyaM, vinyAsaH, vyUhanaM, vyUQiH f., prati- viDAnaM, viDAnaM, saMviDAnaM, racanA, viracanaM -nA, Avft f. — (Way, mode, process) rItiH f., mArgaH, viDiH m., viDAnaM, viDaH, prakAraH, kramaH, niyamaH, sUtraM, ftiH f., rUpaM, yuktiH f., padDatiH f., nyAyaH, maryyAdA, vfttAntaH, kxptiH f., kriyA, DArA; ‘in this method,’ anena viDAnena, anena prakAreRa, anayA rItyA, anayartyA. See MANNER.
METHODICAL: (1) praRAlIsaNgataH (tA, taM) (?); (2) rItyanugataH (tA, taM) (?).

METHODICAL , a. (Said of persons) niyamaSIlaH -lA -laM, kramaSIlaH -lA -laM, yaTAkramakArI -riRI -ri (n), kramAnugataH -tA -taM, kramAnu- [Page498-b+ 51] kArI &c., kramakaH -kA -kaM, kramikaH &c. — (Of things) kramikaH -kA -kaM, kramakaH -kA -kaM, yaTAkramaH -mA -maM, sakramaH -mA -maM, yaTAnukramaH -mA -maM, kramAnusArI &c., vyavasTitaH -tA -taM, sUtritaH -tA -taM, yaTAparyyAyaH -yA -yaM, anupUrvvaH -rvvA -rvvaM, anukrAntaH -ntA -ntaM; ‘methodical pro- ceeding,’ anukramaH -maRaM.
METHODICALLY: (1) supraRAlyA;(2) rItikrameRa.

METHODICALLY , adv. yaTAkramaM, anukrameRa, yaTAnukramaM, sakramaM, kramatas, kramaSas, krameRa, kramAt, paryyAyeRa, yaTAparyyAyaM, yaTAniyamaM, yaTAmArgaM, anu- pUrvvaSas, yaTAsUtraM, viDitas; ‘done methodically,’ anukrAntaH -ntA -ntaM.
METHODICALNESS , s. kramaSIlatA, kramikatvaM, vyavasTitiH f., sakramatA.
METHODISM , s. niyamanizWA, niyamAsaktiH f., karmmanizWA.
METHODIST: of a Christian sect: *rItiDvajaH (jA, jaM).
METHODIST , s. niyamanizWaH, niyamAsaktaH, niyamI m. (n), karmmanizWaH.
METHODISTICAL , a. niyamanizWASIlaH -lA -laM, niyamanizWAsambanDI &c.

To METHODIZE , v. a. vyavasTA in caus. (-sTApayati -yituM), vyavasTApanaM kf, krameRa or yaTAkramaM sTA, virac (c. 10. -racayati -yituM), viDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM), saMviDA, prativiDA, vinyas (c. 4. -asyati -asituM) vyUh (c. 1. -Uhate -hituM).
METHODIZED , p. p. vyavasTitaH -tA -taM, vyavasTApitaH -tA -taM, vinyastaH -stA -staM, prativihitaH -tA -taM, anukrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, paripAwIkftaH -tA -taM.
Meticulous, a. sASaMka. 2 atisAvaDAna, atyavahita.
METONYMICAL , a. ajahallAkzaRikaH -kI -kaM, ajahatsvArTalAkzaRikaH -kI -kaM.
METONYMY: lakzaRA, Kav.
METONYMY , s. ajahatsvArTA, ajahallakzaRA, BaktiH f.
METOPE: *mitopaH; vivftiH.
Metre, s. CaMdas n., vfttaM. Metrical, a. CaMdobadDa, vfttAtmaka, CAMdasa (sI f.), CaMdo-rUpa, padyarUpa, padyAtmaka.
METRE: (1) Candas (n.), sung in various m.s: CandoBirviviDErgotam, G. ;(2) vfttam, in this canto the m. is mostly upajAtiH asmin sarge prAyeRa vfttamupa- jAtiH, M. n.

METRE , s. Candas n., CandaH, vfttaM, varRavfttaM, gaRavfttaM, mAtraCandas, padyaM, vaktraM, vedaH; ‘violation of metre,’ CandoBaNgaH. The following are certain forms of metre explained in Wilson's Dictionary: 1. anuzwup f. (B) or SlokaH, of which varieties are citrapadA, mARavakaH, vidyutmAlA, pramARikA, 2. trizwup f., varieties indravajrA, upendravajrA, upajAtiH f., raTodDatA, 3. jagatI, varieties vaMSasTavilaM, drutavilambitaM, BujaNgaprayAtaM, 4. atijagatI, varieties maYjuBAziRI, praharziRI, puzpitAgrA, 5. SarkkarI or SakkarI, varieties vasantatilakaH, aparAjitA, vAsantI, lolA, nAndImuKaM, 6. atiSarkkarI or atiSakkarI, varieties mAlinI or mAninI, citrA, tURakaM, lIlAKelaH, 7. azwI, varieties cakitA, paYcacAmaraM, madanalalitaM, vARiH f., pravaralalitaM, 8. atyazwI, varieties SiKariRI, mandAkrAntA, hariRI, BArAkrAntA, pfTvI- BaraH, 9. DftiH f. varieties nArAcaH, nandanaM, SArdUlalalitaH, kusumi- talatA, citraleKA, 10. atiDftiH f. of which varieties are SArda- lavikrIqitaH, meGavisPUrjitaM, surasA, PulladAma n. (n), 11. kftiH f., va- rieties suvadanA, gItikA, SoBA, 12. prakftiH, varieties sragDarA, sarasI, 13. AkftiH f., varieties haMsI, madirA, 14. vikftiH f., 15. saNkftiH f., 16. atikftiH f., variety kroYcapadA, 17. utkftiH f., variety BujaNgavijfmbitaM, 18. daRqakaH, varieties jImUtaH, lIlA, SaNkaH, vyAlaH, pracitaM, 19. pratizWA, varieties kanyA, satI, 20. supratizWA, varieties paMktiH f., priyA, 21. maDyA or maDyamA, varieties nArI, mfgI, 22. ukTA, 23. atyukTA, 24. vfhatI, varieties BujaNgaSiSuH m., BujaNgasaNgatA, maRimaDyaM, 25. paMktiH f., varieties rukmavatI, manoramA, tvaritagatiH f., 26. uzRik f. (h), varieties maDumatI, kumAralalitA, 27. gAyatrI, varieties tanumaDyA, SaSivadanA, this and the pre- ceding are found only in the Vedas. There is another class of metres regulated, not by the number of syllables, but by the number of syllabic instants or short syllables, each long syllable being supposed to contain two short. They are called, 1. AryyA, varieties paTyA, vipulA, capalA, muKacapalA, jaGanacapalA, gItiH f., upagItiH f., udgItiH f., AryyAgItiH f., [Page499-a+ 51] 2. vEtAlIyaH, varieties OpaCandasikaH, dohaqikA.
METRICAL: expr. by the above words: m. composition is poetry: CandobadDapadaM padyam, Sah.; what is not m. is prose: vfttabanDojBitaM gadyam, Sah.

METRICAL , a. CAndasaH -sI -saM, CandoyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, CandovAn -vatI -vat (t), CandobadDaH -dDA -dDaM, CandorUpaH -pA -paM, CandoviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, padyarUpaH -pA -paM, padyAtmakaH -kA -kaM, svarabadDaH &c., tAlabadDaH &c.
METRICALLY: vfttabanDena.
Metronome, s. tAlamApanI.

METROPOLITAN (adj.): (1) pOraH (rI, raM);(2) rAjaDAnI in comp.
