Middle, s. maDyaM, maDyaBAgaH-deSaH-sTAnaM-sTalaM; aByaMtaraM, garBaH, aMtaraM, in comp.; ‘in the m(iddle) of the ocean’ maDyesamudraM; ‘in the m(iddle) of the house’ gfhAByaMtare, gfhagarBe; ‘going in the m(iddle)’ maDyaga. a. maDya, maDyama, maDyasTa, maDyavartin, maDyasTita; ‘the m(iddle) classes’ maDyamajAtIyAH, maDyamavarRAH; ‘m(iddle)-aged’ maDyamavayaska, gatayOvana; ‘m(iddle) finger’ maDyamA, karRikA; ‘m(iddle) man’ maDyasTaH, maDyamapuruzaH. [Middl]ing, a. maDya, maDyama, maDyaparimARa. 2 maDyamapadasTa, maDyamaguRa, sAmAnya, sADAraRa (RI f.). Midst, s. maDyaM; See Middle; ‘in the m(idst)’ maDye; ‘from their m(idst)’ tezAM maDyAt; ‘in the m(idst) of this talk’ evaM vadanneva; ‘in the m(idst) of calamities’ vipadgrasta- a.; duHKamagna- a.
MID (adj.): maDyaH (DyA, DyaM): v. Middle.
MID , a. maDyaH -DyA -DyaM, maDyamaH -mA -maM, maDyasTaH -sTA -sTaM. See MIDDLE.
MID-AGE , s. maDyavayas n., maDyamavayas n., AyurmaDyaM.
MID-COURSE , s. ardDamArgaH, ardDapaTaH, mArgArdDaM, mArgamaDyaM.
MID-DAY (subs.): (1) maDyAhnaH: v. Noon.

MID-DAY , s. maDyAhnaH, dinamaDyaM, divAmaDyaM, maDyandinaM, uddinaM; ‘at mid- day,’ dinamaDye, maDyAhne.
MID-DAY , a. mADyAhnikaH -kI -kaM, mADyandinaH -nI -naM; ‘mid-day rites,’ mADyAhnikI kriyA; ‘mid-day meal,’ maDyAhnaBojanaM.
MID-HEAVEN , s. KamaDyaM, gagaRamaDyaM, antarIkzamaDyaM, daSamalagnaM.
Midden, s. avakaranikaraH.

MIDDLE (adj.): (1) maDyaH (DyA, DyaM), the m. men leave off, beset with obstacles: viGnanihatA viramanti maDyAH, Mu.;(2) maDyamaH (mA, maM), following a m. course: puraskftamaDyamakramaH, R. ; the m. world (i. e. the earth): maDyamalokaH, Vi.; (3) maDyasTaH (sTA, sTaM) (= on the m.);(4) maDyamIyaH (yA, yaM) (rare). The m. age: *maDya- yugam or maDyakAlaH.

MIDDLE (subs.): (1) maDyam, the m. of the sky: vyomamaDyam, V. ; in the m. of the ocean: maDye- samudram, Si.; in the m. of the army: sEnyasya maDye, K. ; making the m. (= waist) slender: maDyaM tanUkftya, N. vii. 81.;(2) maDyaBAgaH, and there in the m.: tatra ca maDyamAge, K.

MIDDLE , a. maDyaH -DyA -DyaM, maDyamaH -mA -maM, maDyamIyaH -yA -yaM, maDyasTaH -sTA -sTaM, maDyasTitaH -tA -taM, maDyavarttI -rttinI -rtti (n), mADyaH -DyA -DyaM, mADyamaH -mI -maM, garBasTaH &c., garBasTitaH -tA -taM; ‘middle state,’ maDyasTatA, mADyasTyaM; ‘the middle classes,’ maDyamavarRAH m. pl., maDyavarRajAH m. pl., maDyajAtIyAH m. pl.

MIDDLE , s. maDyaM, maDyaBAgaH, maDyadeSaH, maDyasTAnaM, maDyasTalaM, maDyamapradeSaH, aByantaraM, antaraM, garBaH, hfdayaM; ‘the middle of the arm,’ dormaDyaM; ‘of the night,’ rAtrimaDyaM; ‘of a house,’ gfhAByantaraM; ‘of a bow,’ [Page499-b+ 51] lastakaH; ‘going in the middle,’ maDyagaH -gA -gaM, maDyacArI -riRI -ri (n); ‘in the middle,’ maDye, maDyatas; ‘in the middle of the night,’ rAtrimaDye, mahAniSAyAM; ‘in the middle of the Ganges,’ maDyegaNgaM.
MIDDLE-AGE: maDyaM vayas or maDyavayas (n.) or vayomaDyam; m., decay and death: vayomaDyaM jarA mftyuH, B. p.

MIDDLE-AGED , a. maDyamavayaskaH -skA -skaM, maDyavayaskaH &c., ardDavayaskaH &c., gatayOvanaH -nA -naM, atikrAntayOvanaH -nA -naM, ardDavfdDaH -dDA -dDaM; ‘a middle-aged widow,’ kAtyAyanI.
MIDDLE-EARTH , s. maDyalokaH, maDyamalokaH, maDyaBuvanaM, pfTivI.
MIDDLE-FINGER , s. maDyamA, maDyA, karRikA, jyezWaH.
MIDDLE-MAN , s. maDyasTajanaH, maDyavarttI m. (n), maDyasTitaH.
MIDDLE-SIZED , a. maDyamaparimARaH -RA -RaM, na sTUlo na sUkzmaH &c.

MIDGE: maSakaH (= gnat, mosquito).

MIDRIFF: i. e. diaphragm: udaravakzaHpeSI (?).

MIDSEA , s. samudramaDyaM, sAgaramaDyaM, maDyasamudraH.

MIGHTINESS , s. prabalatA, prAbalyaM, sAmarTyaM, ESvaryyaM, sabalatvaM, atiSaktitA, pratApaH, praBAvaH, vIryyaM, sAratA, sapratApatA, balIyastvaM.

MIGNONETTE: suganDilatAviSezaH.

MIGRATE: (1) nirgacCati (gam, c. l (= go out: q. v.);(2) deSAntaraM, sTAnAntaraM, etc. gacCati: v. To go.

Milch-cow, s. kzIriRI, payasvatI, dugDavatI, pInoDnI.
MILCH: (1) dugDavatI;(2) kzIriRI;(3) payasvinI; (4) dogDrI, Mah. v. 35. 13. M.-cow: DenuH.
MILCH-COW , s. DenuH f., dogDrI, DenukA, goDenuH f., strIgavI, payasvinI, kzIriRI, dugDavatI, pInoDnI, pIvarastanI, pItadugDA, navasUtikA; ‘a herd,’ DEnukaM.

MILD: mfdu (f. dvI), was neither harsh nor very m.: na Karo na ca BUyasA mfduH. R. viii. 9.: m. things: mfdu vastu; m. air: mfdupavanaH, V. ; m. speech: mfdvI vAk, N. iii. 60.; m. action: mfdukriyA, Sr.: v. Also soft, gentle.

MILD , a. (Soft, not harsh) mfduH -dvI -du, mfdulaH -lA -laM, komalaH -lA -laM, sOmyaH -myA -myaM, snigDaH -gDA -gDaM, SAntaH -ntA -ntaM, anugraH -grA -graM, aparuzaH -zA -zaM, apraKaraH -rA -raM, akarkaSaH -SA -SaM, SlakzRaH -kzRA -kzRaM, masfRaH -RA -RaM, sukumAraH -rA -raM, acaRqaH -RqA -RqaM, aKaraH -rA -raM. — (Tender or gentle in temper) mfdusvaBAvaH -vA -vaM, mfduBAvaH -vA -vaM, komalasvaBAvaH &c., sOmyavfttiH -ttiH -tti, komalAntaHkaraRaH -RA -RaM, dayArdraBAvaH -vA -vaM, dayAluH -luH -lu, dayAvAn -vatI -vat (t), sadayaH -yA -yaM, sAntvikaH -kA -kaM, sAntvikaprakftiH -tiH -ti, nirgarvaH -rvA -rvaM. — (Lenient) kzamAvAn &c., sAmabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, atIkzRaH -kzRA -kzRaM, atIvraH -vrA -vraM, anizWuraH -rA -raM, anugradaRqaH -RqA -RqaM, sAmopacArI -riRI &c., sAmopAyI &c.; ‘mild remedy,’ sOmyopa- cAraH, sAmopacAraH, bAlopacAraH; ‘mild means,’ sAmopAyaH; ‘by mild means,’ sAmopAyena, sAmnA; ‘mild air,’ mfduvAtaH, mfduvAyuH m.; ‘mild speech,’ sAntvavAdaH.
MILDEW: (subs.): prob.: Catrakam; Sve tarajas (n.).
MILDEW (v.): I Trans.: CatrakitaM (f. tAM) karoti.II Intrans.: *CatrakitaH (tA, taM) Bavati.
MILDEW , s. vfkzadUzaRaM, tarudUzaRaM, kalaNkaH, SuklakalaNkaH, SvetakalaNkaH, dUzaRa- vastu n., kledajamalaM.
To MILDEW , v. a. SuklakalaNkena duz (c. 10. dUzayati -yituM), kledajamalena duz or kalaNka (nom. kalaNkayati -yituM) or lip (c. 6. limpati, leptuM).
MILDEWED , p. p. SuklakalaNkadUzitaH -tA -taM, kalaNkitaH -tA -taM.
MILDLY: mfdu: v. Gently, softly.
MILDLY , adv. mfdu, mfdulaM, komalaM, sOmyavat, anugraM, aparuzaM, akarkaSaM, sAmnA, sAmopAyena, mArdavena, samArdavaM, atIkzRaM, atIvraM, acaRqaM, apraKaraM, mandaM.
MILDNESS: (1) mfdutA;(2) mArdavam;(3) mradiman (m.): v. Also gentleness, softness.

MILDNESS , s. (Softness, not harshness) mfdutA -tvaM, mArdavaM, mradimA m. (n), sOmyatA, komalatA, snigDatA, anugratA, aparuzatA, akArkaSyaM, SAntatA, SAntiH f. — (Of temper) svaBAvamfdutA, prakftimfdutA, sOmya- vfttitA, komalasvaBAvaH, sAntvikaprakftiH f., dayAlutA. — (Leniency) mfdutA, kzamA, sOmyatA, sAma n. (n), sAmabudDiH f., atIkzRatA, atEkzRyaM, atIvratA, daRqAnugratA, anugratA, anugradaRqatvaM, kfpA.
Mile, s. arDakoSaH; ‘3 m(ile)s’ sArDakoSaH; ‘4 m(ile)s’ kroSadvayaM.
MILE: ardDakroSaH (kroSaH = 4000 cubits).

MILE , s. The measure called kroSaH, or kos, is about two En- glish miles. One English mile will therefore be ex- pressed by ardDakroSaH; ‘three miles,’ sArdDakroSaH; ‘four miles,’ kroSadvayaM; ‘five miles,’ sArdDadvikroSaM; ‘six miles,’ kroSatrayaM.
MILE-POST: *ardDakroSaPalakaH (after sImAvfkzaH of m.).
MILE-STONE , s. ardDakroSamApakaprastaraH, kroSamApanapAzARaH.
MILEAGE: to draw m.: *kroSAnusAreRa BramaRavyayaM nizkarzati.
MILFOIL: sahasrapatraH (?); latAviSezaH.
Militant, a. yudDapravftta, raRodyata, yudDodyukta.
MILITANT: yudDe pravfttaH (ttA, ttaM) and sim. expr.s: v. War.
MILITANT , a. yudDodyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, yudDodyataH -tA -taM, yudDapravfttaH -ttA -ttaM, yudDArUQaH -QA -QaM, yuDyamAnaH -nA -naM, yudDakArI -riRI -ri (n), saNgrA- modyuktaH &c.

Military, a. sAMgrAmika-sAmarika-AyuDika (kI f.), kzAtra (trI f.), yudDa in comp. 2 yudDapravftta, yoDin, SastropajIvin, SastraBft, AyuDajIvin; ‘m(ilitary) preparation’ yudDa-sAmagrI; ‘m(ilitary) profession or life’ AyuDa-Sastra-vftti f., sEnikavfttiH, SastrAjIvaH; ‘m(ilitary) caste’ kzatriyajAtiH; ‘a man of the m(ilitary) class’ kzatraH-traM, kzatriyaH, rAjanyaH, virAw, bAhujaH, mUrDABiziktaH; ‘a woman of the m(ilitary) class’ kzatriyA-yARI; ‘m(ilitary) man’ yoDaH, vIraH, sEnikaH; ‘m(ilitary) duty’ kzAtraDarmaH, kzatriya-kzatra-DarmaH; ‘m(ilitary) science’ yudDaSAstraM, sAMgrAmikaM, SastrAstravidyA, AyuDa-raRa-vidyA. s. sEnyaM, sEnikavargaH, kzatragaRaH.

MILITARY (adj.): I Pertaining to war: yudDa-, etc. in comp.: v. War.II Belonging to a soldier: sEnika-, etc. in comp.: v. Soldier. Ph.: m. man: yoDaH or BawaH; a man of m. caste: kzatriyaH or (rarely) kzatram; m. duty: kzatraDarmaH.
MILITARY (subs.): expr. by pl. of soldiers, yoDAH, etc.

MILITARY , a. (Pertaining to soldiers or arms) yudDasambanDI -nDinI &c., yudDavizayakaH -kA -kaM, sANgrAmikaH -kI -kaM, sAmarikaH -kI -kaM, sEnikaH -kI -kaM, AyuDikaH -kI -kaM, kzAtraH -trI -traM, sAmparAyikaH -kI -kaM; ‘military duty,’ kzatraDarmmaH, kzAtraDarmmaH; ‘following it,’ kzatraDarmmAnugaH -gA -gaM; ‘military profession,’ SastravfttiH f., SastrA- straBfttvaM. — (Engaged in the profession of arms) yudDapravfttaH -ttA -ttaM, yoDI -DinI -Di (n), SastrajIvI &c., SastrAjIvI &c., Sastro- pajIvI &c., AyuDajIvI &c., SastrAstraBft, SastraBft. — (Man of the military class) kzatriyaH, kzatraH, kzatrI m. (n), rAjanyaH, virAw m. (j), bAhujaH, mUrdDABiziktaH; ‘a woman of this class,’ kzatriyA -yI -yARI; ‘the duty of this class,’ kzatriyaDarmmaH; ‘the military class,’ kzatriyajAtiH f.
MILITARY , s. (The body of soldiers) sEnikavargaH, sEnyavargaH, sEni- kajAtiH f., kzatraM, kzatriyajAtiH f., kzatravarRaH.
Militate, v. i. vi-prati-ruD 7 U, virudDa-pratikUla a. BU 1 P.
MILITATE: expr. with viroDin (f. nI) (= opposed).
To MILITATE , v. n. viruD (c. 7. -ruRadDi -rodDuM), pratiruD, virudDaH -dDA -dDaM BU, pratikUla (nom. pratikUlayati -yituM), viparItaH -tA -taM BU.
Militia, s. deSarakziRaH, rakzakayoDAH (pl.).
MILITIA: *rakzAbalam; sAmayikasEnyam.
MILITIA , s. deSarakzakAH m. pl., deSarakziRaH m. pl., nEmittikasEnyAH m. pl.

Milk, s. payas n., dugDaM, kzIraM, stanyaM; godugDaM, gorasaH, gavyaM (‘cowʼs m(ilk)’); ‘fresh m(ilk)’ pIyUzaH-zaM; ‘made of m(ilk)’ payasya; ‘coagulated m(ilk)’ daDi, kzIrajaM; ‘giving much m(ilk)’ bahudugDA; ‘m(ilk) livered’ kAtara, klIva-hfdaya, BIru; ‘m(ilk)-maid’ gopakanyA, ABIrI, godohinI; gopI, gopikA; ‘m(ilk)-man’ dogDf m., dohakaH, gopaH, ABIraH, goDuk; ‘m(ilk)-pail, -pan’ dugDa or kzIra-pAtraM-BAMqaM-BAjanaM; dohanI; ‘m(ilk)-porridge’ kzEreyI; ‘m(ilk)-sop’ kApuruzaH, BIruH; ‘m(ilk)-woman’ gopI, ABIrI, dohinI. v. t. duh 2 U (with two acc.), dugDaM nizkfz 1 P or sru c. [Milk]er, s. dogDf m. dohakaH, duh m. [Milk]y, s. kzIrin, payasya, pAyasa (sI f.); (s.) in comp.; ‘m(ilky) ocean’ kzIra-dugDa-sAgaraH. 2 kzIropama, dugDatulya. 3 kzIrada, dugDaprada, bahudugDa; ‘m(ilky) way’ viyadgaMgA; See Galaxy. 4 BIru, kAtara, sAmya; See Mild.

MILK (subs.): (1) dugDam (best equiv.), buffalo- m.: mahizIdugDam or mAhizaM dugDam; camel's m.: uzwrIdugDam or OzwraM dugDam, Bha.:(2) kzIram (also of plant): doe's m.: mfgakzIram, S.k.; m. -yield- ing trees: kzIriRaH pAdapA, M. viii. 246.;(3) payas (n (rare), m. ing my m. in a vessel of leaves: dugvvA payaH patrapuwe madIyam, R.
MILK (v.): dogDi (duh, c. 2.), m. ed gems from the earth: DaritrIM ratnAni duduhuH, K.

MILK , s. dugDaM, kzIraM, payas n., stanyaM, godugDaM, gorasaH -saM, DenukAdugDaM, gavyaM, gavyapayas n., avadohaH, dohaH, UDasyaM, UDanyaM, dohajaM, dohApanayaH, pAyasaM, pIyUzaM, peyaM, somajaM; ‘made from milk,’ payasyaH -syA -syaM; ‘the skim of milk,’ dugDaPenaM; ‘yielding much milk,’ bahudugDA, dohIyAn -yasI -yaH (s); ‘milk diet,’ dugDAhAraH; ‘coagulated milk,’ daDi n., kzIrajaM; ‘inspissated milk,’ kzIravikftiH f.; ‘drinking milk,’ kzIrapaH -pA -paM, kzIrapAyI -yinI &c.; ‘giving milk,’ kzIradaH -dA -daM; ‘to give milk,’ duh (c. 4. duhyate), kzIraM dA.

To MILK , v. a. duh (c. 2. dogDi, dugDe, dogDuM), nirduh, dohanaM kf, dugDaM sru (c. 10. srAvayati -yituM), gostanaM pIqayitvA dugDaM sru or mokz (c. 10. mokza- yati -yituM) or muc (c. 10. mocayati -yituM), dugDamokzaRaM kf.
MILK-LIVERED , a. BIruhfdayaH -yA -yaM, klIvahfdayaH &c., kAtaraH -rA -raM.
MILK-MAID , s. godogDrI, godohinI, gopI, gopinI, gopikA, ABIrI.
MILK-MAN , s. goDuk m. (-duh), dogDA m. (gDf), dugDavikretA m. (tf), kzIravikrayI m. (n), gopaH, ABIraH.
MILK-PAIL , MILK-PAN, s. dohanaM -nI, godohanI, dugDaBARqaM, kzIraBARqaM, dugDapAtraM, dugDaBAjanaM, dohanapAtraM, daDiBARqaM, nipAnaM, dohaH, pArI.
MILK-PORRIDGE , MILK-POTTAGE, s. kzEreyI.
MILK-SOP , s. klIvahfdayaH, mfduhfdayaH, komalahfdayaH, kApuruzaH.
MILK-WHITE: dugDaDavalaH (lA, laM) and sim. comp.s.
MILK-WHITE , a. dugDasavarRaH -rRA -rRaM, kzIravacCuklaH -klA -klaM, kzIravarRaH &c.
MILKED , p. p. dugDaH -gDA -gDaM, nirdugDaH -gDA -gDaM, kftadohanaH -nA -naM; ‘a cow easily milked,’ suKadohyA, suKasandohyA, suvratA.
MILKER: (1) dogDf (f. gDrI);(2) dohakaH (f. hikA);(3) dohin (f. nI).
MILKER , s. dogDA m. (gDf), dohakaH, dohI m. (n), Duk m. (duh).
MILKINESS: expr. with dugDavat (= like milk): v. Also softness.
MILKINESS , s. dugDatA, dugDavattA, dugDitA, kzIritA, pAyasatA, payasyatvaM, sakzIratA, sadugDatA, dugDasAdfSyaM, dugDasaguRatA.
MILKING (subs.): dohaH, -nam. M. pail: (1) dohana- pAtram;(2) dohinI;(3) dohaH (rare).
MILKMAID: (1) gopI;(2) gopikA;(3) gopinI.
MILKWOMAN , s. dugDavikretrI, dohinI, gopinI, gopA, ABIrI, mahASUdrI.

MILKY: I Yielding milk: v. Milch.II Relating to or made of m.: expr. by comp.: m. cake: dugDakUpA, Bha.III Soft, mild: q. v. Ph.: m. juice: kzIram; m. trees: kzIriRo mahIruhAH, Mah. s. 86. 15.; m. way: (1) mandAkinI;(2) svarnadI;(3) AkASagaNgA.

MILKY , a. dugDI -gDinI -gDi (n), kzIrI -riRI &c., pAyasaH -sI -saM, payasyaH -syA -syaM, payasvI -svinI &c., dugDamayaH -yI -yaM, kzEryaH -ryI -ryaM. — (Resembling milk) dugDasaguRaH -RA -RaM, kzIropamaH -mA -maM, dugDasadfSaH -SI -SaM. — (Yielding milk) kzIradaH -dA -daM, bahudugDaH -gDA -gDaM, dugDapradaH -dA -daM.
MILKY-WAY , s. mandAkinI, AkASagaNgA, svargaNgA, svarnadI, suranadI, AkASanadI, devanadI, viyadgaNgA, nAgavITI, haritAlI.
Mill, s. cakraM, pezaRI, pezaRayaMtraM-cakraM. v. t. piz 7 P, cUrR 10. 2 muzwinA taq 10 or prahf 1 P. [Mill]er, s. pezakaH, pezaRopajIvin m.
MILL (subs.): cakram; oil m.: lEcakram; cotton m.: *kArpAsacakram.
MILL (v.): I To grind: q. v.: cUrRIkaroti. II To cut fine grooves: *danturIkaroti.III To beat: nizpinazwi (piz, c. 7.).
MILL , s. pezaRaM, pezaRI -RiH f., pezaRayantraM, pezaRacakraM, cakraM.
To MILL , v. a. piz (c. 7. pinazwi, pezwuM), cUrR (c. 10. cUrRayati -yituM), cUrRIkf. — (Beat with the fist) muzwyA taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM) or prahf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM).
MILL-DAM: *cakrabanDaH; cakracAlanopayogI banDaH.
MILL-RACE: *cakrapayaHsrotas (n.) and sim. comp.s.
MILL-STONE: (1) pezaRI(RiH);(2) SilApawwaH.
MILL-STONE , s. pezaRaprastaraH, pezaRapAzARaH, pezaRI -RiH f., pezaRaM, SilApawwaH, SilAputraH.
MILLED (adj.): as a coin: danturitaH (tA, taM) (?).
MILLENARIAN: *sahasravarzavAdin (f. nI); kfzwasya sahasravarzADipatyavAdin (f. nI).

MILLENARIAN , MILLENARIAL, a. sahasravarzIyaH -yA -yaM, sahasravarzIRaH -RA -RaM, sahasravatsarI -riRI -ri (n), sahasravArzikaH -kI -kaM, sahasrAbdikaH -kI -kaM, sahasrI -sriRI &c., sAhasraH -srI -sraM.
MILLENIUM , MILLENARY, s. sahasravarzaM, sahasravatsaraM, varzasahasrakaM, varzasAhasraM, daSaSatavarzaM, sahasravarzaparyyantaM sAkzAdBUtaM svrIzwarAjyaM.
MILLENNIAL: sahasravarzIyaH (yA, yaM) and sim. comp.s.: v. Year.
Millennium, Millenary, s. sahasravarzaM, sahasrasaMvatsaraM. Millennial, Millenarian, a. sahasravarzIya-Ra, sahasravArzika (kI f.).
MILLENNIUM: (1) sahasravarzam;(2) varzasahasram; etc.
MILLEPED , s. sahasrapAd m., sahasrapAdaviSizwaH kIwaBedaH.
MILLER: cAkrikaH (?); cakrAjIvaH (?).
MILLER , s. SasyapezakaH, DAnyapezaRajIvI m. (n), pezaRopajIvI m.
Millesimal, a. sahasratama (mI f.), sahasrAMSAtmaka
MILLESIMAL , a. (Thousandth) sahasratamaH -mI -maM. — (Consisting of a thousand parts) sahasrAMSarUpaH -pA -paM, sahasrAMSAtmakaH -kA -kaM.
Millet, s. aRuH, priyaMguH.
MILLET: kzudraDAnyam. Italian m.: priyaNguH; Indian m.: cInAkaH; little m.: SyAmAkaH; spiked m.: kaNguH; kodo m.: kodravaH, Bha.
MILLET , s. (Panicum, a sort of grain) aRuH m., priyaNguH m.; ‘field of it,’ aRavyaM.
MILLIARY , a. ardDakroSamApakaH -kA -kaM, kroSamApanaH -nI -naM.
Milliner, s. strIvastrakft, strIvasanakAriRI. [Mercer]y, s. strIparicCadaH-sajjA, strIvastrasAmagrI.
MILLINER: paricCadopajIvin (f. nI), and sim. expr. s.
MILLINER , s. strIparicCadakAriRI, strIparicCadavikretrI, strIvastravyApAriRI, strIvastrakaraRopajIvinI, strIvastrakft f.
MILLINERY: (1) paricCadaH;(2) vastram (= cloth: q. v.).
MILLINERY , s. strIparicCadaH, strIvastrasAmagrpaM, strIvastraSiraskAdi n., strIsajjA, strIlokaBftaM yatkiYcid vastrAdi.
Million, s. niyutaM, daSalakzaM; ‘ten m(illion)’ kowi f.; ‘hundred m(illion)’ arbudaH- [Million]ary, a. ni-yutIya. [Million]th, a. niyutatama (mI f.). Millionaire, s. kowISvaraH, lakzADISaH.
MILLION: niyutam or prayutam. Ten m. s: kowiH. By m. s: kowiSaH. M.-th: niyutatamaH (mI, maM) (rare).

MILLION , s. niyutaH -taM, prayutaH -taM, daSalakzaM; ‘ten million,’ kowiH f.; ‘one hundred million,’ arbudaH; ‘one thousand million,’ mahArbudaH, mahASaNKaH; ‘ten thousand million,’ padmaM; ‘one hundred thousand million,’ mahApadmaM m.; ‘million million,’ abjaM, svarbaM, nisvarbaM; ‘ten million million,’ mahAsvarbaM. According to Wil- son's Dictionary, svarbaM is equivalent to ten million million, according to the Mahrattī Dictionary to ten thousand million, and niKarbaM to a hundred thousand million: niyutaH is also used for one hundred thousand, and there seems to be much uncertainty in the use of some others of the above Sanskrit terms. The word kowiH is used generally for a large number, and hence the expression ‘by millions’ kowiSas
MILLIONAIRE: (1) kuveraH;(2) lakzapatiH;(3) lakzeSaH, J.
MILLIONAIRE , s. kowISvaraH, lakzADISaH, daSalakzasampannaH.
MILLIONARY , a. niyutasambanDI -nDinI &c., niyutIyaH -yA -yaM.
MILLIONTH , a. niyutatamaH -mI -maM, prayutatamaH -mI -maM.
MILT: I Spleen: q. v.: plIhan (m.).II Roe: q. v.
MILT , s. (Spleen) plIhA m. (n), gulmaH. — (Roe) mInARqaM, matsyARqaM.
MILTER , s. puMmatsyaH, puMjAtIyo matsyaH or mInaH.

Mime, s. nawaH, nartakaH, kuSIlavaH, cAraRaH, raMgAjIvaH. 2 BaMqaH, vidUzakaH, vEhAsikaH. Mimic, ([Mimic]al), a. anukaraRa-SIla-svaBAva, anukArin, viqaMbanakArin. 2 viqaMbana-anu-karaRa-rUpa. s. BaMqaH, vEhAsikaH, vidUzakaH. 2 anukArin m. v. t. (upahAsapUrvaM) anukf 8 U, viqaMb 10. [Mimic]ker, s. anukArin m., viqaMbanakft. [Mimic]ry, s. sopahAsaM anukaraRaM or viqaMbanaM; anukAraH, viqaMbanaM.
MIME: I A farce: perh. BARaH.II A player: BaRqaH; kuSIlavaH.
MIME , s. (Actor, buffoon) nawaH, narttakaH, nAwakaH, kuSIlavaH, cAraRaH, raNgAjIvaH, jAyAjIvaH, BaRqaH, vidUzakaH, vEhAsikaH.
MIMIC (adj.): I Imitative: q. v.:II Imi- -tated: anukftaH (tA, taM), better by circumlo. III Ludicrous: q. v.
MIMIC (subs.): BaRqaH: v. Buffoon.
MIMIC (v.): viqambayati: v. To mock, imitate.

MIMIC , MIMICAL, a. upahAsabudDyA paragaticezwitAdyanukArI -riRI -ri (n) or anukaraRaSIlaH -lA -laM, anukArI &c., anukaraRasvaBAvaH -vA -vaM, [Page501-b+ 51] viqambanakArI &c. — (Consisting of imitation) anukaraRarUpaH -pA -paM, anukaraRAtmakaH -kA -kaM, viqambanarUpaH -pA -paM; ‘mimic art,’ nAwakaviDiH m.
MIMIC , s. (Buffoon) BaRqaH, BARqaH, vEhAsikaH, parihAsavedI m. (n), vidUzakaH. — (Imitator) anukArI m. (n), anukarttA m. (rttf).
To MIMIC , MIMICK, v. a. upahAsabudDyA parasya gatiBAzitacezwitAdi anukf (c. 8. -karoti -kurute -karttuM), hAsotpAdanArTaM paracezwitAnukaraRaM kf or viqambanaM kf.
MIMICKED , p. p. upahAsabudDyA or hAsyotpAdanArTam anukftaH -tA -taM.
MIMICKER , s. anukarttA m. (rttf), anukArI m. (n), viqambanakft m.
MIMICRY: BARqam: v. Buffoonery.

MIMICRY , s. upahAsabudDyA gatiBAzitacezwitAdyanukAraH, hAsotpAdanArTaM cezwi- tAnukaraRaM, anukAraH, anukaraRaM, anukftiH f., anukriyA, anukarmma n. (n), viqambanaM -nA, vyAjaH; ‘of a cry or sound,’ rutavyAjaH.
Mimosa, s. namaskArI, gaMqakArI-lI, samaMgA, KadirA, lajjAluH.

MIMOSA , s. (Kind of sensitive plant) gaRqakArI, gaRqakAlI, samaNgA, namaskArI, KadirI, elAparRI, suvahA, lajjAluH m., mahABItA, lajakA- -rikA, sparSalajjA, rAsnA, yuktarasA; ‘fetid mimosa,’ arimedaH, viwKadiraH; ‘mimosa albida,’ SamI, SamIraH, saktuPalA, SivA.
MINACIOUS , MINATORY, a. BartsanakArI -riRI -ri (n), nirBartsanakft m. f. n., BartsanArTakaH -kA -kaM, BartsanamayaH -yI -yaM, BayapradarSakaH -kA -kaM, BayasUcakaH -kA -kaM.
Minaret, s. SiKaraM, SfMgaM, prAsAda-Bavana-SiKaraM.
MINARET: *dIpanam; BAsaSfNgam; mInArakam.
MINARET , s. SiKaraM, SfNgaM, prAsAdaSiKaraM, BavanaSiKaraM, prAsAdaSfNgaM.
Minatory, a. tarjaka, BayaMkara, BIzaRa.

Mince, v. t. KaMqaSaH-sUkzmalavaSaH-kft 6 P or Cid 7 P or KaMqa 10, SakalIkf 8 U; ‘do not m(ince) matters’ yaTAvfttaM sarvaM sAkalyena nivedaya, sarvaM saMpUrRaM prakASaya; ‘m(inc)ed meat’ CinnamAMsaM. v. i. lalitagatyA cal-r 1 P or gam 1 P, BinnagatyA gam. 2 BinnasvareRa vad 1 P. [Minc]ingly, adv. KaMqaSaH, lavaSaH; Binna-gatyA, BinnasvareRa.
MINCE (v.): sUkzmaKaRqaSaH Cinatti (Cid, c. 7.) (= to cut). Ph.: not to m. matters: spazwaM sampUrRaM prakASayati (?).

To MINCE , v. a. (Cut into small pieces) KaRqaM KaRqaM kf, KaRqaSaH kf or Cid (c. 7. Cinatti, CettuM), sUkzmaKaRqaSaH kf or vyavaCida, bahulavaSaH KaRq (c. 10. KaRqayati -yituM), SakalIkf, KaRqIkf. — (Cut off in speaking) avaCid, BinnasvareRa vad (c. 1. vadati -dituM).

To MINCE , v. n. (Walk with short steps or with affected delicacy) BinnagatyA or salAlityaM or salOlyaM cal (c. 1. calati -lituM), lalitagatyA or vilakzitagatyA car (c. 1. carati -rituM), savElakzyaM car. — (Speak affectedly) BinnasvareRa vad (c. 1. vadati -dituM), lalitasvareRa vad, vilakzitasvareRa vad, savElakzyaM vad.
MINCE-MEAT: viSakalitaM mAMsam; sUkzmaM KaRqIkftaM mAMsam.
MINCE-MEAT , MINCED MEAT, s. CinnamAMsaM, KaRqamAMsaM, KaRqIkftamAMsaM, vyavaCinnamAMsaM, vyaYjanAdinA saha sidDaM CinnamAMsaM.
MINCE-PIE , MINCED PIE, s. CinnamAMsavyaYjanAdigarBaH SazkulIviSezaH.
MINCED , p. p. vyavaCinnaH -nnA -nnaM, sUkzmaKaRqIkftaH -tA -taM, sUkzmaSakalIkftaH -tA -taM, CinnaBinnaH -nnA -nnaM, CinnaviCinnaH -nnA -nnaM, KaRqitaH -tA -taM.
MINCINGLY: Fig.: (1) asampUrRam;(2) KaRqitam; etc.
MINCINGLY , adv. KaRqaSas, lavaSas, BinnagatyA, BinnasvareRa, savElakzyaM.

Mind, s. manas n., mAnasaM, cittaM, cetas n., budDi f., mati f., DIH; prajYA, boDaH; See Intellect. 2 hfdayaM, hfd n., aMtaHkaraRaM, cittaM, manaH, cetaH, aMtaraM. 3 matiH, budDiH, mataM; kAmaH, icCA, vAMCA, ruci f., manoraTaH, vAsanA, BAvaH, IpsitaM, aBilAzaH. 4 aBi-prAyaH; uddeSaH, saMkalpaH, aBipretaM, matiH, budDiH, mataM. 5 smaraRaM, smfti f., smaraRaSakti f., anu-boDaH; ‘to give the m(ind) to’ BAvaM-mano-niviS c. or baMD 9 P or A-ni-DA 3 U, Asakta-nivizwa-citta a. BU; See under Set; ‘out of oneʼs m(ind)’ BrAMta-avyava-sTita-budDi (a.); ‘fixed in the m(ind)’ citta-nizWa; ‘of low m(ind)’ kfpaRa-nIca-budDi; ‘working of the m(ind)’ citta or mano-vyApAraH or vftti f., manaScezwA, cetovikAraH; ‘according to oneʼs m(ind)’ yaTAkAmaM, yaTezwaM, yaTe-psitaM, yaTAruci; ‘have a m(ind) to ask’ prazwumanAH-kAmaH; ‘to cross the m(ind)’ manasi ud-i 2 P or udBU 1 P, budDO saMjan 4 A; See Occur; ‘call to m(ind)’ smf 1 P, saM-anu-°, anuciMt 10; ‘put in m(ind)’ smf c., anu-ud-buD c.; ‘of one m(ind)’ ekacitta a.; ‘being of one m(ind)’ ekacittIBUya; ‘change of m(ind)’ budDi-mati-BedaH; ‘flashing across the m(ind)’ sPuraRaM, sahasA AvirBAvaH. v. t. man 4 A, gaR 10, Adf 6 A, ava-apa-Ikz 1 A, Aloc 10, avaDA 3 U, citte-manasi-kf 8 U, avaDf 10, mano dA 3 U. 2 sev 1 A, Baj 1 U, anu-zWA 1 P, anuruD 4 A, anuvi-DA 3 U. 3 rakz 1 P, pA c. (pAlayati); ‘never m(ind) the first question, answer the second’ AstAM-tizWatu-tAvat praTamaH praSnaH, dvitIyasya uttaraM dehi; ‘never m(ind)’ agurvarTametat; See Matter. [Mind]ed, a. pravftta, pravaRa, SIla, manas, manaska in comp.; ‘worldly-m(inded)’ saMsArAsaktacitta; DIramanaska, &c. [Mind]ful, a. sAvaDAna, avahita, jAgarUka, avahitacitta. 2 kftAdara, manyamAna, avekzaka. 3 avaDArayat, smarat, citte kurvat; ‘to be m(indful) of’ smf. [Mind]fully, adv. sAva-DAnaM, sAdaraM, avekzayA. [Mind]fulness, s. avaDAnaM, avekzA. [Mind]less, a. anavaDAna, pramatta, anavekzaka, nirapekza. 2 nazwasmfti-budDiM, budDi-hIna.

MIND (subs.): (1) manas (n.), m. whose action through the nine passages was prevented: mano navadvAranizidDavftti, Ku. iii. 50.; as his m. is entirely turned to you: etanmano yadBavadekavftti, N. iii. 105.; this person has a m. to ask you some- thing: ayaM janaH kiYcidBavatIM prazwumanAH, Ku. v. 40.; say now what is in your m.: vadedAnoM yatte manasi vartate, Mal. ii.; to cross the m.: manasi udeti, N.; to call to m.: manasi karoti; out of m.: SUnyamanaskaH (skA, skaM);(2) cittam (not used in the sense of memory), knowing of one's m.: cittajYAnam, D.; by all being of one m.: sarvErekacittIBUya, H. ;(3) cetaH (= 2), my unsteady m. is running behind: mama DAvati paScAda- saMsTitaM cetaH, Sa.; not little-m.ed: analpacetas (mfn.), Ki.;(4) hfdayam (= heart: q. v.); (5) antaHkaraRam (lit).
MIND (v.): Adriyate (df, c. 6.): v. To attend, care, look, remember. Never m. the rest: mA SezARi vilokaya.

MIND , s. (The understanding, intellect) manas n., mAnasaM, matiH f., budDiH f., DIH f., cittaM, cetas n., meDA, prajYA, AtmA m. (n), cetanA, boDaH, boDaSaktiH f., cit f., cicCaktiH f., jYAnaSaktiH f., upalabDiH f., SemuzI, turagaH, niguH m., aNgaM; ‘application of mind,’ manoyogaH, manoniveSaH, manaHpraveSaH; ‘to give the mind,’ nivizwacittaH -ttA -ttaM BU, AsaktacittaH -ttA -ttaM BU, mano niviS (c. 10. -veSayati -yituM); ‘exercise of mind,’ manovyApAraH; ‘out of one's mind,’ avyavasTitabudDiH -dDiH -dDi; ‘fixed in the mind,’ cittIkftaH -tA -taM; ‘of inferior mind,’ apakfzwacetanaH -nA -naM. — (Heart or seat of the affections) hfdayaM, hfd n., cittaM, cetas, antaHkaraRaM, anta- rAtmA m. (n), antaHprakftiH f., manas, antarBAvaH, BAvaH, antaraM, aByantaraM; ‘working of the mind, emotion,’ cittavfttiH f., vikAraH, mano- vikAraH, manovikftiH f.; ‘control of the mind,’ manodaRqaH, mano- nigrahaH; ‘peace of mind,’ nanaHSAntiH f. — (Opinion, thoughts) matiH f., budDiH f., mataM, manogataM, manas n., manoBAvaH, hfdgataM; ‘of [Page502-a+ 51] mind,’ ekacittaH -ttA -ttaM; ‘to be of one mind,’ ekacittIBU. ‘change of mind,’ budDiBedaH. — (Inclination, will, desire) manoraTaH, icCA, AkAMkzA, aBilAzaH, vAsanA, budDiH f., matiH f., kAmaH, aBimataM, IpsitaM, aBIpsitaM, izwaM; ‘according to one's mind,’ yaTABimataM, yaTezwaM, yaTepsitaM, manonukUlaH -lA -laM, ‘having a mind to see,’ drazwumanAH -nAH -naH (s), ‘having a mind to go,’ gantumanAH &c. — (Design, intention) budDiH f., matiH f., manas n., aBiprAyaH, aBipretaM, cikIrzitaM, saNkalpaH, uddeSaH. To have a mind matiM kf. — (Memory, remembrance) smaraRaM, smftiH f., anusmftiH f., saMsmftiH f., anucintA, anuboDaH, DyAnaM, ADyAnaM; ‘to call to mind,’ smf (c. 1. smarati, smarttuM), anusmf, saMsmf, anucint (c. 10. -cintayati -yituM), samanucint, anubuD (c. 4. -buDyate -bodDuM), ‘to put in mind,’ smf (c. 10. smAra- yati -yituM), buD (c. 10. boDayati -yituM), udbuD; ‘flashing across one's mind,’ sPuraRaM.

To MIND , v. a. (Attend to, heed) avaDA (c. 3. Datte -DAtuM), mano DA, avaDAnaM kf, sAvaDAnaH -nA -naM BU, avahitaH -tA -taM BU or as; ‘mind!’ sAvaDAno Bava. — (Regard) man (c. 4. manyate, mantuM), anuman, mananaM kf, apekz (c. 1. -Ikzate -kzituM), avekz, pratIkz, buD (c. 1. boDati, c. 4. buDyate, bodDuM), AbuD, Alok (c. 10. lokayati -yituM), Aloc (c. 10. -locayati -yituM), avekzaRaM kf. — (Obey) sev (c. 1. sevate -vituM), Sru in des. (SuSrUzate -zituM), anuzWA (c. 1. -tizWati -zWAtuM), anuvft (c. 1. -varttate -rttituM), anuviDA in pass. (-DIyate), anuvarttanaM kf. — (Take care of, look after) rakz (c. 1. rakzati -kzituM), pAl (c. 10. pAla- yati -yituM), anusanDA; ‘mind a family,’ tantr (c. 10. tantrayati -yituM).

MINDED , a. (Disposed) pravfttaH -ttA -ttaM, pravaRaH -RA -RaM, manAH -nAH -naH or manaskaH -skA -skaM in comp.; as, ‘minded to go,’ gamanamanAH &c., gantumanAH &c., gamanamanaskaH &c., See INCLINED. (In com- position) manAH &c., manaskaH &c., matiH &c., budDiH &c.; as, ‘high-minded,’ mahAmanAH &c., mahAmanaskaH &c., mahAmatiH -tiH -ti &c.
MINDFUL: (1) avahitaH (tA, taM);(2) Ahitamanas (mfn.): v. Attentive. Ph.: to be m. of: smarati (smf, c. l (= to remember: q. v.), R. xvii. 8.

MINDFUL , a. (Attentive, heedful) sAvaDAnaH -nA -naM, avahitaH -tA -taM, kftAvaDAnaH -nA -naM, avahitacetAH -tAH -taH (s), jAgaraH -rA -raM. — (Regarding with care) manyamAnaH -nA -naM, anumanyamAnaH -nA -naM, apekzakaH -kA -kaM, avekzakaH -kA -kaM. — (Bearing in mind) smaran -rantI -rat (t), smftimAn -matI -mat (t), anucintayan -yantI -yat (t); ‘to be mindful,’ smf (c. 1. smarati, smarttuM).
MINDFULLY , adv. sAvaDAnaM, avahitaM, avahitacetasA, smftipUrvvaM, avekzayA.
MINDFULNESS , s. avaDAnaM, sAvaDAnatA, avahitatA, avekzA -kzaRaM, apekzA.

MINDLESS , a. (Heedless) anavaDAnaH -nA -naM, anavahitaH -tA -taM, pramattaH -ttA -ttaM, nirapekzaH -kzA -kzaM. — (Forgetful) nazwasmftiH -tiH -ti, apasmftiH -tiH -ti. — (Stupid) nirbudDiH -dDiH -dDi, budDihInaH -nA -naM.

Mine, a. madIya, mAmakIna, mAmaka (mikA f.), mat in comp. s. AkaraH, Ka(KA)ni-nI f., utpattisTAnaM; ‘m(ine) for jewels’ maRiBUmi f., ratnAkaraH, (fig.) AkaraH, niDiH, rASiH. 2 saMDiH, suruMgA, KAnikaM, kulyA. v. t. Kan 1 P, A-ni-°, aDastAt Kan, UrvIM Bid 7 P or vi-dF 9 P, suruMgAM kf. [Min]er, s. KanakaH, KAtakaH, AKanikaH, Kanitf m. 2 suruMgAkAraH, sOruMgikaH. Mineral, s. DAtuH, KanijaM, AkarajaM vastu. a. DAtusaMbaMDin, DAtu in comp. 2 Kanija, Akaraja, AkarodBava. 3 DAtumaya (yI f.), DAturUpa. 4 DAtusaMsfzwa, DAtuDarmopeta. [Mineral]ogy, s. DAtuvidyA, DAtuparI-kzaRavidyA-SAstraM. [Mineral]ogist, s. DAtuvidyAjYaH.
MINE (adj.): (1) madIyaH (yA, yaM);(2) mAmakInaH (nA, naM) or mAmakaH (kI, kaM) (very rare).

MINE (subs.): I Lit.:(1) AkaraH (= any source), in a m. of rubies: Akare padmarAgARAm, H. ;(2) KaniH or KanI, KaniBiH suzuve ratnam, R.; (3) BUmiH, etc. (= earth), as he digs the place there is copper-m.; yAvattaM pradeSaM Kanati tAvattABramayI BUmiH, P. v. 3.II Fig.:(1) AkaraH, the m. of mercy: AkaraH karuRAyAH, C. iii.;(2) niDiH: v. Abode.III Military:(1) kulyA, over- charged m.: *aDicUrRakulyA;(2) suraNgaH, Nil.
MINE (v.): Kanati (Kan, c. l (in both senses): v. To dig.
MINE (subs.): Kanaka (in both senses), so with machines and m. s: sayantraKanakAstaTA, Mah. iii. 15. 5.
MINE , pron. a madIyaH -yA -yaM, asmadIyaH -yA -yaM, mama gen. c. (asmad), mAmakInaH -nA -naM, AtmIyaH -yA -yaM, mat in comp.; as, ‘mine own master, matpraBuH m.

MINE , s. (Excavation in the earth for any metals, &c.) AkaraH, KaniH -nI f., KAniH -nI m. f., KanyAkaraH, gaYjaH -YjA -YjaM, kulyA, yoniH m. f. — (For gold, &c.) kanakasTalI, kanakasTAnaM, kAYcana- kandaraH, suvarRAdiDAtUtpattisTAnaM, suvarRAdyutpattisTAnaM. — (For precious stones) KaniH -nI f., maRiBUmiH f., rAnotpattisTAnaM, maRisTalI, kuwWimaH -maM, gaYjaH -YjA -YjaM. — (For military purposes) sanDiH m., suruNgA, KAnikaM, kulyA, ranDraM. — (Metaphorically) as, ‘a mine of good qualities,’ guRAkaraH, guRaniDiH m., guRAspadaM.

To MINE , v. a. and n. (Excavate) Kan (c. 1. Kanati -nituM), AKan, niKan. — (Form a hole or subterraneous passage) suruNgAM kf, vivaraM kf, ranDraM kf, gUQaranDraM kf gUQamArgaM kf or utKan, gUQakulyAM kf, gUQakUpaM kf. — (Undermine) aDastAt Kan or gUQaKAtaM kf.
MINER , s. (Excavator) KanakaH, KanitA m. (tf), AKanikaH, KAtakaH, Kanan m. (t), KanikaraH. — (Military) suruNgAKanakaH, suruNgAkft m., sOruNgikaH.
MINERAL: DAtuH (= metal). M. product: AkarajaM dravyam, should appropriate all m. sub- stances: AkareByaH sarvamAdadyAt, V.s.; m. water: *DAtujalam.
MINERAL , s. DAtuH m., upaDAtuH m., Kanijavastu n., Akarajavastu n., KanijaM SilAjaM, AkarodBavadravyaM, AkarIyadravyaM.

MINERAL , a. (Pertaining to minerals) DAtu in comp.; as, ‘the mineral kingdom,’ DAtujAtiH f., DAtujAtaM. — (Produced in a mine) KanijaH -jA -jaM, AkarajaH -jA -jaM, AkarodBavaH -vA -vaM, AkarI -riRI -ri (n), AkarIyaH -yA -yaM, SilAjaH -jA -jaM. — (Con- sisting of minerals) DAtumayaH -yI -yaM, DAturUpaH -pA -paM, DAtumayaH -yI -yaM, SilAmayaH &c., aSmamayaH &c., dArzadaH -dI -daM. — (Impreg- nated with minerals) DAtusaMsfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, DAtusaMsargI -rgiRI &c., DAtuguRakaH -kA -kaM, DAtuguRopetaH -tA -taM, DAtuDarmmakaH -kA -kaM.
MINERALIST, MINERALOGIST: *DAtuvidyAviSAradaH (dA, daM) and sim. comp.s.
MINERALOGIST , s. DAtuvidyAjYaH, svanijavastuparIkzakaH, AkarIyadravyanirUpakaH, DAtuvettA m. (ttf), DAtuguRavAdI m. (n), kAranDamI m. (n).
MINERALOGY: *DAtuvidyA; AkaradravyavijYAnam, and sim. comp.s.
MINERALOGY , s. DAtuvidyA, DAtunirUpaRavidyA, DAtuparijYAnaM, Kanijavastu- parijYAnaM, AkarIyavastuparIkzA, DAtuguRavizayakA vidyA, DAtuguRavicAraH, pArTivAMSavizayakaM jYAnaM.

Mingle, v. t. miSr 10, vi-saM-vyA-°, saMyuj 7 U, 10, saMsfj 6 P, saMpfc 2 A, 7 P, saMkf 6 P, saMmil c., miSrIkf 8 U, ekIkf; utkaMWAsADAraRaM paritozamanuBavAmi (S. 4) ‘I experience pleasure m(ingl)ed with regret’. v. i. saMmil 6 P, miSrI-ekI-BU 1 P, saMkF-saMsfj- pass. [Mingl]ed, a. miSrita, saMpfkta, saMsfzwa, saM-, miSra, saMkIrRa. [Mingle]ment, s. saMmiSraRaM, saMsargaH.
MINGLE (v.): I Trans.:(1) miSrayati, vi-, saM-, (miSr, c. l.);(2) miSrIkarotiH v. To mix. II Intrans.: milati, saM-, (mil, c. 6.); EkyaM gacCati, Si. xvii. 3.

To MINGLE , v. a. miSr (c. 10. miSrayati -yituM), sammiSr, vimiSr, mi- SrIkf, sammiSrIkf, ekIkf, saMyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yoktuM, c. 10. yoja- yati -yituM), saMsfj (c. 6. -sfjati -srazwuM), saMsargaM kf, saNkF (c. 6. -kirati -karituM -rItuM), sampfc (c. 7. -pfRakti -parcituM), ekatra kf, vyatikaraM kf.
To MINGLE , v. n. miSrIBU, sammiSrIBU, mil (c. 6. milati, melituM), sammil, saNkF in pass. (-kIryyate), saMsfj in pass. (-sfjyate), saMsfzwIBU.

MINGLED , p. p. miSritaH -tA -taM, sammiSraH -SrA -SraM, miSraH -SrA -SraM, mi- SrIkftaH -tA -taM, saMsfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, militaH -tA -taM, saNkIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, sampfktaH -ktA -ktaM, vyAmiSraH -SrA -SraM.
MINGLEMENT , s. miSraRaM, sammiSraRaM, samparkaH, saMsargaH, saMyogaH, milanaM.
MINGLING (subs.): miSraRam: v. Mixture.
Miniature, a. sUkzmAkAra, sUkzma. s. Ex. by hrasva or sUkzma; ‘world in m(iniature)’ hrasva-mAnena viSvaM.
MINIATURE: expr. with: hrasva (f. svA) (= short) or sUkzma (f. kzmA) (= minute, fine).
MINIATURE , s. sUkzmAkAracitraM, laGvAkAracitraM, sUkzmacitraM.
MINIATURE , a. sUkzmaparimARaH -RA -RaM, sUkzmAkAraH -rA -raM.
Minikin, s. sUcikA. 2 Minion, q. v.
MINIKIN , a. atisUkzmaH -kzmA -kzmaM, atpalyaH -lyA -lyaM, aRukaH -kA -kaM.
Minim, s. biMdu m. [Minim]um, s. alpizWA-atyalpA-saMKyA.
MINIM: in music: ardDasvaraH (??); dIrDasvaraH, Wilson.
MINIM , a. (Note in music) dIrGasvaraH. — (Dwarf) hrasvamUrttiH.
MINIMUM: expr. with sarvAlpaH (lpA, lpaM) or laGizWa (f. zWA).
MINIMUM , s. kanizWasaMKyA, avarasaMKyA, alpizWaparimARaM, alpizWAMSaH.
MINIMUS , s. alpizWamUrttiH m., kanizWaH, hrasvatamamUrttiH m.
MINING (subs.): Kanikarman (n.) and sim. comp.s.
MINING , s. KananaM, KaniKananaM, AkaraKananaM, KAniKananaM, AKananaM.
Minion, s. vallaBaH, priyaH, nfpa-rAja-vallaBaH; See Favourite.
MINION: vallaBaH: v. Favourite.
MINION , s. vallaBaH, rAjavallaBaH, nfpavallaBaH, rAjalAlI m. (n).

Minister, s. sacivaH, maMtrin m., amAtyaH, prakftipuruzaH, DuryaH, DUrvahaH, DurIRaH, DuraMDaraH, mahAmAtraH, rAjasacivaH, rAjAmAtyaH. 2 niyo-gin m., niyuktaH, niyojyaH, karmakaraH, aDi-kftaH. 3 upADyAyaH, AcAryaH, purohitaH. 4 rAjadUtaH, rAjapratiniDiH; ‘prime m(inister)’ praDAna-muKya-maMtrI, praDAnasacivaH; ‘m(inister) of counsel’ DIsacivaH, amAtyaH; ‘m(inister) for ordinary affairs’ karmasacivaH. v. sev 1 A, pari-upa-car 1 P, upAs 2 A, upasTA 1 U, Sru desid. (SuSrUzate). 2 (upa-karaRadravyARi) parikxp c., saMBf 1 P, upa-pad c., upasTA c. (sTApayati). 3 (to) saM-pad 4 A; kxp 1 A; See Tend. MINUTE , s. (Sixtieth part of an hour) pazwiprARapAdAH m. pl., kzaRapAdaH, kzaRacaturTAMSaH, sArdDadvipalaM; ‘half a minute,’ triMSatprA- RapAdA. According to the Hindu reckoning a daRqaH or hour contains 24 minutes, and a palaM is equal to the 60th part of a daRqaH, therefore 2(1/2) palas are equal to a minute. A kzaRaH is equal to 30 kalA or 4 minutes. When, however, the word minute is used generally for a small portion of time it may be expressed by kzaRaH, palaM, vipalaM, truwiH f., nimizaH, nimezaH; as, ‘a minute's delay,’ kzaRakzepaH; ‘for a minute,’ kzaRaM -RAt -Rena; ‘in a minute,’ nimezamAtreRa; ‘a minute afterwards,’ kzaRAntaraM -re. — (In geometry, the sixtieth part of a degree) kalA. — (Note, memorandum) smaraRaleKaH, smaraRArTaliKitaM, leKaH, liKitaM, smaraRacihnaM.

(Failure) asidDiH f., vipattiH f., kAryyavipattiH f., asampattiH f., anupapattiH f., apratipattiH f., BaNgaH, akaraRiH f., asadgatiH f., durgatiH f., vEPalyaM, asatPalaM, aSuBaPalaM, aSuBagatiH f. — (Ill-conduct) kunItiH f., anItiH f., avinayaH, durvfttiH f., kucaryyA, durAcaraRaM, kucezwitaM. — (Bringing forth before the time) garBasrAvaH, garBapAtaH, garBapatanaM, garBasravaH, garBaprasravaRaM, garBacyutiH f., garBavisraMsanaM, garBasyandanaM, aprAptakAlagarBaniHsaraRaM, piRqapatanaM, sravaH, srAvaH. Misconceive, v. t. miTyA grah 9 U, anyaTA buD 1 P or upalaB 1 A or avagam 1 P. Misconception, s. miTyA-mati-budDi f., miTyA or anyaTA-grahaRaM or boDaH, viparItArTaboDaH, BramaH.

To MISCONCEIVE , v. a. or n. anyaTA or miTyA buD (c. 1. boDati -DituM) or grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM) or upalaB (c. 1. -laBate -labDuM) or avagam (c. 1. -gacCAtaM -gantuM), anyaTArTaM grah, viparItArTaM grah, viparI- taboDanaM kf, viparItArTagrahaRaM kf, arTaviparyyAsaM kf.

MISCONCEPTION , s. anyaTAgrahaRaM, miTyAgrahaRaM, miTyAmatiH f., miTyAbudDiH f., viparItagrahaH -haRaM, anyaTAboDaH, anyaTArTaboDaH, viparItaboDaH, viparI- tArTaboDaH, viparItArTagrahaRaM, BramaH, BrAntiH f., arTaviparyyAsaH.

Misconduct, v. t. asamyak nirvah c. or pra-RI 1 P or pravft c. 2 (Oneself) a-samyak Acar 1 P or vft 1 A. s. durRayaH, asamyaN nirvAhaH. 2 durAcAraH, duScezwitaM, kucaritaM, kucaryA, avinayaH, maryAdAtikramaH, kukftyaM.
MISCONDUCT (subs.): (1) duScaritam;(2) duSce- zwitam;(3) durnayaH: v. Also misdeed.
MISCONDUCT (v.): duScarati (car, c. l (?); duzwaM carati; na samyak vyavaharati (hf, c. l.).

MISCONDUCT , s. (Ill-behaviour) duScaritaM, durScezwitaM, kucezwitaM, kucaritaM, avinayaH, avinItatA, kucaryyA, kucaritaM, kucezwitaM, durRItaM, durRItiH f., durRayaH, durAcAraH, durAcaraRaM, asadAcAraH, asadAcaraRaM, kadAcAraH, kuvya- vahAraH, asadvyavahAraH, kukarmma n. (n), kukftyaM, vyaBicAraH, anyaTAcAraH, anyaTAcaraRaM, apacAraH, kuSIlatA, amaryyAdA, maryyAdAtikramaH. — (Ill- management) durRayaH -yanaM, durnivAhaH, asavivAhaH.

To MISCONDUCT , v. a. (Conduct badly) anyaTA or ayuktaM or duzwu or asamyag nirvaq (c. 10. -vAhayati -yituM) or praRI (c. 1. -Rayati -RetuM) or sampraRI or pravft (c. 10. -varttayati -yituM), durnirvAhaM kf, asannirvAhaM kf, durRayanaM kf. — (Misconduct one's self) ayuktaM or asamyak car (c. 1. carati -rituM) or Acar or vft (c. 1. varttate -rttituM), vyaBicAraM kf, maryyAdAtikramaM kf.
MISCONDUCTED , a. durvinItaH -tA -taM, duScaritaH -tA -taM. See MISBEHAVED.
Misconjecture, v. t. miTyA tark 10 or Uh 1 A. s. miTyAtarkaH, miTyAnumAnaM.
MISCONJECTURE , s. miTyAnumAnaM, anyaTAnumAnaM, miTyAvitarkaH.
To MISCONJECTURE , v. n. miTyA or anyaTA anumA (c. 2. -mAti -tuM) or tark (c. 10. tarkayati -yituM) or vitark, miTyAnumAnaM kf.
MISCONSTRUCTION: asaNgatavyAKyA; ayaTArTavyAKyA (?).

MISCONSTRUCTION , s. anyaTAgrahaRaM, miTyAgrahaRaM, viparItaboDanaM, miTyA- boDanaM, ayaTArTaboDanaM, anyaTAboDanaM, viparItagrahaRaM, viparItArTaboDaH, anyaTArTaboDaH, viparItArTakaraRaM, anyaTArTakaraRaM, miTyArTavyAKyA.
Misconstrue, v. t. miTyA-anyaTA-arTaM buD 1 P or grah 9 U, miTyA yuj 10 or arTaM vyAKyA 2 P. Misconstruction, s. anyaTArTaboDaH, viparIta-miTyA-grahaRaM-boDaH.
MISCONSTRUE: na samyak parigfhRAti (grah, c. 9.), etc.

To MISCONSTRUE , v. a. anyaTA or miTyA arTaM buD (c. 1. boDati -DituM) or grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM) or upalaB (c. 1. -laBate -labDuM), miTyA arTaM vyAKyA (c. 2. -KyAti -tuM), viparItArTaM grah, viparItaboDanaM kf, viparItArTagrahaRaM kf.
Miscreant, s. pApaH, KaMqitavfttaH, KalaH, narA-pasadaH, pApizWaH, durAtman m., durvfttaH, jAlmaH; See Villain. 2 nAstikaH, miTyAdfzwiH.
MISCREANT: (1) KaRqitavfttaH (ttA, ttaM);(2) pApA- cAraH (rA, raM); etc.
MISCREANT , a. (Infidel) nAstikaH. — (Vile wretch) pApIyAn m. (s), pApizWaH, pApaH, durjanaH, durAtmA m. (n), durvfttaH, jAlmaH, KalaH, narADamaH; ‘daring miscreant,’ sAhasikaH.
MISDATE (v.): *liKanadinaBramaM karoti.
Misdeed, s. duzkftaM, apakriyA, kukarman n. ku-kftyaMkriyA, duzkfti f., apacAraH, kucaritaM, pApaM.
MISDEED: (1) kukarman (n.), etc.;(2) akAryam; of all m.s: sarvezAmakAryARAm, Mah. s. 35. 36.: v. Also crime.
MISDEED , s. kukarmma n. (n), duzkftaM, duzkarmma n., apakarmma n., duzkftiH f., kukftyaM, akarmma n., kukriyA, pApakarmma n., duScaritaM, kucaritaM, kucezwitaM, apacAraH.
MISDEMEANOR , s. See MISCONDUCT, (Minor offence) upapAtakaM.
MISDEMEANOUR: duScaritam: v. Misconduct.
Misdirect, v. t. vimArgaM dfS c. or diS 6 P, vipaTaM diS. 2 ‘Address’ (wrongly), q. v. [Misdirect]ion, s. vimArgadarSanaM; miTyopadeSaH.
MISDIRECT: expr. by circumlo., he m.ed the letter to Jāhānābād in Gayā instead of to Jāhānābād in Burdwan: *patraM varDamAnAntargataM jAhAnAbAdamaprezya gayAyAM jAhAnAbAdaM nirdideSa.

To MISDIRECT , v. a. (Put in the wrong road) vimArgaM or viparI- tamArgaM dfS (c. 10. darSayati -yituM), vipaTaM pradfS, anyaTA mArgaM dfS or uddiS (c. 6. -diSati -dezwuM), viparItapaTaM pradiS, vimArgapradarSanaM kf. — (A letter) anyaTA patrasaMjYAM liK (c. 6. liKati, leKituM) or kf.
MISDIRECTION , s. vimArgapradarSanaM, viparItamArgadarSanaM, miTyoddeSaH.
Misdoer, s. pApaH, pApakarman m., pApakft m., kukarmA. Misdoing, s. Misdeed, q. v.
MISDOER , s. kukarmmakArI m. (n), kukarmmA m. (n), pApakArI m. (n), pApakarttA m. (rttf), pApakaraH, pApakft m., pApakarmmA m., asatkarmmA m., anyAyakArI m., anyaTAcArI m., mandacaritraH.
MISDOING , s. duzkftaM, kukarmma n. (n), pApaM, aparADaH. See MISDEED.
Misemploy, v. t. anyaTA vini-yuj 7 A, 10 or vyApf c. [Misemploy]ment, asadvyayaH, kuviniyogaH, apavyayaH.
To MISEMPLOY , v. a. kuprayogaM kf, kuviniyogaM kf, asatprayogaM kf, anyaTA or asamyak prayuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yoktuM, c. 10. -yojayati -yituM) or viniyuj.
MISEMPLOYED , p. p. kuprayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, kuviniyuktaH &c., asamyakprayuktaH &c.
MISEMPLOYMENT , s. kuprayogaH, kuviniyogaH, asatprayogaH, asamyakprayogaH, [Page506-a+ 51] anyaTAprayogaH, asadupayogaH, kuvyApAraH kuvyayaH, asadvyayaH.

Miser, s. kfpaRaH, kadaryaH, kzudraH, mitaMpacaH, kiM-pacAnaH, dfQa-badDa-muzwiH, adAnaSIlaH, dAna-SatruH-vimuKaH. [Miser]ly, a. kfpaRa, kadarya, kzudra, badDa-dfQa-muzwi, dAnavimuKa (KI f.), adAnaSIla, mitaMpaca, svalpavyayin, vyayavimuKa, anudAra.
MISER: (1) kfpaRaH, -janaH, H. ;(2) mitaMpacaH (cook- -ing little) (rare), H.

MISER , s. kfpaRaH, dfQamuzwiH m., gAQamuzwiH, dAnaSatruH m., dAnavimuKaH, dAnaparANmuKaH, adAnaSIlaH, atyAgaSIlaH, svalpavyayI m. (n), svalpa- dAtA m. (tf), adAtA m., mitampacaH, kimpacaH, kadaryyaH, matsarI m. (n), vyayaSaNkitaH, vyayaparANmuKaH, arTaparaH, DanalABaparaH.

sanskrit.slp1: sahante santApaM tadapi DaninAM dvAri kfpaRAH
sanskrit.word: सहन्ते सन्तापं तदपि धनिनां द्वारि कृपणाः
sanskrit.iast: sahante santāpaṃ tadapi dhanināṃ dvāri kṛpaṇāḥ

details.body: MISERABLE: (1) kfpaRa (f. RA) (= mean), yet m. (men) bear distress at the door of the rich: sahante santApaM tadapi DaninAM dvAri kfpaRAH, J.;(2) dInaH (nA, naM) (= wretched), very m. condition: sudInA daSA, Ku.;(3) duHKitaH (tA, taM) (= un- -happy), surely the poor fellow is m. like me: nUnamahamiva duHKitastapasvI, Mu. vi.

MISERABLE , a. (Very unhappy) atiduHKI -KinI -Ki (n), gAQaduH- KAnvitaH -tA -taM, atiduHKitaH -tA -taM, atikleSI -SinI &c., ati- kleSitaH &c., atiduHKArttaH -rttA -rttaM, atiSokArttaH -rttA -rttaM, nirAnandaH -ndA -ndaM, atidInaH -nA -naM, anirvfttaH -ttA -ttaM, anirveSaH -SA -SaM; ‘making one's self miserable,’ AtmadrohI &c. — (Very poor or mean) atikfpaRaH -RA -RaM, kfpaRaH -RA -RaM, kutsitaH -tA -taM, tucCaH -cCA -cCaM, garhyaH -rhyA -rhyaM, garhitaH -tA -taM. — (Unfortunate) ApadgrastaH -stA -staM, vipadgrastaH &c., vipannaH -nnA -nnaM, ApannaH -nnA -nnaM, duHKApannaH &c., durdaSAgrastaH &c., mandaBAgyaH -gyA -gyaM, durBAgyaH &c., dEvopahataH -tA -taM, ApatprAptaH -ptA -ptaM; ‘miserable wretch,’ tapaKI m. (n).
MISERABLENESS: (1) kArpaRyam;(2) kadaryatA;(3) lubDatA (= covetousness).
MISERABLENESS , s. atiduHKitA, atidInatA, kfpaRatA, atikArpaRyaM.
MISERABLY: (1) kArpaRyena;(2) dInam: v. Meanly, wretchedly.
MISERABLY , adv. kfpaRaM, atikfpaRaM, atikArpaRyena, atiduHKitavat.
MISERLY: (1) kfpaRa (f. RA);(2) kadarya (f. ryA): v. Also mean.

MISERLY , a. kfpaRaH -RA -RaM, kadaryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM, dAnavimuKaH -KA -KaM, dAna- parANmuKaH &c., dfQamuzwiH -zwiH -zwi, gAQamuzwiH -zwiH -zwi, adAnaSIlaH -lA -laM, KalyavyayI -yinI -yi (n), vyayaparANmuKaH -KA -KaM, vyayaSaNkitaH -tA -taM, mitampacaH -cA -caM, kimpacaH -cA -caM, kimpacAnaH -nA -naM, atyAgaSIlaH -lA -laM, adAtA -trI -tf (tf), anudAraH -rA -raM, matsarI -riRI &c., arTaparaH -rA -raM, DanalABaparaH -rA -raM, kzudraH -drA -draM, kIkawaH -wI -waM.

Misery, s. duHKaM, vipad-Apad f., vyasanaM, dEnyaM, niHsvatA, vipatti f., durgati f., durdaSA, kfcCraM, anizwaM, kazwaM, anarTaH. 2 ati-duHKaM, gAQaSokaH, dEnyaM, anirvfti f., kleSaH, ativyaTA-bADA-vedanA, pari-saM-tApaH. Miserable, a. duHKita, duHKAnvita, atiduHKArta, anirvfta, nirAnaMda, kazwaprAya, atikleSArta, vi-A-panna, Apad-vipad-grasta, durgata, maMdaBAgya, dEvopahata, durBAgya, duHKApanna, durdaSApanna; ‘a m(iserable) man’ tapasvin m., narahatakaH. 2 kfpaRa, dIna, tucCa, garhaRIya, garhya, kutsita, niMdya, ni-apa-kfzwa, aDama, kzudra; See Mean.

MISERY: (1) duHKam (gen. term = distress, trou- -ble), the same becomes the seed of the tree of m.: tadeza duHKavfkzasya bIjatvamupagacCati,V p.; even m.ies met in the Daṇḍakā: prAptAni duHKAnyapi daRqakAyAm, R. xiv. 25.;(2) dEnyam (the state), full of m. and thievishness: dEnyastEnyamayAH, N. xvii. 25.; (3) vyasanam (= calamity). fellow-disciple of m.: vyasanasabrahmacArin, Mu. vi.;(4) kArpaRyam (rare), D. iv.

MISERY , s. (Great unhappiness, distress) atiduHKaM, atiSayaduHKaM, duHKaM, kleSaH, atikleSaH, atiSayakleSaH, duHKAvasTA, duHKaduHKaM, gAQaduHKaM, SokaH, gAQaSokaH, dEnyaM, dInatA, atidInatA, viqambanaM -nA, anirvftiH f. — (Extreme pain) atibADA, ativyaTA, atiSayatApaH, paritApaH, santApaH, atikfcCraM, ativedanA. — (Calamity) duHKaM, vyasanaM, vipattiH f., Apad f., vipad f., durgatiH f., durdaSA, dOrgatyaM, duravasTA, apAyaH, anizwaM, arizwaM, nirftiH f., vyatikaraH.
Misfeasance, s. atikramaH, vikarman n.

Misfortune, s. maMdaBAgyaM, durdEvaM, durBAgyaM, durjAtaM. 2 anarTaH, anizwaM, vyasanaM, A-vi-pad f., kfcCraM, duHKaM, atyAhitaM, kazwaM, durgati-vipatti. f. apAyaH, anizwapAtaH; ‘m(isfortune)s never come single’ raMDropanipAtino'narTAH (S. 6), CidrezvanarTA bahulIBavaMti. 3 alakzmIH, nirfti f.
MISFORTUNE: (1) durBAgyam (both of ill-luck and of disasters);(2) durdEvam (rarely of disasters), this is my m.: mama durdEvametat, H. v.

MISFORTUNE , s. (Ill-fortune) durdEvaM, durBAgyaM, dOrBAgyaM, kuBAgyaM, durgatiH f., dOrgatyaM, aSuBaM, akuSalaM, aBadraM, amaNgalaM, duradfzwaM, durjAtaM, aSlIkaM, anayaH, anarTaH, AlakzaRyaM, nirvftiH f. — (Calamity, disaster) Apad f., vipad, vipattiH f., vyApad f., vyasanaM, anizwaM, anizwapAtaH, anizwApAtaH, apAyaH, durGawanA, utpAtaH, anayaH, duHKaM, kazwaM, durdaSA, duravasTA. — (Misfortune personified) alakzmIH f., avalakzmIH f., mahAmAyA; ‘fallen into misfortune,’ ApadaNgataH -tA -taM, vipadaNgataH -tA -taM, ApatprAptaH -ptA -ptaM, ApadgrastaH -stA -staM, anayaNgataH -tA -taM.

Misgive, v. t. Ex. by vi-A-SaMk 1 A, na prati-i or viSvas 2 P, vikxp 1 A, vep 1 A; See Doubt; ‘my mind m(isgive)s me’ udeti me manasi SaMkA, SaMkate-vepate me hfdayaM. [Misgiv]ing, s. SaMkA, A-vi-°, saMdehaH, saMSayaH, vikalpaH, apratyayaH, aviSvAsaH.
MISGIVE: my heart m.s me: udeti manasi SaNkA or anizwaM SaNkate me hfdayam.

To MISGIVE , v. a. (Used in English with heart and the reciprocal pronoun, and expressed in Sanskrit by) SaNk (c. 1. SaNkate -NkituM), ASaNk, viSaNk, udvij (c. 6. -vijate -jituM), vep (c. 1. vepate -pituM), pravep, na viSvas (c. 2. -Svasiti -tuM), na pratI (c. 2. pratyeti -tuM rt. i), sandehaM kf, saMSayaM kf, vikxp (c. 1. -kalpate lituM, c. 10. -kalpayati -yituM); ‘my heart misgives me,’ vepate me hfdayaM, udvijate me hfdayaM.
MISGIVING (subs.): SaNkA: v. Apprehension.
MISGIVING , s. SaNkA, ASaNkA, sandehaH, saMSayaH, vikalpaH, vikalyitaM, aviSvAsaH, apratyayaH, apratItiH f.; ‘having misgivings,’ sASaNkaH -NkA -NkaM, ASaNkAnvitaH -tA -taM, SaNkASIlaH -lA -laM.
Misgotten, a. anyAyArjita.
MISGOTTEN (adj.): anyAyopArjitaH (tA, taM) and sim. comp.s.
MISGOTTEN , a. anyAyopArjitaH -tA -taM, anyAyArjitaH &c., dfjinArjitaH &c.
Misgovern, v. t. asamyak SAs 2 P or pA c. (pAlayati) or IS 2 A. [Misgovern]ment, s. kuSAsanaM, asamyak pAlanaM.
MISGOVERN: na samyak SAsti (SAs, c. 2); better by subs.
To MISGOVERN , v. a. asamyak pAl (c. 10. pAlayati -yituM) or SAs (c. 2. SAsti -situM), asamyakpAlanaM kf, kuSAsanaM kf, asamyakSAsanaM kf, asatpAlanaM kf.
MISGOVERNED , p. p. asamyakpAlitaH -tA -taM, kuSAsitaH -tA -taM.
MISGOVERNMENT: (1) kuSAsanam;(2) duzwaSAsanam; etc.
MISGOVERNMENT , MISGOVERNANCE, s. asamyakpAlanaM, asamyakSAsanaM, kuSAsanaM, kuSAstiH f., asatpAlanaM, anyaTASAsanaM.
Misguide, v. t. apaTe pat c., vimArgeRa-kupaTena-nI 1 P or pravft c., vimArgaM dfS c. [Misguid]ed, a. unmArgapravftta, mArgaBrazwa, satpaTaBrazwa, kumaMtrita, durvinIta, apaTagAmin.
MISGUIDE: apaTe pAtayati (c. of pat) and sim. expr. s.
To MISGUIDE , v. a. vimArgeRa or unmArgeRa or kumArgeRa nI (c. 1. nayati, netuM), vimArgaM dfS (c. 10. darSayati -yituM) or uddiS (c. 6. -diSati -dezwuM), anyaTA nI.
MISGUIDED (adj.): vimArgaDAvitaH (tA, taM) and sim. comp.s.
MISGUIDED , a. asamyagupadizwaH -zwA -zwaM, kumantritaH -tA -taM, kuSikzitaH -tA -taM, durvinItaH &c., satpaTaBrazwaH -zwA -zwaM, sanmArgaBrazwaH &c., mArgapraBrazwaH &c.
MISHAP: durGawanA: v. Calamity.
MISHAP , s. vipad f., Apad f., vipattiH f., durgatiH f., dOrgatyaM, anizwapAtaH, anizwApAtaH, durGawanA, vyasanaM, durjAtaM. See MISFORTUNE.
To MISINFER , v. a. miTyA or anyaTA anumA (c. 2. -mAti -tuM), miTyAnumAnaM kf.
Misinform, v. t. anyaTA ni-vid c., miTyA kaT 10 or vi-jYA c. (jYApayati), mfzA buD c.
MISINFORM: na samyak nivadayati (c. of vid) etc.: v. To inform.
To MISINFORM , v. a. ayaTArTaM or anyaTA in caus. (jYApayati, jYapayati -yituM), miTyA or mfzA buD (c. 10. boDayati -yituM), asamyag arTaM KyA (c. 2. KyAti -tuM) or AKyA.
MISINFORMED , p. p. miTyAjYaptaH -ptA -ptaM, miTyAboDitaH &c., ayaTArTAjYaptaH &c.
MISINTERPRET: na yaTArTaM vyAKyAti (KyA, c. 2.) or vyAcapwe (cakz, c. 2.).

To MISINTERPRET , v. a. apaTArTaM or anyaTA vyAKyA (c. 2. -KyAti -tuM), anyaTArTaM vyAKyA. — (Understand in a wrong sense) anyaTA or miTyA arTaM buD (c. 1. boDati -DituM) or grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM), viparItArTaM grah, viparItArTaboDanaM kf.
MISINTERPRETATION: asaNgatA or ayaTArTA vyAKyA, etc.
MISINTERPRETATION , s. ayaTArTavyAKyAnaM, anyaTArTavyAKyAnaM, ayaTArTa- boDaH, miTyAboDanaM, viparItaboDanaM, anyaTAgrahaRaM.
MISINTERPRETED , p. p. anyaTAvyAKyAtaH -tA -taM, anyaTAboDitaH -tA -taM.
Misjudge, v. i. miTyA-anyaTA-vicar c.
To MISJUDGE , v. a. anyaTA or miTyA vicar (c. 10. -cArayati -yituM) or biBAvanaM kf.
MISJUDGEMENT , s. miTyAvicAraH, anyaTAvicAraH, kuvivecanA, kunizyattiH f.
MISLAID , p. p. sTAnaBrazwaH -zwA -zwaM, sTAnapraBrazwaH -zwA -zwaM, asTAnavarttI -rttinI rtti (n), asTAnaH -nA -naM, nazwaH -zwA -zwaM; ‘a thing mislaid,’ JaH, JaYJA.
Mislay, v. t. asTAne ni-DA 8 U or rakz 1 P, naS c.; See Lose.
MISLAY: the letter is m.id: *asTAte nihitaM patram.
To MISLAY , v. a. asTAnIkf, visTAnIkf, apasTAnIkf, asTAne kf or DA (c. 3. daDAti, DAtuM), asTAne Df (c. 1. Darati, DarttuM), naS (c. 10. nASayati -yituM).

Mislead, v. t. pra-tF c., vaMc 10; See Cheat; vimArgeRa-utpaTaM-nI 1 P or gam c. (gamayati), Bram c. (Bramayati), muh c., BramaM-BrAMtiM-utpad c., vimArgaM dfS c. or upadiS 6 P, anyaTA upadiS. [Mislead]ing, a. BramakArin, moha-BrAMti-janana (nI f.). Misled, a. vimArga or unmArgagAmin or pravftta, BrAMta, satpaTaBrazwa, kumArga-gAmin-pravftta, BrAMtabudDi.
MISLEAD: (1) apaTe pAtayati (c. of pat);(2) vaYcayate (vaYc, c. 10.): v. To deceive.

To MISLEAD , v. a. vimArgeRa or unmArgeRa nI (c. 1. nayati, netuM), vimArgaM or vipaTaM dfS (c. 10. darSayati -yituM) or uddiS (c. 6. diSati -dezwuM) or pradiS, anyaTA or ayaTArTam upadiS or nirdiS or AdiS or Sikz (c. 10. Miss, s. (As a prefixing title) ex. by BartfdArikA, kumArI. 2 BramaH, dozaH, aparADaH, BraMSaH. 3 hAni f., aBAvaH, virahaH, nASaH, lopaH; See Loss. v. i. moGI-viPalI-BU 1 P, na siD 4 P; ‘never-m(iss)ing arrow’ amoGaH bARaH. 2 Bram 1, 4 P, pra-mad 4 P, sKal 1 P. 3 cyu 1 A; See below. v. t. (with instr.); See Lose; ‘he m(iss)ed the mark in shooting’ sa lakzyacyutasAyakaH; nimittAdaparAdDezuH; ‘m(iss)ed his way’ mArgAd BrazwaH &c. 2 na prAp 5 P or vid 6 U or laB 1 A, (Get q. v.). 3 kzip 6 P, hA 3 P, tyaj 1 P, apAs 4 U, visfj 6 P; ‘you have m(iss)ed a splendid opportunity’ SoBanAvasarastvayA kziptaH, na gfhItaH, tyaktaH. 4 (Feel the absence of) aBAvaM jYA 9 U or vi-BU c., nyUna. a. man 4 A; utkaMW 1 A, uttam 4 P, utsukAyate (D.); ‘I m(iss) him very much’ tasya balavadutkaMWe, tasyAsanniDAnAt nitarAM duHKitosmi, taddarSa-nAya uttAmyAmi, tadvirahaviDuraH &c. Also anxious.VI To err: q. v.

(hIyate) with instr. or abl. c., BraMS with abl. c. See To LOSE.

Mistake, s. BramaH, BrAMti f., vyA-, mohaH, mati-BramaH, miTyA-mati f. -budDi f. 2 pramAdaH, dozaH, sKalitaM; ‘m(istake) in calling names’ gotra-sKalitaM. v. t. anyaTA-miTyA-grah 9 U or man 4 A or buD 1 P, miTyA jYA 9 U, BrAMtyA-saMdehena-man, saMdih 2 U; gen. ex. by budDiH, DIH in comp. or by s. (1); ‘why do you strike me, m(istak)ing me for Siva’ purArAtiBrAMtyA mAM kiM praharasi; vyAGraDiyA-budDyA tasmAt palAyaMte; PenapawalEH saMdehitatUlarASiBiH (Ka. 23); ‘which were m(istak)en for heaps of cotton’; ketakaSiKAsaMdigDamugDeMdavaH (Mal. 1) ‘the lovely moon being m(istak)en for a Ketaka point’. v. i. (Method, manner) rItiH f., mArgaH, viDiH m., viDAnaM, prakAraH, niyamaH, vfttiH f., ftiH f., kramaH, saMviDAnaM, paryyAyaH, maryyAdA, DArA, viDaH in comp.; ‘mode of living,’ vfttiH f.; ‘in this mode,’ anena viDAnena, eMvaviDaM -Dena, anena prakAreRa; ‘mode of speaking,’ vAgvyApAraH, vAgvfttiH f. — (Form) rUpaM, AkAraH, AkftiH f., [Page510-a+ 51] saMskAraH. — (Custom) AcAraH, vyavahAraH, pracAraH, rItiH f., niyamaH, aByAsaH, sTitiH f., AvfttiH f., sampradAyaH. — (Fashionable custom) saByalokavyavahAraH, saByarItiH f., SizwavyavahAraH, SizwamArgaH, saByasampradAyaH, lokAcAraH. — (In metaphysics) viSezavasturUpaM, viSezadravyarUpaM, viSe- zadravyaprakAraH. — (In grammar) vAcyaM. — (In music) rAgaH m., rAgiRI f., varRaH. The musical modes are personified as either male or female. The male are called Rāgas; the female are Rāginīs, and are considered to be the wives of the Rāgas. The following are some of the names for the male: BEravaH, mAlavaH, sAraNgaH, hindolaH, vasantaH, vasantadUtaH, paYcamaH, dIpakaH, meGaH, nawaH, nawanArAyaRaH, kalpARaH, kAmaboDaH, trowakaH, viBAsaH. The following are some of the Rāginīs, or fe- male personifications: dIpikA, nawI, trowakI, deSakArI, gOqI, jaNgalA, DaneSvarI, BEravI, rAmakarI or rAmakelI or rAmakalI, sEnDavI, pUrvvI, BUpAlI, maDumADavI.
