To MODULATE , v. a. kal (c. 10. kalayati -yituM), svaralayaM kf, kalatAM kf, svarAnukramaM kf, svarAnupUrvyaM kf. — (Inflect or vary sound) svaraBedaM kf, svaraviBedaM kf, svaraBaNgaM kf, svaraviBaNgaM kf, svaraparivarttanaM kf.
MODULATION: m. of voice: svarasaMkramaH, Mr. iii. 5.

MODULATION , s. kalatA, layaH, svaralayaH, kalanaM, svaraBedaH, svaraviBedaH, svaraBaNgaH, svaraviBaNgaH, svarAnukramaH. — (Transition from one key to another) SudDAntayuk f. (j), svaraparivarttanaM. — (Melody) susvarA- nukramaH, svaramADuryyaM, mADuryyaM, suSrAvyasvaraH, tAlaH.
MODULATOR , s. svaraBedakArI m. (n), svaraviBedakaH, layakArI m.
MOHAMMEDAN , a. yAvanaH -nI -naM, yavanadeSIyaH -yA -yaM, yavanaDarmmasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), yavanaDarmmAvalambI -mbinI &c.
Moiety, s. arDaH-rDaM, arDaBAgaH-aMSaH.
MOIETY: ardDam; ardDaBAgaH: v. Half.
MOIETY , s. ardDaM -rdDaH, ardDaBAgaH, ardDAMSaH; ‘of an estate,’ rikTAdDa.
Moil, v. t. Dirty, q. v. v. i. vrAtaM kf 8 U, dehAyAsena Sram 4 P.
To MOIL , v. a. (Make dirty) malina (nom. malinayati -yituM), malinIkf, malena duz (c. 10. dUzayati -yituM) or lip (c. 6. limpati, leptuM).
To MOIL , v. n. (Toil) atidehakleSena Ayas (c. 4. -yasyati -yasituM) or Sram (c. 4. SrAmyati, SramituM), atiSarIrAyAsaM kf, kazwaM kf.

Moist, a. Ardra, klinna, sarasa, unna, utta, sadrava, sikta, jalArdra, timita; ‘to be m(oist)’ klid 4 P, stim 4 P. [Moist]en, v. t. klid c., ArdrIkf 8 U, sic 6 P, uMd 7 P, ukz 1 P. [Moist]ening, s. kledanaM, ukzaRaM, uMdanaM. [Moist]ness, s. ArdratA, klinnatA, sarasatA. [Moist]ure, s. kledaH, temaH, stemaH, rasaH, sajalatA, ArdratA, klinnatA; oft. ex. by jalaM.
MOIST: (1) sarasaH (sA, saM);(2) klinna (f. nnA) (?);(3) Ardra (f. rdrA) (= wet).

MOIST , a. ArdraH -rdrA -draM, sArdraH -rdrAM -draM, IzadArdraH, &c., jalArdraH &c., klinnaH -nnA -nnaM, IzatklinnaH &c., siktaH -ktA -ktaM, IzatsiktaH &c., unnaH -nnA -nnaM, samunnaH &c., sarasaH -sA -saM, sadravaH -vA -vaM, rasayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, timitaH -tA -taM, stimitaH -tA -taM, vodaH -dA -daM; ‘to be moist,’ klid (c. 4. klidyati), tim or stim (c. 4. timyati or tImyati).
MOISTEN: (1) kledayati, saM-, pari-, (c. of klid) (?);(2) ArdrIkaroti (= to make wet).

To MOISTEN , v. a. klid (c. 10. kledayati -yituM), pariklid, Izat klid, ArdrIkf, IzadArdrIkf, sic (c. 6. siYcati, sektuM), Izat sic, jalena sic, ukz (c. 1. ukzati -kzituM), samukz, und (c. 7. unatti, undituM).

MOISTENED , p. p. klinnaH -nnA -nnaM, kleditaH -tA -taM, pariklinnaH &c., pari- kleditaH -tA -taM, ArdrIkftaH -tA -taM, siktaH -ktA -ktaM, jalasiktaH &c., ukzitaH -tA -taM, samukzitaH -tA -taM, unnaH -nnA -nnaM, samunnaH &c., uttaH -ttA -ttaM, timitaH -tA -taM, stimitaH -tA -taM.
MOISTENER , MOISTENING, s. or part. kledakaH -kA -kaM, kledanaH -nA -naM.
MOISTENING , s. kledanaM, secanaM, jalasecanaM, ukzaRaM, undanaM, samundanaM.
MOISTNESS , s. ArdratA, sArdratA, IzadArdratA, jalArdratA, klinnatA, IzatklinnatA, siktatA, jalasiktatA, unnatA, sarasatvaM.
MOISTURE: rasaH, m. of the lip: aDararasaH: v. Also wetness.
MOISTURE , s. kledaH -daM, saMkledaH, klinnatA, ArdratA, temaH, stemaH, temanaM, ciklidaM, rasaH, snehaH, undanaM, samundanaM; ‘of the lips,’ aDararasaH, aDaramaDu n., aDarAmftaM, muKasuraM.
Molar, s. daMzwrA, carvaRadaMtaH.
MOLAR: i. e. m teeth: carvaRadantAH (?).
MOLAR , a. (Tooth) dAQA, carvaRadantaH, mahAdantaH, daMzwrA.
Molasses, s. guqaH, ikzusAraH, mastyaMqI-qikA, PARitaM.
MOLASSES: guqaH, old m.: purARaguqaH, Bha.
MOLASSES , s. ikzusAraH, ikzurasakvATaH, maDuDUliH f., kzAraH, SarkarAkzAraH, rasikA, maDuraM, guqaH -qakaM, rasajaH, dravajaH, sitAdiH m., pARiH f.

Mole, s. tilakaH, jaqulaH, kAlakaH, pipluH. 2 vapraH-praM, setuH, cayaH, piMqalaH, Ali f. 3 CuCuM-darI, gaMDamuKI, dIrGatuMqI, divAMDikA; ‘m(ole) eyed’ sUkzmanayana, ‘m(ole)-hill’ valmIkaH-ka, vAmalUraH, kfmiSElaH, kUlakaH, syamIkaH; ‘he makes mountains of m(ole)-hills’ tile tAlaM paSyati.
MOLE: I A mark on the body: tilaH, -kaH. II An animal: *talpaH; bileSayo jantuBedaH. III A mound: q. v. vapram.

MOLE , s. (Spot on the body) tilaH -lakaH, tilakAlakaH, kiRaH, [Page511-b+ 51] sAmudraM, kAlakaH, jawulaH. — (Mound) vapraH -praM, piRqalaH, piRqanaH, setuH m., cayaH. — (The animal) CuCundaH, CucCundarI, garttASrayaH, vilavAsI jantuBedaH.
MOLE-EYED , a. sUkzmanayanaH -nA -naM, sUkzmadfzwiH -zwiH -zwi.
MOLE-HILL , s. kfmiSElaH, BUSravAH m. (s), valmIkaH -kaM, kUlakaH, vamrIkUwaM, mfttikAkUwaM, vAmalUraM, syamIkaH.
Molecule, s. aRuH, paramARuH, kaRaH.
MOLECULE: paramARuH: v. Particle.
MOLECULE , s. aRuH m., paramARuH, kaRaH, kaRikA, lavaH, kAkiRikA.
MOLECULISM , s. aRimA m. (n), aRutvaM.
MOLEHILL: (1) valmIka (mn.), born in a m.: valmIkamavaH, A. r.;(2) vAmalUraH. Ph.: to make mountains of m.s: tile tAlaM paSyati (comp. Bengali tilake tAla karA).
Moles, s. vyaMgaM.
Molest, v. t. bAD 1 A, ard 1 P or c., pIq 10, upadru 1 P, A-yas c., uparuD 7 U; See Harass. [Molest]ation, s. bADA, pIqA, upadravaH, AyAsaH, kleSaH. [Molest]er, s. utpIqakaH, bADakaH, AyAsakaH.
MOLEST: bADate (bAD, c. 1.): v. To harass, trouble.

To MOLEST , v. a. Ayas (c. 10. -yAsayati -yituM), bAD (c. 1. bADate -DituM), paribAD, prabAD, aDibAD, uparuD (c. 7. -ruRadDi -rodDuM), ruD, tap (c. 10. tApayati -yituM), santap, pIq (c. 10. pIqayati -yituM), upapIq, aBipIq, kliS (c. 9. kliSnAti, kleSituM), vyaT (c. 10. vyaTayati -yituM), ard (c. 10. ardayati -yituM).
MOLESTATION: (1) utpIqanam;(2) by verb: v. Annoyance.
MOLESTATION , s. kleSaH, bADaH -DA, bADanaM, uparoDaH, pIqA, vyaTA, duHKaM, AyAsaH, prayAsaH, upadravaH, upaplavaH; ‘free from molestation, nirupadravaH -vA -vaM.
MOLESTED , a. bADitaH -tA -taM, pIqitaH -tA -taM, klizwaH -zwA -zwaM, kleSitaH -tA -taM, pariklizwaH -zwA -zwaM, uparudDaH -dDA -dDaM, vyaTitaH -tA -taM, upadrutaH -tA -taM.
MOLESTER: (1) utpIqaka (f. qikA);(2) bADaka (f. DikA), pra-.
Mollient, a. mfdukArin, Samaka, SAMtida.
MOLLIENT , a. mfdukArI -riRI -ri (n), snigDakArI &c. See EMOLLIENT.
MOLLIFICATION , s. mfdUkaraRaM, snigDIkaraRaM, SamanaM, praSamanaM, upaSamanaM.
MOLLIFIED , p. p. mfdUkftaH -tA -taM, SamitaH -tA -taM, upaSAntaH -ntA -ntaM.
Mollify, v. t. Sam c. (Samayati), pra-upa-° sAMtv 10, mfdUkf 8 U, laGUkf.
MOLLIFY: Samayati (c. of Sam): v. To calm.
To MOLLIFY , v. a. mfdUkf, snigDIkf, komalIkf, Sam (c. 10. Samayati -yituM), praSam, upaSam, sAntv or SAntv (c. 10. sAntvayati -yituM), upasAntv, aBiSAntv.
MOLLUSCA , s. pl. komalaSarIraviSizwA prARijAtiH.
MOLLUSK: *kambuH, -jAtIyaH.
Molten, a. vilIna; See Liquid.
MOLTEN: I Melted: vilInaH (nA, naM), etc. II Made of melted metal: DAtumayaH (yI, yaM) and sim. comp.s.
MOLTEN , a. vilInaH -nA -naM, drutaDAtumayaH -yI -yaM, vilInaDAtumayaH &c.

Moment, s. kzaRaH, muhUrtaH, nimi(me)zaH, palaM; ‘pleasant for the m(oment)’ ApAtaramaRIya; ‘but for a m(oment)’ kzaRamAtraM; ‘this very m(oment)’ asminneva kzaRe; ‘the m(oment) he is here’ atra tasminnAgatamAtre or Agata eva; ‘for the present m(oment)’ ApAtataH; ‘in a m(oment)’ kzaRAt, kzaRena, nimezamAtrAt, ekapadaM; ‘auspicious m(oment)’ SuBamuhUrtaH, lagnaM; See Instant also. 2 gurutvaM, mahattvaM, praBAvaH, gOravaM, mahiman m.; See Importance; ‘of little m(oment)’ aguruka, akiMcitkara (rI f.), laGvarTa, kzudra. [Moment]ary, a. kzaRika, kzaRasTAyin, acira, asTAyin; kzaRa, nimeza in comp.; ‘m(omentary) flash’ acirapraBA, kzaRadyuti f.; ‘m(omentary) obstacle’ kzaRaviGnaH. [Moment]ous, a. guru, gurupraBAva, alaGu; See Important.

MOMENT: I Importance: q. v.: gurUtvam.II Of time:(1) muhUrta (mn.), for about a m.: muhUrtamiva, K. ; in a m.: muhUrtena, R. ; but for a m.: muhUrtamAtram, N. ; after a m.: muhUrtApagame, K. ; (2) kzaRaH in a m.: kzaRena, V. ; even for a m.: kzaRamapi, R. ; at this very m.: asminneva kzaRe, D. ; in the next m.: tasminneva kzaRAntare, D.

MOMENT , s. (Minute portion of time) kzaRaH, vipalaM, palaM, truwiH f., nimezaH, nimizaH, mAtrA; ‘the present moment,’ ApAtaH; ‘for the present moment,’ ApAtatas; ‘in a moment,’ kzaRAt kzaRena, nimezamAtreRa, kzaRamAtreRa, kzaRAntare, ekapade, ekavipale; ‘for a moment,’ kzaRaM -Rena, kzaRamAtraM, nimezamAtraM, muhUrttaM; ‘at that moment,’ tatkzaRAt -Re, tatkAle, tadAnImeva; ‘every moment,’ pratikzaRaM, anukzaRaM, kzaRe kzaRe; ‘the next moment,’ kzaRAntaraM; ‘auspicious moment,’ lagnaM. See INSTANT. (Importance) gurutA -tvaM, gOravaM, praBAvaH, BAraH.
MOMENTARILY: (1) anukzaRam;(2) pratikzaRam; (3) pratimuhUrtam.
MOMENTARILY , adv. kzaRe -RaM -RAt, tatkzaRe, pratikzaRaM, sadyas, sapadi, kzaRamAtraM, nimezamAtraM.
MOMENTARY: kzaRikaH (kA, kaM), m. pleasure: kzaRikA prItiH, H. : v. Transient, fleeting.

MOMENTARY , a. kzaRikaH -kA -kI -kaM, kzaRI -RinI -Ri (n), kzaRaBUtaH -tA -taM, kzaRamAtrasTAyI -yinI &c., kzaRasTAyI &c., atyalpakAlasTAyI &c., alpakAlInaH -nA -naM, atyalpakAlInaH -nA -naM, aciraH -rA -raM, acirasTAyI &c., sAdyaskaH -skI -skaM, nEmizaH -zI -zaM, nEmizikaH -kI -kaM, tatkzaRikaH -kI -kaM, tAtkAlikaH -kI -kaM, kzaRa in comp.; as, ‘a momentary obstacle,’ kzaRaviGnaH; ‘a momentary flash,’ kzaRapraBA.
MOMENTOUS: gurU (f. rvI): v. Important.
MOMENTOUS , a. guruH -rvI -ru, gurvarTaH -rTA -rTaM, bahvarTaH &c., mahArTaH &c. gurupraBAvaH -vA -vaM, alaGuH -GuH -Gu; ‘a momentous affair,’ gurukAryyaM. See IMPORTANT.
MOMENTOUSNESS: gurUtvam: v. Importance.
MOMENTOUSNESS , a. gurutA -tvaM, gOravaM, gurvarTatA, praBAvaH, alaGutA.
Momentum, s. javaH, vegaH, A-saM-vegaH.
MOMENTUM: javaH (= speed: q. v.).
MOMENTUM , s. vegaH, AvegaH, saMvegaH, ApAtaH, gativegaH.
MONACHAL , a. maWavAsasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n). See MONASTIC.
Monachism, s. maWavAsaH, saMsAratyAgaH, AraRyakavftti f.
MONACHISM: saMnyAsASramaH and sim. comp.s.: v. Anchorite.
MONACHISM , s. maWavAsaH, maWADyAsanaM, vanavAsaH, vAnaprasTAtA, araRyavAsaH, vEKAnasavfttiH f., saMsAratyAgaH, udAsInatA.
Monad, s. aBedya-acCedya-vastu n.
MONAD: paramARuH: v. Atom.
MONAD , MONADE, s. tanmAtraM, mAtraM, aRumAtraM, aBedyavastu n., acCedyavastu n., adfSyavastu n., aKaRqanIyavastu.

Monarch, s. rAjan m., ISaH, ISvaraH, patiH, aDipaH, aDISaH, svAmin m.; See Lord; ‘m(onarch) of the herd’ yUTapatiH-pAlaH. 2 aDI-SvaraH, nfpaH, nfpAlaH, BUpatiH, See King. [Monarch]al, [Monarch]ic, [Monarch]ical, a. rAjakIya, rAjayogya, rAja in comp. 2 ekapraBuka, ekarAjAyatta, samrAqa-DIna. [Monarch]y, s. ekarAjaSAsanaM, ekarAjataMtraM, ekarAjADipatyaM. 2 rAjyaM, vizayaH, rAzwraM.
MONARCH: (1) rAjan (f. rAjYI): v. King; (2) ISvaraH (f. rI): v. Lord.

MONARCH , a. rAjA m. (n), nfpatiH m., BUpatiH m., nfpaH, pArTivaH, BUpaH, narapatiH m., mahIpatiH m., aDipaH, aDipatiH m., mahArAjaH, aDirAjaH, ISvaraH, aDISvaraH; ‘universal monarch,’ samrAw m. (j), maRqale- SvaraH, cakravarttI m. (n). See KING.

MONARCHAL , MONARCHIC, MONARCHICAL, a. (Relating or suited to a monarch) rAjakIyaH -yA -yaM, rAjayogyaH -gyA -gyaM, rAjocitaH -tA -taM, ADirAjikaH -kI -kaM, rAja in comp. — (Vested in a single ruler) ekarAjADInaH -nA -naM, ekarAjAyattaH -ttA -ttaM, samrAqa- DInaH -nA -naM, ekarAjakaH -kA -kaM, ekapraBukaH -kA -kaM.
MONARCHICAL: I Royal: q. v.II Vested in a monarch: m. government: *rAjADInaM rAjyam; m. form of g.: *rAjatantram.
MONARCHY: I M.cal government:(1) rAjaSAsanam;(2) rAjatantram.II Kingdom: q. v.: rAjyam.
MONARCHY , s. ekarAjaSAsanaM, ekarAjADipatyaM, ekADipatyaM, ekarAjakatvaM, ekaBarttfkatvaM, ekasvAmitvaM, rAjatvaM, rAjyaM, nfpatvaM, narendratvaM.
Monastery, s. vihAraH, maWaH, ASramaH, muni-vAsaH, vAnaprasTASramaH. Monastic, [Monast]ical, a. vihArika, ASramika (kI f.), vEKAnasa (sI f.); ‘m(onastical) vow’ vEKAnasaM vrataM.
MONASTERY: (1) vihAraH, make him the chief of all m.ies: sarvavihArezu kulapatirayaM kriyatAm, Mr.; (2) maWaH, Ayatanam, etc. (when the sense is clear.), here in the m.: ihEvAyatane, D. ii.
MONASTERY , s. maWaH, ASramaH, vAnaprasTASramaH, munivAsaH, munivAsasTAnaM, DarmmaSAlA, puRyasTAnaM, puRyAlayaH, puRyavanaM.
MONASTIC, -AL: expr. by comp., m. life: *vihArajIvanam: v. Monastery, monk, ancho- -rite.
MONASTIC , MONASTICAL, a. maWavAsasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), ASrama- sambanDI &c., ASramI -miRI &c., ASramikaH -kI -kaM, munisambanDI &c
Monday, s. somavAraH-vAsaraH, iMduvAsaraH.
MONDAY: (1) somavAraH;(2) somavAsaraH and sim. comp.s.
MONDAY , s. somavAraH, candravAraH, induvAraH, somavAsaraH.
Monetary, a. dravyasaMbaMDin, mOdrika (kI f.).
MONETARY , a. mudrAsambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), mOdrikaH -kI -kaM.

sanskrit.slp1: Danena kiM yo na dadAti nmaSnute
sanskrit.word: धनेन किं यो न ददाति न्मश्नुते
sanskrit.iast: dhanena kiṃ yo na dadāti nmaśnute

details.body: Money, s. DanaM, arTaH, vittaM, dravyaM, viBavaH, vasu n.; See Wealth. 2 mudrA, nizkaH-zkaM, nARakaM, waMkakaH; ‘m(oney)-bag’ koSaH-zaH, mudrA-kozaH; ‘m(oney)-changer’ mudrAparivartakaH; ‘m(oney)-lender’ kusIdikaH, vArdDuzikaH, vfdDyA-jIvaH, vArdDuziH; uttamarRaH. [Money]ed, a. Danin, Danika, DanasaMpanna, DanAQya. [Money]less, a. Dana-hIna, nirDana, niHsva, gataviBava, parikzIRa; See Poor.

MONEY: (1) Danam, to make m.: DanaM karoti, H. ; to acquire much m.: mahadDanam upArjayati, D. ; if we are rich with m. dug in the middle of a house: gfhamaDyaniKAtena Danena Danino yadi, P. ; what is the use of m. who does not give, does not enjoy: Danena kiM yo na dadAti nmaSnute, H. ;(2) arTaH, loss of m.: arTanASaH, H. ; man is slave of m.: arTasya puruzo dAsaH, J. ;(3) vittam, buying his poverty with own m.: vittErnijEH krItvA dAridram, D. : v. Coin, wealth.

MONEY , s. (Coin) mudrA, dInAraH, nARakaM, waNkaH, waNkakaH, nizkaH -zkaM, kArzApaRaM. — (Riches, wealth) DanaM, arTaH, vittaM, dravyaM, viBavaH, vEBavaM, sampattiH f., rikTaM, DanasampattiH f., DanabAhulyaM, DanasamfdDiH f., DanavEpulyaM, ‘love of money,’ DanaloBaH, arTaloBaH, DanASA; ‘making money,’ DanArjanaM, dravyArjanaM.
MONEY-BAG: DanaBastrikA (after ratnaBastrikA of D. ii.).
MONEY-BAG , s. kozaH, koSaH, DanakozaH, mudrAkozaH.
MONEY-BOX , s. mudrABARqaM, mudrApAtraM, DanaBARqaM, dInAraBARqaM.
MONEY-CHANGER: *DanaparivartakaH; waNkavyApArin (m.).
MONEY-CHANGER , s. mudrAparivarttakaH, huRqikApatrasuvarRarUpyAdiparivarttakaH, DanavyApArI m. (n), mudrAvyApArI.
MONEY-LENDER: DanikaH: v. Usurer.
MONEY-LENDER , s. kusIdikaH, kusIdaH -dA -daM, kOsIdikaH, kusIdajIvI m. (n), vArDuzikaH, vfdDijIvI m., nizidDavfdDyupajIvI m. (n), kalopa- jIvI m., fRadAtA m. (tf), DanikaH, DanaprayogI m. (n).
MONEY-LESS , a. DanahInaH -nA -naM, aDanaH -nA -naM, nirDanaH -nA -naM, dravya- hInaH -nA -naM, arTahInaH &c., vittahInaH &c., kzIRaDanaH &c., gatArTaH -rTA -rTaM.
MONEY-ORDER: waNkaSAsanam; DanAjYApatram, to pay a m.: SAsananirdizwaM DanaM dadAti.
MONEYED: I Rich:(1) Danavat (f. tI);(2) Danin (f. nI,);(3) DanaSAlin (f. nI);(4) DanAQya (f. QyA).II Composed of money: “m. capital”: sAraDanam, D.
MONEYED , a. DanavAn -vatI -vat (t), DanI -ninI -ni (n), DanikaH -kA -kaM, saDanaH -nA -naM, DanAQyaH -QyA -QyaM, mahADanaH -nA -naM, dravyavAn &c., vittavAn &c.
MONEYLESS: (1) nirDanaH (nA, naM);(2) DanahInaH (nA, naM) and sim. comp.
MONEYWORT: latAviSezaH; *numalAriH.
Monger, s. vyApArin m., vyavahArin m. kraya-vikrayikaH, vaRij m.
MONGER , s. vyApArI m. (n), vyavasAyI m. (n), krayavikrayikaH, vikretA m. (tf), baRik m. (j).
Mongrel, a. saMkIrRa, saMkarajAtIya, saMkaraja.
MONGREL: saNkara- in comp.: v. Hybrid, mixed.
MONGREL , a. saNkIrRajAtIyaH -yA -yaM, saNkarajAtIyaH -yA -yaM, saNkarajAtaH -tA -taM, saNkarajaH -jA -jaM, vijAtIyaH -yA -yaM, saNkIrRaH -rRA -rRaM.
Monism, s. advEtavAdaH.
MONITION: SAsanam: v. Admonition.
MONITION , s. upadeSaH, pratyAdeSaH, praboDaH -DanaM, mantraRaM, boDaH -DanaM.
Monitor, s. SAsakaH, boDakaH, upadeSakaH, SikzakaH. 2 upaguruH. [Monitor]y, Monitive, a. praboDaka, upadeSaka, Sikzaka, upadeSarUpa.
MONITOR: I Lit.: SAsakaH.II In a school: SAsakaH (?).
MONITOR , s. (Warner, admonisher) mantA m. (ntf), aBimantA m., mantrI m. (n), boDakaH, praboDakaH, upadeSakaH, pratyAdeSakaH, SikzakaH. — (In a school) upaSikzakaH, upaguruH m.
MONITORIAL s. upaSikzakasambanDI -nDinI &c., upaSikzAsambanDI &c.
MONITORY , MONITIVE, a. upadeSakaH -kA -kaM, upadeSAtmakaH -kA -kaM, upadeSarUpaH -pA -paM, SikzakaH -kA -kaM, udboDakaH -kA -kaM, praboDakaH. &c.
Monk, s. yatiH, saMnyAsin m., muniH, yogin m., maWavAsin m., tapasvin m., vAnaprasTaH. [Monk]ish, a. munisaMbaMDin, yatisadfSa (SI f.).
MONK: no spe. equiv.: (1) brahmacArin (m.); (2) yatiH;(3) saMnyAsin (m.). Chief of m.s: kulapatiH, Mr.

MONK , s. maWavAsI m. (n), muniH m., sannyAsI m. (n), yogI m. (n), yatI m. (n), tapasvI m. (n), vEKAnasaH, udAsInaH, vErAgI m. (n), [Page512-b+ 51] vErAgikaH, vErAgyASramI m., vAnaprasTaH, saMsAratyAgI m., lokatyAgI m., sarvvasaNgaparityAgI m.
MONKERY: brahmacaryA, L.
Monkey, s. vAnaraH, kapiH, markawaH, plavaM(va)gaH, SAKAmfgaH, balImuKaH, kISaH, vanOkas m.; ‘m(onkey)-like’ kApeya (yI f.).
MONKEY: (1) vAnaraH;(2) kapiH;(3) markawaH; (4) plavaNgaH, -BaH.

MONKEY , s. vAnaraH, kapiH m., plavagaH, plavaNgaH -NgamaH, markawaH, SAKAmfgaH, vfkzacaraH, JampI m. (n), JampAkaH, JampAruH m., vanOkAH m. (s), balimuKaH, balImuKaH, kalipriyaH, kISaH, hanumAn m. (t), rAmadUtaH; ‘Female monkey,’ vAnarI f., markawI; ‘monkey-like,’ kApeyaH -yI -yaM; ‘monkey-tricks,’ vAnaracezwA, markawacezwA. — (Iron weight) lohaBAraH.
MONKISH , a. munisambanDI -nDinI &c., munisadfSaH -SI -SaM.
MONK'S-HOOD: i. e. aconite: vatsanABaH.
Monochord, s. ekataMtrIvAdyaM.
MONOCHORD , s. ekatantrI m. (n), ekatArI m. (n), ekatantrIvAdyaM.
Monochromatic, a. ekavarRa-raMga.
Monochronic, a. samakAlIna, vartamAna.
Monocrat, s. aDISvaraH, anAyattaSAsanaH.
Monocular, a. ekAkza (kzI f.), ekanayana, kARa. 2 ekanetropayukta.
MONOCULAR , MONOCULOUS, a. ekAkzaH -kzA -kzaM, ekalocanaH -nA -naM, ekanetraH -trA -traM, kARaH -RA -RaM, ekAkzivikalaH -lA -laM.
MONODY: vilApaH (when the sense is clear); vilApagItam, etc.
MONOGAMIST , s. ekapatnIkaH, ekaBAryyakaH, sakfdvivAhI m. (n), apuna- rvivAhI m., ekastrIkaH.
Monogamy, s. sakfdvivAhaH, ekapatnIvrataM, ekastrIvivAhaH. [Monogam]ist, s. ekapatnIkaH, eka-strIkaH.
MONOGAMY: ekamAryA-pariRayaH or -parigrahaH; and sim. comp.s.
MONOGAMY , s. ekapatnIvrataM, ekaBAryyAvrataM, ekastrIvivAhaH, sakfdvivAhaH, apunarvivAhaH.
MONOGRAM: *AdyakzarabanDaH.
MONOGRAM , s. parasparasaMyuktaM nAmAdyAkzaraM.
MONOGRAPH: prabanDaH (= dissertation). M.s.: ekEkavizayaprabanDAH.
Monologue, s. Atma-sva-gataBAzaRaM.
MONOLOGUE: svagatoktiH and sim. comp.s. (?).
MONOLOGUE , s. AtmaBAzaRaM, AtmagataBAzaRaM, svagataBAzaRaM, svasamIpaBAzaRaM,
Monomachy, s. dvaMdvaM, niyudDaM, dvaMdvayudDaM.
MONOMACHY , s. dvandvayudDaM, dvandvaM, dvandvAyoDanaM, niyudDaM.
Monomania, s. ekavizayAsakti f., ekavi-zayonmAdaH. Monomaniac, a. ekavizayo-nmatta.
MONOMANIA: ekavizaya unmAdaH (?); ekavizaye citta- vikzepaH: v. Madness.
MONOMANIA , s. ekavizayonmAdaH, ekavizayavikzepaH, ekavizayaBrAntiH f.
MONOMANIAC , s. ekavizayonmattaH, ekavizayavikziptaH, ekavizayaBrAntaH.
Monopetalous, a. ekadalaviSizwa.
MONOPETALOUS , a. ekadalakaH -kA -kaM, ekadalaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM.
Monoplane, s. ekatalaM vimAnaM.
MONOPOLIST: *ananyasADAraRavyavasAyin (f. nI) and sim. comp.s.

MONOPOLIST , MONOPOLIZER, s. (One who purchases the whole of a commodity) pUrvvakretA m. (tf), pUrvvakrayI m. (n), sarvvaBARqakretA, ekavyavasAyI m. — (One who takes the whole) pUrvvagrAhakaH, sarvvagrAhakaH.
MONOPOLIZE: I To forstall: q. v.II In gen.: ananyasADAraRaM (f. RAM) karoti (?).

To MONOPOLIZE , v. a. (Purchase the whole of a commodity with the view of selling at higher prices) aDikamUlyavikraya- budDyA sarvvaBARqaM pUrvvaM krI (c. 9. krIRAti -RIte, kretuM) or sarvvapaRyadravyARi pUrvvaM krI or sarvvadravyARAM pUrvvakrayaM kf. — (Take or obtain the whole) sarvvaM grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM) or prAp (c. 5. -Aptoti -AptuM), sAkalyaM grah or pUrvvaM grah. — (Have the sole right of dealing) ekavyavasAyaM kf, ekavyApAraM kf, krayavikrayADikAram ekato or asAmAnyena Df (c. 10. DArayati -yituM).
MONOPOLIZED , p. p. pUrvvagfhItaH -tA -taM, pUrvvakrItaH -tA -taM, pUrvvaprAptaH &c.

Monopoly, s. ekADikAraH, ananyasADAraRaH aDikAraH, ekavyApAraH-vyavasAyaH. [Monopol]ist, [Monopol]izer, s. pUrvakrayin m., sarvagrAhakaH. [Monopol]ize, v. t. (sarvaM) pUrvaM krI 9 U, (sarvaM) svAyattIkf 8 U, AtmasAtkf, ananyasADAraRaM AtmADInIkf, asAmAnyena Buj 7 A or juz 6 A.
MONOPOLY: *ananyasADAraRo vyavasAyaH or vyApAraH, etc.
MONOPOLY , s. ekavyavasAyaH, ekavyApAraH, ekavyavahAraH, ekapaRAyA, ekabARijyaM, asAmAnyavyavahAraH, ekaprayogaH, asAmAnyaprayogaH, krayavi- krayayor ekADikAraH.
MONOSYLLABIC: (1) ekAkzaraH (rA, raM);(2) ekAkzarin (f. RI);(3) ekasvaraH (rA, raM).
MONOSYLLABIC , a. ekAkzaraH -rA -raM, ekAkzarI -riRI -ri (n).
Monosyllable, s. ekAkzaraM. Monosyllabic, a. ekAkzara, ekAc; ‘m(onosyllabic) roots’ ekAco DAtavaH.
MONOSYLLABLE: (1) ekAkzaram;(2) ekAkzaraSabdaH.
MONOSYLLABLE , s. ekAkzaraM, ekAkzaraSabdaH, ekAkzaraviSizwaH SabdaH.
MONOTHEISM: advEtavAdaH and sim. comp.s.
MONOTHEISM , s. advEtaM, advEtavAdaH, kevaleSvaravAdaH, kevaleSvaramataM.
Monotheist, s. advEtavAdin m. Monotheism, s. advEtaM, advEtavAdaH.
MONOTHEIST: (1) advEtavAdin (f. nI);(2) ekeSvaravAdin (f. nI).
MONOTHEIST , s. advEtavAdI m. (n), advayavAdI m., kevaleSvaravAdI m.
MONOTONE: ekasvaraH; aBinnasvaraH.
MONOTONOUS: Lit.: ekasvaraH (rA, raM). II Fig.: ekatAnaH (nA, naM) (?).

MONOTONOUS , a. (Having but one tone) ekasvaraH -rA -raM, ekatAnaH -nA -naM, ekasvanaH -nA -naM, samasvaraH -rA -raM, samAnasvaraH -rA -raM, ananya- svaraH -rA -raM. — (Always the same, tediously uniform) ekarUpaH -pA -paM, ekaprakAraH -rA -raM, samarUpaH -pA -paM, samAnarUpaH -pA -paM, sama- samAnaH -nA -naM, ekasAraH -rA -raM, nirvikAraH -rA -raM, nirvikriyaH -yA -yaM, aviSezaH -zA -zaM, ekaraNgI -NgiRI &c.
MONOTONOUSLY , adv. ekasvareRa, samasvareRa, ekarUpeRa, samarUpeRa, sama- samAnaM, nirvikAraM, avikAreRa.

Monotony, s. ekasvaraH-svanaH, svarABedaH, eka-svarasaMtAnaH, svarasamatA, svaraBedABAvaH. 2 eka-sama-samAna-rUpatA, viSezABAvaH, ekavyApAra-saMtati f. [Monoton]ous, a. ekasvara-tAna-svana, sama-aBinna-svara. 2 eka-sama-samAna-rUpa, eka-prakAra, nirvikAra, nirviSezaM. [Monoton]ously, adv. ekasvareRa, samarUpeRa, nirvikAraM. [Monoton]ousness, s. See (s.) above.
MONOTONY: expr. by adj., avoid m. of deli- very: ekasvaravyAhAraM parihara.

MONOTONY , s. (Sameness of tone) ekasvaraH, svarEkyaM, svarABedaH, svara- samatA, svarasamAnatA, samAnasvaratvaM, svaraBedABAvaH. — (Dull uniformity) [Page513-a+ 51] ekarUpatA, samarUpatA, samasamAnatA, samAnarUpatA, ekavyApAratvaM, sama- vyApAratvaM, vyApArABedaH, vikArABAvaH, viSezABAvaH.
Monsoon, s. varzAH (f. pl.). varzAkAlaH-samayaH, prAvfz f., meGakAlaH, parjanyakAlaH.
MONSOON: *kAlavAtaH, during the m.s: *kAla- vAtAgame.
MONSOON , s. (Rainy season) vfzwikAlaH, meGAgamaH, meGakAlaH, meGasamayaH, GanasamayaH, parjanyakAlaH, jaladAgamaH, prAvfwkAlaH.

Monster, s. rAkzasaH, krUra-Gora-karman m. 2 rAkzasa-vikawa-BIma-SarIraH-vigrahaH, bfhatpari-mARaH, vikawAkAraH; See Giant. 3 adButaM, apUrvavastu n., aparUpaM, virUpavizayaH; ‘m(onster)s in the form of men’ mAnavarAkzasAH; ‘m(onster)s of the deep’ makarAdayaH, yAdAMsi. Monstrous, a. adButa, vilakzaRa, apUrva, sfzwikramabAhya. 2 apa-vi-rUpa, vikftAkfti. 3 rAkzasarUpa, GoradarSana, vikawa-BIma-karAla-rUpa-SarIra, atimahat, GorarUpa, GorAkfti, vikawA-kAra, BIma-ugra-rOdra-darSana. 4 (Of acts) dAruRa, Gora, atibIBatsa, vikawa. [Monstrous]ly, adv. adButaM, vikawaM, dAruRaM, utkawaM, BfSaM, atIva, atyaMtaM, atiSayena; See Exceedinglyness. Monstrosity, s. adButatA, GoratA, dAruRatA, &c.
MONSTER: I Anything monstrous: expr. by adj..II A marvel: adButam. Ph.: a man- m.: nararAkzasaH (?).

MONSTER , s. (Something unnatural) adButaM, adButavipayaH, adButavastu n., apUrvvavizayaH, mahodButaM. — (Something deformed) aparUpavastu n., virUpavizayaH, aparUpaM, aparUpatA, vErUpyaM. — (A being enormously large or very frightful) rAkzasaSarIraH, BImaSarIraH, vikawAkAraH, vikawarUpaH, GorarUpI m. (n), suvfhatparimARaH. — (Horribly wicked person) rAkzasaH, rAvaRaH, GorakarmmA m. (n).

MONSTROUS: I Unnatural and misshapen: (1) aparUpaH (pA, paM) (?);(2) vikftAkfti (mfn.), Vi. v. 29.; and sim. comp.s.II Dread- -ful, horrible: GoradarSanaH (nA, naM) and sim. comp.s.(?).III Fig.; revolting to reason: rAkzasa (f. sI) or pESAca (f. cI).

MONSTROUS , a. (Unnatural, extraordinary, out of the course of nature) adButaH -tA -taM, mahodButaH -tA -taM, apUrvvaH -rvvA -rvvaM, vilakzaRaH -RA -RaM, vilakzaH -kzA -kzaM, sfzwimArgavahirgataH -tA -taM, sfzwirItivAhyaH -hyA -hyaM, sfzwikramavAhyaH &c. — (Deformed) aparUpaH -pA -paM, virUpaH -pA -paM. — (Enormously large) rAkzasaSarIraH -rA -raM, ativfhacCarIraH -rA -raM, vikawaSarIraH &c., atimahAn -hatI -hat (t), sumahAn &c., ativfhan -hatI &c., muvfhatparimARaH -RA -RaM. — (Frightful) GorarUpI -piRI &c., GorAkftiH -tiH -ti, vikawAkAraH -rA -raM, BImadarSanaH -nA -naM, rOdradarSanaH &c., karAlarUpaH -pA -paM. — (Atrocious) dAruRaH -RA -RaM, aGoraH -rA -raM, vikawaH -wA -waM.
MONSTROUSLY: utkawam: v. Dreadfully, ex- -ceedingly.
MONSTROUSLY , adv. adButaM, vikawaM, dAruRaM, BfSaM, atiSayaM -yena, atIva.
MONSTROUSNESS: aparUpatA, etc.: v. Monstrous, enormity.
MONSTROUSNESS , s. adButatA, aGoratA, GoratA, dAruRatA, vikawatA.

Month, s. mAsaH; ‘half a m(onth)’ pakzaH; ‘bright half of the m(onth)’ Sukla-SudDa-sita-pakzaH, pUrva-pakzaH; ‘dark half’ kfzRa-uttara-tamisra-pakzaH, bahulaH, tamisraH; ‘a m(onth) old’ mAsajAta. [Month]ly, a. mAsika (kI f.), mAsya, prAtimAsika; ‘half-m(onthly)’ pAkzika (kI f.); ‘m(onthly) allowance’ mAsikaM. adv. mAse mAse, pratimAsaM.
MONTH: mAsaH, within six m.s: zaRmAsAmyantare, H. ; in the auspicious m. of Mārgaśīrṣa (Nov.-Dec.) mArgaSIrze SuBe mAsi, M. ; for two m.s: dvO mAsO, H. or mAsadvayam, D.

MONTH , s. mAsaH, mAs m., pakzadvayaM, pakzayugaM, nAkzatraM, yavyaH, varzAMSaH, varzANgaH. The following are the twelve Hindu months, 1. cEtraH, corresponding to the last half of March and the first half of April, 2. vESAKaH, April, May, 3. jyezwaH, May, June, 4. AzAQaH, June, July, 5. SrAvaRaH, July, August, 6. BAdraH or BAdrapadaH, August, September, 7. ASvinaH or ASvayujaH, September, October, 8. kArttikaH, October, November, 9. mArga- SIrzaH, November, December, 10. pOzaH, December, January, 11. mAGaH, January, February, 12. PAlgunaH, February, March. — (Lunar month) cAndramAsaH; ‘half of a lunar month,’ pakzaH; ‘light or first half of the month,’ SuklapakzaH, SudDapakzaH, sitapakzaH, pUrvapakzaH, praTamapakzaH, devapakzaH; ‘dark or second half of the month,’ kfzRapakzaH, tamisraH, tamisrapakzaH, uttarapakzaH, aparapakzaH, bahulaH; ‘last day of the half-month,’ pakzAntaH, pakzAvasaraH. — (Solar month) sOramAsaH, sOraH; ‘a month old,’ mAsajAtaH -tA -taM, mAsInaH -nA -naM.
MONTHLY (adj.): (1) mAsikaH (kI, kaM);(2) by comp.;(3) by adv.
MONTHLY (adj.): (1) mAse mAse;(2) pratimAsam; (3) mAsi mAsi.

MONTHLY , a. mAsakaH -kI -kaM, mAsInaH -nA -naM, mAsyaH -syA -syaM, prAti- mAsikaH -kI -kaM, mAsAnumAsikaH -kA -kaM; ‘half-monthly,’ ArdDa- mAsikaH -kI -kaM, pAkzikaH -kI -kaM; ‘monthly allowance,’ mAsikaM.
MONTHLY , adv. pratimAsaM, mAse mAse, mAsi mAsi, anumAsaM.
Monument, s. kIti-yaSaH-staMBaH, smAraka-cihnaM. 2 cEtyaM, samADiH; stUpaH. [Monument]al, a. smaraRArTaka, smaraRakArin. 2 cEtyasaMbaMDin.
MONUMENT: kIrtistammaH (= memorial pillar), R. and sim. comp.s.
MONUMENT , s. (Memorial) smaraRArTakacihnaM. — (Tomb, monument to the dead) cityaM, cEtyaM, citAcUqakaM, cEtraH, stUpaH, samADiH m.
MONUMENTAL , a. (Memorial) smaraRArTakaH -kA -kaM. — (Belonging to a tomb) cEtyasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).

Mood, s. BAvaH, vftti f., prakfti f., avasTA, daSA, cittavfttiH, manoBAvaH; ‘an angry m(ood)’ kopavfttiH. 2 vAcyaM, arTaH. [Mood]y, a. ruzwa, krudDa, vakraBAva, udAsIna, udAsIna-vftti, cittodvigna, vizaRRa, udvigna, dInamanaska. 2 svacCaMda, svErin; See Humorsome.
MOOD: I Frame of mind: BAvaH.II In gram: expr. with prakAraH. N.B. Note how expr. in Sanskrit: here the verb is in the imperative, subjunctive m.: atrAnujYAyAM low, ASaNkAyAM liN.

MOOD , s. (Temper of mind) vfttiH f., cittavfttiH f., manovfttiH f., BAvaH, manoBAvaH, prakftiH f., manaHsTitiH f., manovasTA; ‘cheerful mood,’ AnandavfttiH f., hAsyavfttiH f. — (In grammar) vacyaM, arTaH. — (In logic) prakAraH, rUpaM.
MOODINESS: vakratA: v. Peevishness, anger.
MOODINESS , s. udAsInatA, kroDaSIlatA, vizaRatA, kArkaSyaM, vakratA.
MOODY: vakra (f. krA): v. Peevish, angry.

MOODY , a. kroDavaSAd udAsInaH -nA -naM or udAsavfttiH -ttiH -tti or vizaRaH -RA -RaM, kroDaSIlaH -lA -laM, utkaRwitaH -tA -taM, dInamanAH -nAH -naH (s), udvignamanAH &c., cintodvignaH -gnA -gnaM, karkaSaBAvaH -vA -vaM, vakraBAvaH &c., ruzwaH -zwA -zwaM.

Moon, s. caMdraH, SaSin m., iMduH, somaH, viDuH, caMdramas m., niSAkaraH, rajani(nI)karaH, glOH, SaSaDaraH, SaSAMkaH, mfgAMkaH, himAMSuH, suDAMSuH, SuBrAMSuH, ozaDISaH, ozaDIpatiH, kumudabAMDavaH, dvijarAjaH, kalAniDiH-nATaH, abjaH, jEvAtfkaH, nakzatreSaH, kzapAkaraH; and comp. of patiH, ISaH, nATaH, paH, with words for ‘Night’, ‘Star’, or of ‘Ray’ with ‘Cold’ or ‘Nectar’, q. v.; kzapA-nATaH, SItakaraH, tArAnATaH, uqupaH; ‘orb of the m(oon)’ biMbaH-baM, maMqalaM; ‘digit of the m(oon)’ kalA, re(le)KA; ‘full m(oon)’ pUrRimA, pOrRamAsI; ‘new m(oon)’ amA, amAva(vA)sI, amAva(vA)syA, darSaH, sUryendusaMgamaH; ‘m(oon)-beam’ caMdrapAdaH, SaSikaraH-raSmiH, suDAMSuH, (Ray, q. v.); ‘m(oon)-light’ kOmudI, caM-drikA, jyotsnA, caMdra-SaSi-praBA, caMdrAtapaH; (a.) jyotsnAvat, jyotsnAyukta, caMdraprakASita; ‘enjoys m(oon)-light evenings’ jyotsnAvato nirviSati pradozAn (R. vi. 34); ‘m(oon)-plant’ somalatA, somavallI, vallarI, brAhmI, matsyAkzI; ‘m(oon)-shine’ caMdrapraBA-dyuti-kAMti f.; ‘m(oon)-stone’ caMdrakAMtaH, somakAMtaH, caMdramaRiH; ‘m(oon)-struck’ vikzipta-BrAMta-budDi, vipluta-hata-mati. [Moon]less, a. hata-nazwa-caMdra, caMdrahIna. [Moon]y, a. caMdratulya.

MOON: (1) candraH, enjoy the m.-beams: sevyantAM candrapAdAH, V. ; full m.: q. v.; half m.: ardDacandraH, P. ; approaching m. -rise: AsannacandrodayaH, K. ; (2) SaSI, m. -light passes with the m.: SaSinA saha yAti kOmudI, Ku.;(3) induH, the new m.: navenduH, R. ; the m. -set: gato'staminduH, B. ;(4) candramasa (m.), fixing my sight on the m. which has whitened the quarters with its rays: karE- rDavalitASAmuKe candramasi nihitadfzwiH, K. ii.;(5) viDuH;(6) niSAkaraH;(7) SaSANkaH;(8) suDAMSuH; (9) dvijarAjaH;(10) SItamayUKaH. The day of new m.: pratipad.

MOON , s. candraH -ndrakaH, candramAH m. (s), somaH -mA m. (n), induH m., viDuH m. — (Marked like a hare or rabbit) SaSI m. (n), SaSANkaH, SaSaDaraH, SaSaBft m., SaSavinduH m., SaSalAYCanaH. — (Mark- ing the night) rajanIkaraH, niSAkaraH, kzapAkaraH, niSAketuH m. — (Lord of the night) niSApatiH m., kzapAnATaH, yAminIpatiH m., niSITinInATaH, rajanInATaH. — (Gem of the night) rAtrimaRiH m., niSAmaRiH. — (Lord of the constellations) nakzatranATaH, nakzatrapaH, fkzeSaH, uqupaH, uqupatiH, uqurAw m. (j), dAkzAyiRIpatiH m., tArA- DipatiH m., BapatiH m. — (The repository and producer of nectar or ambrosia, which is supposed to be distilled in its rays) amftasUH m., amftadIDitiH m., amftADAraH, amftasut m., suDAniDiH m., suDADAraH, suDABftiH m., suDAsUtiH m., suDAMSuH, suDAkaraH, suDANgaH, pIyUzaruciH m., pIyUzamahAH m. (s), pIyUzaniDiH m. — (Having cool rays or radiance) SItAMSuH m., SItamayUKaH, SItamarIciH m., SItaBAnuH m., himAMSuH m., himakaraH, himaraSmiH m., himadyutiH m., SItaruk m. (c), SItaguH m., himaSraTaH, prAleyAMSuH m., tuhinAMSuH m. — (Having white rays or pale radiance) SuBrAMSuH m., sitAMSuH, sitaraSmiH m., sitadIDitiH m., SvetaDAmA m. (n), SvetarocIH m. (s), CAyABft m. — (Marked like a deer) mfgANkaH, mfgavipluH m., hariRANkaH, hariRakalaNkaH, mfgalAYCanaH, mfgaDaraH, CAyAmfgaDaraH. — (Containing many digits) kalAniDiH m., kalApUrRaH, kalAvAn m. MOON-BEAM , s. candrapAdaH, SaSipAdaH, candrakiraRaH, candraraSmiH m., SaSi- kiraRaH, SaSikaraH, SaSimayUKaH, aMSuH m., somAMSuH m., candrAMSuH m., candrikA, candramarIciH m., pUrRAnakaM.

MOONLIGHT , s. candrapraBA, SaSipraBA, candraprakASaH, candrikA, candrimA, jyotsnA, candrajyotis n., candrAtapaH, candragolikA, kOmudI, candraSAlA, dIpikA, cAndrI, mAlatI, tuhinaM, amftataraNgiRI, kEravI, haricandanaM, mudI, candakaH.

MOONY , a. ardDacandraDvajANkitaH -tA -taM, ardbacandraDvajaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM.
Moor, v. t. rajjvA baMD 9 P or gatiM ruD 7 U. s. ‘m(oor)-land’ kacCaH, kacCa-anUpa-BUH. [Moor]ish, [Moor]y, a. AnUpa (pI f.), kacCa, in comp.; anUpa.
MOOR (subs.): I An open waste: sarasapatita- BUmiH (?).II A dark African: *mOraH (f. rI).
MOOR (v.): baDnAti (banD, c. 9.), m. the ark with the peak of the Himālaya: himavataH SfNge nAvaM baDnIta, Mah. iii. 187. 49.; ark-m.ing peak: nObanDanaM SfNgam, Mah.
MOOR , s. jaNgalaBUmiH f., KilaBfmiH f., anupaBUH f., kacCaH, kacCaBUH.

MOOR-HEN: jalakukkuwI.
MOOR-LAND: sarasapatitaBUmiH (?).

To MOOT , v. a. (Discuss) vicar (c. 10. -cArayati -yituM), vitark (c. 10. -tarkayati -yituM), vivad (c. 1. -vatati -te -dituM), vivAdAspadIkf, vicArA- spadIkf, vitarkAspadIkf — (Bring forward) upanyasa (c. 4. -asyati -amituM).
MOOT , MOOT-CASE, MOOT-POINT, s. vicAravizayaH, vicArapadaM, vicArAspadaM, vicArasTalaM, vivAdAspadaM, vivAdavizayaH, sandigDavizayaH, anipyannavizayaH, asidDAntaH.
MOOT-POINT: sandigDavizayaH and sim. comps.
MOOTED , p. p. vicAritaH -tA -taM, vAdagrastaH -stA -staM, vicArAspadIkftaH &c.
Mop, s. saMmArjanI, SoDanI. 2 bAlikA, taruRI. v. t. mfj 2 P or c., SuD c.
MOP (subs.): I A brush: mArjanI.II A young girl: bAlA.
MOP (v.): saM-mArzwi or mArjayati (mfj, c. 2. and 10.).
MOP , s. mArjanI mammArjanI, SoDanI, vimArgaH, parizkArakaH.
To MOP , v. a. mfj (c. 2. mArzwi -rzwuM), sammfj, SuD (c. 10. SoDayati -yituM).
Mope, v. i. vi-ava-sad 1 P, mlE 1 P, durma-nAyate (D.), vizaRRIBU 1 P. [Mop]ing, [Mop]ish, a. vizaRRa, avasanna, udvigna, durmanAyamAna, vizaRRavadana; See Deject, [Deject]ed.
MOPE (v.): durmanAyate (nomi.): v. To drowse, dejected.
To MOPE , v. n. vizad (c. 1. -zIdati -zattuM), avasad, udAs (c. 2. -Aste- AsituM), vizaRIBU, udvignIBU, durmanasa (nom. durmanAyate), unmanas, glE (c. 1. glAyati, glAtuM).
MOPING, MOPISH (adj.): nistejas (mfn.): v. Dull, gloomy.
MOPING , MOPISH, a. vizaRaH -RA -RaM, avasannaH -nnA -nnaM, udAsInaH -nA -naM, udAsI -sinI -si (n), durmanAH -nAH -naH (s), udvignamanAH &c., antarmanAH &c.
Moppet, s. vasrapAMcAlikA, pawaputrikA.
MOPPET , MOPSEY, s. pawaputrikA, vastraputrikA, vastraKaRqamayI puttalikA.

Moral, a. sADu, sADuvftta, sadAcAra, DArmika-sAtvika- (kI f.); nItimat, nayAnusArin; Darmya, puRya, nyAyAnusArin, DarmAnurUpa, nyAyya; gen. ex. by sat, nIti, naya in comp., ‘m(oral) instruction’ nayopadeSaH, nIti f.; ‘m(oral) lessons’ nItipAWAH; sometimes by citta, mAnasa in comp.; ‘m(oral) freedom’ cittasvAtaMtryaM; ‘m(oral) advancement’ mAna-sonnati f.; ‘m(oral) science’ nItiSAstraM; ‘m(oral) duties’ SASvataDarmaH, sadAcAraH. 2 niyamA-DIna. 3 anumAna-yukti-sidDa. s. tAtparyaM, aBiprAyaH, BAvArTaH, tAtparyArTaH. [Moral]ist, s. nItiSAstrajYaH, nItijYaH, nayajYaH; nItyupadeSakaH, nItivid, sadasadvivecakaH. [Moral]ity, s. nItiH, nayaH, nIti or naya vidyA or SAstraM, sadvyavahAra-SAstraM, sadasadvivekaH-vicAraH. 2 DarmAnuzWAnaM, sADuvfttaM, puRyaSIlatA, sadAcAraH, su-sat-caritaM, Darmavftti f. 3 nyAyyatA, DarmyatA, Darma-nyAya-anusAraH. [Moral]ize, v. t. DarmopadeSAspa-dIkf 8 U. v. i. nItyupadeSaM dA 3 U or liK 6 P. [Moral]ly, adv. nItiSAstrAnurUpaM, nayataH, nItyA, DarmeRa, DarmataH, nyAyena, nyAya-taH. 2 yuktyA, manasA, anumAnena. Morals, s. nItiH, nItiSAstraM-vidyA. 2 AcAraH, AcaraRaM, vfttiH, caritaM, vfttaM, vyavahAraH, rIti f.; ‘good m(orals)’ suSIlaM, sadAcAraH, sADuvfttaM, vinayaH, sADu-su-sat-caritaM.

MORAL (adj.): I Relating to m.s: nIti- or naya- in comp., m. bond: nayabanDanam (?); m. philosophy: *nItidarSanam.II Virtuous, just: nyAyya (f. yyA).III Probable: there is m. certainty of his guilt: *tasyAparADitAM prati nAsti kaScidapyAntaraH sandehaH.
MORAL (subs.): I Behaviour: q. v.II In pl.: nItiSAstram.III Drift: q. v.:(1) BAvaH;(2) aBiprAyaH.

MORAL , a. (Virtuous) sadAcAraH -rA -raM, sadAcArI -riRI -ri (n), DArmmikaH -kI -kaM, DarmmAcArI &c., DarmmacArI &c., sADuH -DuH -DvI -Du, sADuvfttaH -ttA -ttaM, sucaritaH -tA -taM, saccaritaH -tA -taM, sADvAcAraH -rA -raM, DarmyaH -rmyA -rmyaM, DarmmI &c., suDarmmA -rmmA -rma (n), DarmmaBfta m. f. n., nyAyAcAraH &c., vfttavAn -vatI -vat (t), avyasanI &c., puRyaH -RyA -RyaM, sAttvikaH -kI -kaM, nItimAn &c. — (Relating to the prac- tice of men, or to actions good or evil) lokavyavahArasambanDI &c., lokAcAravizayakaH -kA -kaM, sadasadAcArasambanDI &c., sadasadnyava- hAravizayaH -yA -yaM, viDinizeDAnvitaH -tA -taM. — (Subject to moral laws, bound by precepts and prohibitions) viDinizeDADInaH -nA -naM, viDinizeDAyattaH -ttA -ttaM, viDinizeDavAn &c., niyamADInaH &c. — (Supported by reason or probability, founded on experience) anumAnasidDaH -dDA -dDaM, yuktisidDaH &c., AnumAnikaH -kI -kaM, yOktikaH -kI -kaM, anuBUtisidDaH &c., yuktiBAvyaH -vyA -vyaM, anu- mAnamUlaH -lA -laM; ‘moral philosophy,’ nItiSAstraM, nItividyA, vyavahAraSAstraM, nItiH f.
MORAL , s. (Moral doctrine taught by a fiction) tAtparyyaM, tAtparyyArTaH, aBiprAyaH, BAvATeH, tAttvikaM, DvanitArTaH, garBaH.
MORALIST: nItiSAstravid (mfn.) and sim. comp.s.

MORALIST , s. (Teacher of moral duties) nItiSAstropadeSakaH, nItyu- padezwA m. (zwf), nItiSikzakaH, DarmmopadeSI m. (n), nItivivecakaH, sada- sadvivecakaH, nItiSAstrajYaH, nItividyAjYaH, karttavyAkarttavyopadeSakaH. — (Mere moral person) nItimArgAvalambI m., kevalanItimArgASrayI.

MORALITY , s. (System of moral duties) nItiH f., nItividyA, nItiSAstraM, vyavahAraSAstraM, nayaH, nayavidyA, nayaSAstraM, arTaSAstraM, vina- yavidyA, SIlavidyA, sadasadvicAraH, sadasadvivekaH, kartavyAkarttavyavicAraH, karttavyAkarttavyavivekaH. ‘as invented by Vrihaspati,’ vArhaspatyaM. — (Practice of moral duties, virtue) DarmmAnuzWAnaM, DarmmAcaraRaM, DarmmA- cAratA, DarmmaH, DarmmatvaM, sadAcAratvaM, saccaritaM, sucaritaM, sADuSIlatA, puRyatA, puRyaSIlatvaM sADuvfttaM. — (Conformity to the principles of rectitude) DarmmAnusAritvaM, nyAyAnusAraH, nyAyaH, DarmyatA, Darmmatva.
MORALIZE (v. i.): nIticintAM karoti, nItiprabanDaM liKati, etc.
To MORALIZE , v. a. Apply to the purposes of moral instruc- tion) hitopadeSAspadIkf, DarmmopadeSAspadIkf, nItiSikzAspadIkf.
To MORALIZE , v. n. (Make moral reflections) hitopadeSaM kf, Darmmo- padeSaM kf, nItyupadeSaM kf, hitopadeSaM liK (c. 6. liKati, leKituM).
MORALIZER , s. hitopadeSakaH, DarmmopadezwA m. (zwf), nItiSikzakaH.
MORALLY: I In a moral point of view: nItimArgAnusAreRa.II Virtuously, honestly: nyAyataH.III Probably: expr. as shewn under Moral (adj (III).

MORALLY , adv. (According to the rules of morality) nItiSA- stratas, nItiSAstravat, nItitas. — (Virtuously) DarmmeRa, Darmmatas, nyAyatas. — (According to reason or the usual course of things) anumAnena, yuktyA, anumAnatasa, yuktitas, yaTAmamBavaM.

MORALS , s. (System of morality) nItiH f., nItiSAstraM, nItividyA. See MORALITY. (Conduct) AcAraH, AcaraRaM, AcaritaM, caritaM, vyavahAraH, vfttiH f., pravfttiH f., vfttaM, rItiH f.; ‘good morals,’ vinayaH, sadAcAraH, saccaritaM, mucaritaM, sADucaritaM, SIlaH, suSIlaH.
Morass, s. kacCaH, anUpaH, anUpaBUH.
MORASS: sajalaBUmiH (?): v. Marsh.
MORASS , s. kacCaH, kacCaBUH f., anUpaH, anUpaBUH f., jalAQyaBUmiH f., paNki- laBUH f., AzyaBUH f.
Morbid, a. dUzita, udBrAMta, vikfta, asvasTa, asusTa, rogAkrAMta, vyADita.
MORBID: duzwaH (zwA, zwaM); v. Also diseased.
MORBID , a. asvasTaH -sTA -sTaM, asusTaH &c., rogI -giRI -gi (n), rogavAn -vatI -vat (t), sarogaH -gA -gaM, vikArI &c., vikftaH -tA -taM, vyADitaH -tA -taM.
MORBIDNESS: (1) duzwatA;(2) dozaH (= fault, defect).
MORBIDNESS , s. asvasTatA, asvAsTyaM, asusTatA, sarogatA, rogitvaM.
Morbific, a. roga-vyADi-kara (rI f.), rogada.
MORBIFIC, -AL: rogakaraH (rI, raM) and sim. comp.s.: v. Disease.
MORBIFIC , MORBIFICAL, a. rogajanakaH -kA -kaM, rogakaraH -rA -raM, asvA- sTyajanakaH &c., vyaDikaraH -rA -raM, anArogyakaraH &c., rogadaH -dA -daM.
Morbose, a. rogajanita, vyADyudBava.
MORBOSE , a. rogajanitaH -tA -taM, rogajaH -jA -jaM, asusTaH -sTA -sTaM.
Mordacious, a. daMSaka. Mordacity, s. daMSakatA, daMSanaM.
MORDACIOUS , a. daMSakaH -kA -kaM, daMSanakArI -riRI -ri (n).
MORDACITY , s. daMSakatA, daMSanaSIlatA, daMSanaM, daMSanaguRaH.
Mordant, a. ugra, aruMtuda, tIkzRa, niMdAgarBa.
MORDANT: I Adj.: kawu (mfn.);II Subs.: raNgasaMsTApakaM dravyam.
MORDICANT , a. KAdakaH -kA -kaM, aruzkaraH -rI -raM, daMSakaH &c.

More, a. aDika, BUyas, aDikatara; uttara, atirikta, para, anya; oft. ex. by tara or Iyas affixed; ‘m(ore) in strengh’ balI-yas, prabalatara; ‘something m(ore)’ kiMcit anyadapi; ‘what m(ore)’ kimaparaM, kimanyat; ‘after m(ore) than three years’ samaDikA-dvarzatrayAt; ‘m(ore) or less’ nyUnADika; ‘for m(ore) than 1,000 years’ paraH sahasrAH SaradaH. s. aDikaM, ADikyaM, atirekaH, atiSayaH; oft. ex. by aparaM, anyat; See above; ‘m(ore) or less’ nyUnAtirekaH, nyUnADikyaM; ‘no m(ore) of solicitation’ alaMkftaM-atiprArTanayA; ‘what m(ore)’ kimanyat; kiM-bahunA. adv. (With adj.) ex. by aDika in comp.; aDikamanojYa; or gen. by compar. degree in tara or Iyas. 2 (With verbs) by aDikaM, aDikataraM ataHparaM, punaH, BUyaH; ‘m(ore) and m(ore)’ uttarottaraM, aDikADikaM; ‘no m(ore)’ na ataH-itaH paraM or UrDvaM; alaM, kftaM; See Enough ‘how much m(ore)’ kiM punaH, kimuta. Moreover, adv. anyacca, aparaM-api-ca, kiMca, paraM, api tu, api.

MORE (Adv.): I With adj.:(1) by comp. degree, m. beloved: priyataraH (rA, raM), K. ; m. tall: drAGIyas (f. sI), Ki.;(2) aDika in comp., m. beautiful: aDikamanojYaH (jYA, jYaM), Sa.II With verbs:(1) aDikam, puts the eye more: aDikaM cakzurAropayati, P. ;(2) aDika- taram (in comp.), shines m. now: aDikataramidAnIM rAjate,V Ph.: what can be m. distressing: tato duHKataraM nu kim, G. ; what can be m. wonder- ful: kimataH paramAScaryam, K. ; favoured her every day m. and m.: amyaDikaM pratidivasamasyAH prasAda- makarot, K. : increases m. and m.: uttarottaraM varDate (only of succession), H. ; as said and m.: yaToktamaByaDikaYca, D. ; no m.: na itaH param, D. or na ataH param or ata UrDvam, A.r.

MORE (adj.): (1) aDikaH (kA, kaM), m. devotion: aDikA BaktiH, K. ; five times m. than it: tataH paYcaguRADikam, Mah.; m. than twenty times: aDikaviMSAnvArAn, Ana.;(2) aDikataraH (rA, raM) (in comp.), their trouble is m.: kleSo'Dikatara- stezAm, G. Ph.: something m.: anyadapi, Sa.; anything m.: ato'pyaparam, Na.; what m.: kimanyat,V
MORE (subs.): aDikam, and the king who gave m. than the wish of the petitioner: nfpo'rTi- kAmAdaDikapradaSca, R. ; no m. = enough: q. v.: alam (with ins.).

MORE , a. aDikaH -kA -kaM, aDikataraH -rA -raM, aDikasaMKyakaH -kA -kaM, BUyAn -yasI -yaH (s), BUyizWaH -zWA -zWaM, uttaraH -rA -raM, atirekI -kiRI -ki (n), atiriktaH -ktA -ktaM, paraH -rA -raM, parataraH -rA -raM; often expressed by the comparative affixes tara and Iyas; as, ‘more in number.’ bahutaraH -rA -raM, baMhIyAn &c.; ‘more or less,’ nyUnADikaH -kA -kaM, nyUnAtirekaH -kA -ka; ‘more than a thousand,’ paraHsahasraH -srA -sraM; ‘more than a hundred,’ paraM SataM.

MORE , s. ADikyaM, aDikatA, AtirekyaM, atiriktatA, udrekaH, AtiSayyaM; ‘more or less,’ nyUnADikyaM, nyUnAtirekyaM, nyUnAtiriktaM; ‘neither more nor less, anyUnAnatiriktaM; ‘no more,’ kftaM, alaM with inst. c., as, ‘no more of this ceremony!’ kftam AdareRa, alam AdareRa; ‘what more need I say?’ kim anyat, kim bahunA.

MORE , adv. aDikaM, aDikatara, BUyas, BUyizWaM, atiriktaM, paraM; or often expressed by the comparative affixes tara and Iyas; as, ‘more heavy,’ gurutaraH -rA -raM, garIyAn -yasI -yaH (s); ‘more and more,’ uttarottaraM, aDikADikaM; ‘how much more?’ kimpunar, kimuta, sutarAM. — (Any more, again) punar, BUyas.

MOREOVER: (1) anyacca, m. spies have been employed: anyacca niyUktAH praRiDayaH, Mu.;(2) aparaYca, m. (he) is cruel: aparaYca krUraH, P. ;(3) kiYca, and m. you are our enemy: kiYcAnyat SatrurBavAna- smAkam, H. ;(4) api ca, C.
MOREOVER , s. apica, aparaYca, aparaM, paraM, paraYca, parantu, aparantu, anyacca, kiYca, aDikantu, aDikaM, punaSca, apitu, api, aTa.
Morganatic, a. anuloma (vivAhaH).
MORGANATIC: m. marriage: vAmAcAravivAhaH.
Moribund, a. mftakalpa-prAya, mumUrzu.
MORIBUND: (1) mumUrzu (mfn.);(2) Asannamftyu (mfn.): v. Death, near.
MORIBUND , a. mumUrzuH -rzuH -rzu, mfnakalpaH -lpA -lpaM, mftaprAyaH -yA -yaM.
Moringa, s. so(sO-So-SO)BAjanaM, SigruH, tIkzRagaMDakaH, a(A)kzIvaH, mocakaH.
Morion, s. SiraskaM, SirastrARaM, SIrzakaM.
MORION , s. SirastraM, SirastrARaM, SiraskaM, mastakarakzaRI, SIrzakaM.

Morn, Morning, s. vi-pra-BAtaM, pratyu(tyU)zaH-zas n., uzA, uzas f., vyuzwaM, kalyaM, aruRodayaH, prAtar ind., aharmuKaM, praBAta or uzaH-kAlaH or samayaH. 2 (Opposed to afternoon) pUrvAhRaH, prAhRaH; ‘it is broad m(orning)’ supraBAtA rajanI; ‘in the m(orning)’ prAtaH, prAtaHkAle, praBAte, pratyUze, vyuzwaM, prage; ‘I bid you good m(orning)’ ‘good m(orning) to you’ SuBaste prAtaHkAlaH (BUyAt); ‘early in the m(orning)’ suprAtaH, mahati pratyUze, atiprage, prAtareva. a. prAtaH-uzaH-kAlIna, prABAtika, Ozika (kI f.), uzasya, praBAtIya; gen. ex. by prAtar or (s.) in comp.; ‘m(orning) breeze’ viBAtavAyuH; ‘m(orning) devotion’ prAtarupAsanA; ‘m(orning) star’ praBAtatArA; ‘m(orning) twilight’ prAtaHsaMDyA.
MORN: (1) viBAtam;(2) dinamuKam, R. : v. Morning.

MORN , MORNING, s. praBAtaM, prAtaHkAlaH, prAtaHsamayaH, praBAtakAlaH, pratyUza- kAlaH, pratyUzaH, pratyUzas n., pratyuzaH, pratyuzas n., uzaH, uzas n., uzA- kAlaH, viBAtaM -takaM, BAtaH, vyuzwaM, aruRaH, aruRodayaH, kalyaM, kAlyaM, aharmuKaM, divasamuKaM, dinAramBaH, dinAdiH m., niSAvamAnaM, niSAntaH -ntaM, kzapAntaH, rAtrivigamaH, prAvoDikaH, vAsarasaNgaH. — (As opposed to afternoon) pUrvvAhnaH or pUrvvAhlaH, prAhlaH, pUrvvAhlakAlaH, prAhlakAlaH; ‘in the morning,’ prAtar, praBAte, prAtaHkAle, praBAtakAle, pratyUpe, upA, prage, prAhle, pUrvvAhle, niSAnte, pUrvvedyus; ‘to be chanted in the morning,’ prAtargeyaH -yA -yaM; ‘early in the morning,’ suprAtar, atipraBAte, atiprage; ‘to-morrow morning,’ SvaH praBAte; ‘good morning,’ supraBAtaM; ‘morning, noon, and evening,’ trikAlaM.

MORNING (subs.): I Lit.: praBAtam or viBAtam, tomorrow m.: SvaH praBAte, A.r., good m. to you: *supramAtaM te: v. Dawn; early in the m.: pratyUze or pratyUzasi or Uzasi, K. or atikalyam, M. ; the m. has dawned: pramAtA rajanI, Sa.; this m.: adya prAtaH, H. ; from m.: prAtarAraBya, Vi. II Forenoon: pUrvAhRaH, in the m.: pUrvAhRe, M.

MORNING (adj.): (1) by comp., m. breeze: viBAtavAyuH, R. ; the m. star: *praBAtatArA;(2) prAtar- in comp., m. time: prAtaHkAlaH; m. meal: prAtarASaH; m. duties: prAtaHkftyAni;(3) prABAtikaH (kI, kaM);(4) pragetanaH (nI, naM);(5) prAtaHkAlInaH (nA, naM). Ph.: the m. sun: bAlArURaH, R.

MORNING , a. prAtar in comp., prAtaHkAlInaH -nA -naM, prAtaHkAlikaH -kI -kaM, praBAtIyaH -yA -yaM, prABAtikaH -kI -kaM, pragetanaH -nI -naM, prAhletanaH -nI -naM, pUrvvAhletanaH -nI -naM, uzasyaH -syA -syaM, OzikaH -kI -kaM, OzasaH -sI -saM, vEyuzwaH -zwI -zwaM; ‘morning duties,’ prAtaHkftyaM; ‘morning ablution,’ prAtaHsnAnaM; ‘morning meal,’ prAtarASaH, prAtarBojanaM.
MORNING-GOWN , s. prAtaHkAle Bfto laGuprAvAraH, prAtarvasanaM, prAtarvastraM.
MORNING-STAR , s. praBAtasUcakatArA, praBAtatArA, SukraH.
MORNING-TWILIGHT , s. prAtaHsanDyA, prAksanDyA, pUrvvasanDyA, praBAtasanDyA.
MOROCCO: *mOracarman (n.).

Morose, a. karkaSa-kawu-vakra-svaBAva-prakfti, vAma or vakra-BAva or SIla, rUkzasvaBAva, sadA-vakra, pratIpa, udAsIna, duHSIla, udAsavftti. [Morose]ly, adv. vakraBAvena, karkaSaBAvAt, svaBAva-rOkzyeRa. [Morose]ness, s. karkaSatA, rUkzatA, vAmatA, vakratA, svaBAvakawutA, vakraSIlatA, pratIpatA, OdAsInyaM.
MOROSE: rUkza (f. kzA) (= rough, harsh: q. v.).

MOROSE , a. karkaSasvaBAvaH -vA -vaM, kawusvaBAvaH -vA -vaM, karkaSaBAvaH -vA -vaM, karkaSaSIlaH -lA -laM, vakraBAvaH -vA -vaM, sadAvakraH -krA -kraM, rukzasva- BAvaH -vA -vaM, nEkftikaH -kI -kaM, pratIpaH -pA -paM, udAsInaH -nA -naM, udAsavfttiH -ttiH -tti, aruntudaH -dA -daM, duHSIlaH -lA -laM, vAmaSIlaH &c.
MOROSELY: rUkzam: v. Harshly, roughly.
MOROSELY , adv. karkaSasvaBAvAt, kawusvaBAvAt, karkaSaM, kArkaSyena, vakraBAvena, sadAvakravat, duHSIlatvAt, rukzasvaBAvAt.
MOROSENESS: rOkzyam: v. Harshness, severity.

MOROSENESS , s. kArkaSyaM, karkaSatA, karkaSaSIlatA, kawutA, kawuSIlatA, duHSIlatA, dOHSIlyaM, vakratA, vakraSIlatA, svaBAvavakratA, svaBAvakArkaSyaM, svaBAvakawutA, udAsInatA, udAsavfttitvaM, pratIpatA, vAmaSIlatA, nikftiH f., SuktatA.
MORRIS: Ph.: m.-dance: lAsyaviSezaH; nine men's m.: alAvUkartanam (comp. Bengali lAu kAwAkAwi).
Morrow, s. para or uttara-divasaH or dinaM; ‘on the m(orrow)’ SvaH, paredyuH, paredyavi, kalye, uttaredyuH.

MORROW , s. (The day next after the present) paradivasaH, paradinaM, SvastanadivasaH, AgAmidivasaH, kalyaM; ‘to-morrow, on the morrow,’ Svas, paredyus, paradine, paradivase, paredyavi, kalli, kalye, anyedyus. — (The next day subsequent to any day) uttaradivasaH, uttaradinaM, uttaredyus; ‘the day after to-morrow,’ paraSvasa; ‘to-morrow morning,’ SvaH praBAte.
Morsel, s. kavalaH, grAsaH, piMdaH. 2 KaMqaH, lavaH, SakalaH-laM, kzudraBAgaH.
MORSEL: I Lit.: muzwiH: v. Also mouthful. II Fragment: KaRqa (mn.): v. Also little.

MORSEL , s. (Mouthful, small piece of food) grAsaH, piRqaH, kavalaH; ‘a morsel as big as an egg,’ aRqaparimARo grAsaH. — (Piece, bit) KaRqaH -RqakaH, kzudraBAgaH, lavaH, SakalaH, BinnaM, BittaM, BittiH f.; ‘a dainty morsel,’ sugrAsaH.
Morsure, s. daMSanaM.
MORSURE , s. daMSanaM, vidaMSanaM, daMSaH, daMSakaraRaM.

Mortal, s. martyaH, manuzyaH, martyaDarman, janmin, prARin, SarIrin, dehin, all m., deha-tanu-Bft, mftyuvaSaH; See Man. a. martya, martyaDarman, maraRaSIla, mftyuvaSa, naSvara, nASa-maraRa-aDIna, maraRa-kAla-Ayatta, anitya, vinASin; ‘men are m(ortal)’ manuzyA martyaDarmARaH. 2 prARahara (rI f.), jIvitApaha, prARAMtaka, mArAtmaka, marmaBedin, aMtakara (rI f.), prARApaha, prARaGna (GnI f.), maraRAvaha. 3 martya, mAnuza(zI f.), manuzyaDarman; See Human. 4 atyaMtadAruRa, atikleSaka; ‘m(ortal) enemy’ AmaraRAMtavErin m., dfQa-badDa-vEraH. [Mortal]ity, s. martyatA, maraRaSIlatA, mftyuvaSatA, mftyu-maraRa-DarmaH, kAlaDarmaH, naSvaratA, anityatA. 2 mftyu-maraRaM, nASaH, jIvitanASaH. 3 mAnuzyaM, mAnuzatA [Mortal]ly, adv. saprARanASaM, ex. by a.; ‘he was m(ortally) wounded’ tasya prARaharA vraRAH saMjAtAH, BinnamarmA'BUt.
MORTAL (subs.): martyaH: v. Man.

MORTAL (adj.): I Subject to death:(1) mftyuvaSaH (SA, SaM) and sim. comps.;(2) by circumlo., every one is m., all are m.: sarveRa Kalu martavyam, sarvAnAviSate mftyuH, Mah. s.II Causing death:(1) prARaharaH (rI, raM);(2) sANGAtikaH (kI, kaM), etc.III Human: q. v.: martya- in comp.

MORTAL , a. (Subject to death) maraRADInaH -nA -naM, martyaH -rtyA -rtyaM, marttavyaH -vyA -vya, nASADInaH -nA -naM, kAlADInaH -nA -naM, mftyaDInaH -nA -naM, maraRaDarmmakaH -kA -kaM, mftyuDarmmakaH -kA -kaM, mftyuvaSaH -SA -SaM, maraRavaSaH &c., antavAn -vatI -vat (t), anityaH -tyA -tyaM. — (Deadly) prARaDAtakaH -kA -kaM, prARaharaH -rA -raM, prARAntikaH -kI -kaM, prARAntakaH &c., jIvAntakaH &c., prARahArI -riRI -ri (n), prARanASakaH -kA -kaM, mArAtmakaH -kA -kaM, mftyujanakaH -kA -kaM, marmmaBedAM -dinI &c., marmmAntikaH &c., antakaraH -rA -raM. — (Belonging to man, human) mAnuzaH -zI -zaM -zikaH -kI -kaM, manuzyajAtIyaH -yA -yaM, manuzyaDarmmakaH -kA -kaM, pOruzeyaH -yI -yaM; ‘mortal state,’ mAnuzadaSA.
MORTAL , s. (A human being) martyaH, manuzyaH, mAnuzaH, mAnavaH, prARAM m. (n), prARaBft m., janmI m. (n), janmavAn m., SarIrI m., dehI m., dehaBft m., tanuBft m., cetanaH, mftyupAtraM, maraRapAtraM.
MORTALITY: I Subjection to death: expr. by adj. or circumlo.II Death: q. v. mftyuH. III Humanity: q. v.

MORTALITY , s. (Subjection to death) maraRADInatA, martyatA, mftyuvaSatA, nASADInatA, mftyuDarmmaH, maraRaDarmmaH, anityatA. — (Human nature) manuzyatA -tvaM, mAnuzyaM, mAnupattaM -tA, puruzatA. — (Death, death of great numbers) mftyuH m., maraRaM, atyayaH, nASaH, bahunASaH, bahujananASaH.
MORTALLY: I Lit.: expr. by adj., m. wounded: sANGAtikavraRopetaH (tA, taM).II Ex- -tremely: q. v.: durBaram.
MORTALLY , adv. prARanASena, prARaGAtena, sanASaM, saprARaGAtaM, saprARanASaM; mortally wounded,’ BinnamarmmA -rmmA -rmma (n).
Mortar, s. ulU(dU)KalaM; ‘m(ortar) and pestle’ ulUKalamusale. 2 lepaH, suDA, cUrRalepaH.
MORTAR: I For pounding: udUKalam.II A cement: izwakakzodalepaH and sim. expr. accord- -ing to its composition.III A kind of can- -non: *muzalam.

MORTAR , s. (Vessel in which substances are pounded) ulUKalaM, uqUKalaH -laM, udUKalaM; ‘pestle and mortar,’ ulUKalamuzale; ‘pounded in a mortar,’ ulUKalikaH -kI -kaM. — (Cement) suDA, lepaH, vilepaH, cUrRalepaH, karkaralepaH, udapepaH; ‘very hard,’ vajralepaH.

sanskrit.slp1: ADiH praRaSyeddviguRe Gane yadi na mokzyate
sanskrit.word: आधिः प्रणश्येद्द्विगुणे घने यदि न मोक्ष्यते
sanskrit.iast: ādhiḥ praṇaśyeddviguṇe ghane yadi na mokṣyate

details.body: Mortgage, s. ADiH, kzetra-sTAvara-ADiH BUminikzepaH, baMDakaH, nyAsaH. v. t. A-DA 3 U, ADIkf 8 U, baMDe dA 3 U, (sTAvara-DanaM) nyAsIkf. [Mortgag]ee, s. ADigrAhakaH, ADi baMDaka-nyAsa-grAhin m. [Mortgag]or, s. ADAtf m. nikzeptf m.

MORTGAGE (subs.): (1) AGiH (gen. term), m. -deed: ADileKyam, Kat.; a m. becomes lost if it is not redeemed when the debt is doubled: ADiH praRaSyeddviguRe Gane yadi na mokzyate, Y. ; m. of real property: sTAvara ADiH, N.s.;(2) banDaH, -kaH (= 1), the same field given on m. to two (persons): kzetramekaM dvayorbanDe dattam, Vri.;(3) ADAnam (= m.ing), Kat.

MORTGAGE (v. t.): (1) A-daDAti (DA, c. 3.), who first m.s and then sells it: yaH pUrvataramADAya vikrIRIte tu taM punaH, Vas.;(2) ADIkaroti, who m.s the same property to two: ADimekaM dvayoryastu kuryAt, Kat.;(3) banDe dadAti (dA, c. 3.), Vri.
MORTGAGE , s. ADiH m., sTAvarADiH m. kzetrADiH, sTAvaraDanADiH m., ADAnaM, ADamanaM, kzetranyAsaH, sTAvaraDananyAsaH, BUminyAsaH, upanyAsaH, sTAvaravanDakaH, banDakaH, upaniDiH m., BUminizwopaH.
To MORTGAGE , v. a. ADIkf, kzetrAdi sTAvaraDanaM nyasa (c. 4. -asyati [Page516-a+ 51] asituM) or nikzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM), nyAsaM dA, banDakaM dA, nyAsIkf.
MORTGAGED , p. p. ADIkftaH -tA -taM, nyAsIkftaH -tA -taM, nyastaH -stA -staM, upanyastaH &c.; ‘to be mortgaged,’ ADeyaH -yA -yaM.
MORTGAGEE: (1) banDagrahItf (f. trI);(2) ADi- grAhaka (f. hikA).
MORTGAGEE , s. ADiDArI m. (n), nyAsaDArI m. (n), ADigrAhI m. (n), banDakagrAhI m., banDakaDArI m., ADigrAhakaH.
MORTGAGER: (1) ADAtf (f. trI);(2) ADi- kartf (f. rtrI);(3) banDadAtf (f. trI).
MORTGAGER , s. ADidAtA m. (tf), banDakadAtA m., ADIkattA m. (rttf).
Mortiferous, a. maraRAvaha; See Mortal.
MORTIFEROUS , a. mftyujanakaH -kA -kaM, maraRAvahaH -hA -haM, prARaGAtakaH &c.

MORTIFICATION: I Gangrene: perh. nASaH. II Subjection, opposition: indriyajayaH, -damaH, and sim. comp.s.III Humiliation:(1) aBimavaH; mAnamaNgaH and sim. comp.s., aBimAna- vyasanam, Ki.IV Vexation, disappointment: q. v.: expr. with duHKam.

MORTIFICATION , s. (In surgery, local extinction of life) mAMsanASaH, mAMsAtipAkaH, mAMsapAkaH, cetanAnASaH, jIvitvanASaH, mAMsakoTaH, mAMsa- vidraDiH m., mAMsapUtiH f. — (Subjugation of the passions and appetites) damaH, dAntiH f., damanaM, saMyamaH -manaM, indriyadamaH, indriyajayaH, indriyaparAjayaH, indriyasaMyamaH, jitendriyatvaM, idriyavaSIkaraRaM, kAmAvasAyaH, vItakAmatvaM, vizayaparANmuKatA. — (By penance, &c.) tapas, tapaScaryyA, tapasyA, kfcCraM, kAyakleSaH, vErAgyaM. — (Humiliation, vexation) aBiBavaH, aBiBUtiH f., mAnaBaNgaH, mAnaKaRqanaM, aBimAnaKaRqanaM, mAna- hAniH f., tejoBaNgaH, darpaBaNgaH, apakarzaH -rzaRaM, vyaTA, duHKaM, kleSaH, viqa- mbanA. — (Disappointment) ASABaNgaH, manoBaNgaH, ASAnASaH, icCAnASaH, icCAvinASaH, icCAkzayaH, utsAhaBaNgaH.

MORTIFIED , p. p. (In surgery) nazwamAMsaH -sA -saM, nazwacetanaH -nA -naM, koTavAn -vatI -vat (t), atipakvaH -kvA -kvaM. — (Subdued) dAntaH -ntA -ntaM, damitaH -tA -taM, sayamitaH -tA -taM, vaSIkftaH -tA -taM, jitaH -tA -taM; ‘one whose passions are mortified,’ jitendriyaH, yatendriyaH, saMyatendriyaH, vItakAmaH, vItarAgaH, vItaspfhaH, viraktaH, vErAgI m. (n), jitakAmaH, jitakAmakroDAdiH m. — (Humiliated, vexed) aBiBUtaH -tA -taM, parABUtaH -tA -taM, KaRqitaH -tA -taM, BagnamAnaH -nA -naM, klizwaH -zwA -zwaM, savyaTaH -TA -TaM, udvignaH -gnA -gnaM, viqambitaH -tA -taM.

Mortify, v. t. aBiBU 1 P, avaman c., apa-kfz 1 P, mAnaM-garvaM-BaMj 7 P, KaMq 10; See Humble. 2 nigrah 9 P, saM-ni-yam 1 P, dam c. (damayati), vaSIkf 8 U, Avf 5 U, ji 1 P. 3 kliS 9 P, saM-pari-tap c., Ayas c.; See Afflict. 4 cEtanyaM naS c. or hf c. v. i. naS 4 P, cEtanyaM naS c. 2 tap 4 A, tapastap or car 1 P, tapasyati (D.). [Mortifi]ed, a. aBiBUta, KaMqita, Atta-hfta-Bagna-garva, KaMqitamAna, Bagna-darpa-mAna. 2 dAMta, vaSIkfta jita; ‘whose passions are m(ortified)’ jiteMdriyaH, vaSin m., dAMtaH, vItakAmaH, vItarAgaH, niHspfhaH. 3 klizwa, savyaTa, pIqita. 4 nazwa-cEtanya-mAMsa, koTIBUta. [Mortif]ication, s. aBiBavaH, avamAnaH, apakarzaH, mAna or darpa-BaMgaH or KaMqanaM, mAnahAni f. 2 damaH, nigrahaH, saMyamaH-manaM, jayaH, iMdriyadamaH-jayaH; kAmavirakti f., vi-zayavimuKatA, vErAgyaM. 3 tapaScaryA, tapasyA, kfcCraM. 4 duHKaM, kleSaH, AyAsaH, vyaTA. 5 ASABaMgaH-nASaH, manoBaMgaH. 6 mAMsapAkaH, mAMsakoTaH, cEtanyanASaH. [Mortify]ing, a. mAnaDvaM-sin, darpahArin, vyaTAvaha; kleSakara, (rI f.), saMtApaka.
MORTIFY (v. i.): perh. naSyati (naS, c. 4.) or mriyate (mf, c. 4).

MORTIFY (v. t.): I To destroy: mArayati (c. of mf), “of m. ed” iron: mAritasya lOhasya, Bha.II Of passions: jayati (ji, c. 1.) one who has m.ed his lusts: jitendiyaH (yA, yaM).: v. Also to control.III To vex, pain: q. v.: duHKAkaroti.

To MORTIFY , v. a. (Destroy the vitality of) jIvitvaM or cEtanyaM naS (c. 10. nASayati -yituM), cetanAnASaM kf, cEtanyanASaM kf. — (Subdue) dam (c. 10. damayati -yituM), vaSIkf, ji (c. 1. jayati, jetuM), parAji; ‘one's passions,’ indriyARi dam, indriyadamanaM kf; ‘the body,’ SarIrakleSaM kf. — (Humble) aBiBU, apakfz (c. 1. -karzati -krazwuM), mAnaM BaYj (c. 7. Banakti, BaMktuM) or KaRq (c. 10. KaRqayati -yituM), aBimA- naKaRqanaM kf, mAnaviDvaMsaM kf. — (Vex) kliS (c. 9. kliSnAti, kleSituM), vyaT (c. 10. vyaTayati -yituM), tap (c. 10. tApayati -yituM).

To MORTIFY , v. n. (Lose vitality, as flesh) nazwacEtanyaH -nyA -nyaM BU, nazwajIvitvaH -tvA -tvaMBU, nazwamAMsaH -sA -saMBU, mAMsEkadeSe pUtIBU, koTIBU. — (Practise austerities) tap (c. 4. tappate), tapas tap, tapas (nom. tapasyati), tapaScaryyAM kf, vErAgyAcaraRaM kf, SarIrakleSaM kf, brahmacaryyaM kf.
MORTIFYING (adj.): santApaka (f. pikA) (?): v. Also painful.
MORTIFYING , a. mAnaBaYjakaH -kA -kaM, darpaBaYjakaH &c., vyaTAkaraH -rA -raM.
Mortise, s. kAzWasaMDiH, dArusIvanaM, dAru-kAzWa cCidraM. v. t. kAzWadvayaM saM-DA 3 U.
MORTISE (subs.): Cidram (used in Bengali ranDram) (?).
MORTISE (v.): I To make a m.: CidraM karoti. II To join: lagayati (c. of lag) (?).
MORTISE , s. kAzWaCidraM, kAzWamanDiH m., kAzWagrahaRI, kAzWaDaraRI, dAruCidraM, dArusIvanaM, kAzWasIvanaM, kAzWaranDraM.
To MORTISE , v. a. anyakAzWaDaraRArTam ekakAzWAgraM Cid (c. 7. Cinatti, CettuM), kAzWadvayasanDAnaM kf, kAzWadvayaM sanDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM).
Mortmain, s. anyAdeyaBogaH.
MORTMAIN: *samavAyaBuktiH; asKalitaBuktiH.
MORTMAIN , s. anyAdeyaBogaH, parAdeyaBogaH, adeyaBogaH.
Mortuary, s. SmaSAnaM, paretaBUmi f.- vAsaH.
MORUNGA , s. (Plant) SoBAYjanaH, SoBanakaH, SOBAYjanaH, soBAYjanaH, SigruH m., tIkzRaganDaH -nDakaH, akzIvaH, AkzIvaH, kAkzIvaH, mocakaH; ‘its root,’ SigrumUlaM; ‘seed,’ SigrujaM, SigruvIjaM.
Mosaic, a. nAnAvarRa(viDa)prastaraKacita, ‘m(osaic) work’, s. citrakarman n.
MOSAIC: I Relating to Moses: *mOzaH (zI, zaM). II Variegated: vicitraH (trA, traM) (?).
MOSAIC , a. nAnAvarRaprastaraKacitaH -tA -taM, nAnAviDaprastaraCuritaH -tA -taM, nAnAvarRadravyapraRihitaH &c.; ‘mosaic work,’ citrakarmma n. (n).
Mosque, s. yAvanaDarmamaMdiraM, yavanIyaM devatAyatanaM.
MOSQUE: (mahammadIya- or -yAnAM) sidDAyatanam: v. Temple.
MOSQUE , s. yAvanaDarmmamaRqapaH, yAvanaDarmmamandiraM, yAvanaprAsAdaH.
Mosquito, s. maSaH, maSakaH.
MOSQUITO: maSaH, -kaH, H. , m.-curtain: maSaharI, Wilson.
Moss, s. SEva(vA)laH, Seva(vA)laH-laM, jalanIlI-likA, ‘m(oss)-grown’ rUQaSEvala, SEvalAvfta. [Moss]y, a. SEvalavat, SEvalin.
MOSS: SEvAlaH (or SEvalaH or SevalaH), m. -grown: jAtaSEvAlaH (lA, laM).
MOSS , s. SilAvalkA, SEvalaH, SEvAlaH, SevalaH, SevAlaH, SepAlaH, SEvaM, [Page516-b+ 51] kAvAraM, sUkarI, SUkarI, SUkarAkrAntA, varAhakrAntA.
MOSS-GROWN , a. SEvalAvftaH -tA -taM, SEvalAcCAditaH -tA -taM, rUQaSEvalaH &c.
MOSS-TROOPER: dasyuH: v. Robber, bandit.
MOSSY: (1) SEvalin (f. nI);(2) SEvalavat (f. tI), R. xvi. 46.
MOSSY , a. SEvAlamayaH -yI -yaM, saSEvAlaH -lA -laM, SEvAlayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, SEvAlitaH -tA -taM, SevAlaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, SEvalI -linI -li (n).

Most, a. BUyizWa, aDikatama, bahu (pl.); prAyeRa sarva; ‘m(ost) people think so’ prAyeRa sarve (bahavaH) evaM manyaMte. 2 niratiSaya, atyaDika, parama, uttama; ‘for the m(ost) part’ BUyizWaM, prAyaH, prAyeRa, bahuSaH. s. BUyizWa parama BAgaH, bahutama-aDikaBAgaH, prAyaH, sarvaBAgaH; bahutaraBAgaH; ‘m(ost) of the spot is green’ prAyaSaH sA sTalI haridvarRA; ‘to the m(ost) of oneʼs power’ yAvacCaktitaH, yAvacCakyaM. adv. BUyizWaM, paramaM, atyaMtaM, atIva, su-ati-atyaMta in comp.; gen. ex. by superlative of adj. 2 aDikaM, sarvADikaM (with verbs). [Most]ly, adv. prAyaH, prAyeRa, prAyaSaH, BUyasA, bahuSaH, bahuDA, sAmAnyataH, sADAraRataH; gen. ex. by BUyizWa affixed to adj.; ‘an assembly m(ostly) composed of learned men’ aBirUpaBUyizWA parizad (S. 1).

MOST (adj.): I In number: prAyeRa sarve (f. rvA, n. rvARi): v. All, many.II Greatest: niratiSayaH (yA, yaM). Ph.: at the m. antataH; to the m. of one's ability: yAvacCaktitaH; for the m. part: prAyeRa.

MOST (adv.): I As a sign of the super- -lative: expr. with: -tamaH (mA, maM) or with: ati-, m. wealthy: AQyatamaH (mA, maM).II In the greatest degree: expr. by circumlo., confides on him m.: sarvApekzayA tasminnaDikaM viSvasiti or tamaDikaM SradDaDAti.

MOST , a. BUyizWaH -zWA -zWaM, aDikatamaH -mA -maM, aDikataraH -rA -raM, aDikaH -kA -kaM, aDikasaMKyakaH -kA -kaM, paramaH -mA -maM, uttamaH -mA -maM; ‘the most part,’ BUyAn -yasI -yaH (s), BUyizWaH &c., bahutaraH -rA -raM, bahutamaH -mA -maM; ‘for the most part,’ BUyizWaM, prAyas, prAyaSas, bAhulyena, bahuSas.

MOST , adv. BUyizWaM, aDikaM, aDikataraM, aDikatamaM, BUyas, paramaM; often expressed by the superlative affixes tama and izWa, as, ‘most excellent,’ SrezWatamaH -mA -maM, SrezWaH -zWA -zWaM; ‘most heavy,’ gurutamaH -mA -maM, garizWaH &c., or by. ati or su or atyanta or atiSaya pre- fixed; as, ‘most powerful,’ atibalavAn &c.
MOST , s. aDikaBAgaH, BUyizWaBAgaH, paraBAgaH, paramaBAgaH, bahutaraBAgaH, bahutamaBAgaH, aDikapakzaH, uttamaBAgaH, uttamapakzaH, aDikAMSaH.
MOSTLY: (1) prAyaSaH;(2) prAyeRa.: v. Also principally.
MOSTLY , adv. BUyizWaM, prAyas, prAyaSas, prAyeRa, bahuSas, bAhulyena, bahuGA, BUyas, sAmAnyatam, bahutaraM, sADAraRyena.
